payload.text:
Highlights

1828-04-12 Journey to Ireland

1828-08-07 First voyage on Hope to London

1828-08-27 Isle of Wight
At church morning & afternoon. Dined quietly with Mrs Scott A cold raw day. Wind SE. Heavy sea on the bar
Another very cold day. Wind NNE. Dined with the whist club invited by H Harry. Spent a pleasant day

A fine morning. Wind WNW Captain Webb & I with the boys went on a boat down to the rocks to fish but had no sport. Whilst there a part of the cliff gave way & falling upon a poor girl who happened to be sitting underneath completely buried. She was soon dug out but dreadfully crushed & quite dead. Her sister was close to her & saw the accident. Returned home & had some dinner at 5 o'clock. Spent the latter part of the evening at H Harry's

A pleasant morning but rather dull. Wind SSW & blowing hard. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. Again in the evening walked with Mark to Tynemouth. Heard this evening of Leddill having resigned! Consequently there is no possibility of a contest for the county

A cloudy morning blowing fresh at SW. Walked up to Tynemouth, met Harry Nicholson & Richardson who had been over the bar with the Harvey bound to Ascksaget. Dined at home. Took wine with Richardson & spent a very pleasant afternoon & in the evening again walked to Tynemouth

A pleasant morning But again blowing hard at WSW It large concussion of people with A professional gentleman with Baudr, flags to went to Chester Whence they met the Bale & brought him through the upper part of town to the George Tavern after which low sat down to an excellent & well arranged discussion nearly 200 freehold all went off well. The latter part of the evening a glorious scene of drunk cuffs and confusion amongst the lower set of freeholders.

A fine morning Wind SW. Walked to Tynemouth Had a little rain. In the afternoon Henry Mark Nicklinson had a little Wiskey todd at Koddams. Walked to Tynemouth again in the evening and finished off at the Duke of York (paid the sushious wives the amount of £16-10)
A beautiful day with puffs of wind at WSW. Went to Church in the morning. Stayed at home in the evening walked to Tynemouth in large afternoon blaze of company thence
A fine morning, wind W by S and WNW. Walked to Tynemouth and shuffled home to denby for M W Kedley cause afraid N South Shields Then took Wenes walk at Nicklinson at the George

A dull morning & blowing fresh ay WSW. Took a walk to Dr Drurgs garden where we played at quoits. An immense number of people went out to Chistow to meet Mr Hodgson where they took the horses out of the carriage & drew him into town in procession to the George tavern where he addressed the people in a short speech. I afterwards dined with him. We sat down about 85 to dinner & spent a very pleasant evening. Mr Ildeston slept at our house

Wind NNW & NW. A most beautiful Day. Breakfasted at the George with Rec Hodgson who afterwards with his friends set off for Blyth where they were to decide with the Premium. At ½ past 1 o'clock, Harry, Drury & I took a boat & rowed up to Sadless to dinner. I Dale also there. We spent a very pleasant day it being his birthday. Took a glass of wine & water with Dale on our return. Received a letter from Fanny Soneth informing us of Emma being rather unwell & requesting if I would allow to stay with them a little longer, which I agreed to.
A very fine morning. Wind NW. Afterwards changed to SW. Walked to Tynemouth. Returned home to dinner. In the afternoon at the Pig & Whistle with A Harry & in the evening again walked to Tynemouth
Good Friday. A cold morning. Wind N by E with snow showers. Attended Divine service. Dined at home.
A cloudy morning, The qlaps fallen a little, wind NNW. Walked to Tynemouth & came home To dinner. In the afternoon A Harry & I walked round by the Doctor's garden. In the evening a little rain
A fine morning. Wind NW. Dined at home. In the afternoon walked round by the Doctor's garden & the Bullring. In the evening at Tynemouth

A most beautiful sunny morning. Wind SW. Walked to Tynemouth. Could not go to church, having taken taken Cubebs. Our new vicar. Mr Reed preached today for the first time. Dined at home. A Harry and Allen took wine with me & in the evening we walked to Tynemouth. An immense deal of company there
A most delightful morning. Very slight breeze from SW. Afterwards NW. A Harry & I took a cullier & went round ...

... to Tynemouth haven where I bathed. Walked home to dinner. In the afternoon we took I Richardson's coble & went to sea mackerel fishing. Stood as far as Hartley Bay but caught nothing. Ran to the south & brought up off the Herd where we caught several guraets & got home at 10 o'clock after a very pleasant day

Further most beautiful day & but for a SE breeze would have been insufferably hot. Bathed again this morning. The water in fine order. Walked to Tynemouth. Got home to dinner. Took Wine at the George. Tea at A Harry's & in the evening again walked to Tynemouth. A great many people in the castle yard
A continuance of most beautiful weather. Wind SE. Bathed again this morning. Walked part of the way to Tynemouth. Dined at home. Received a letter from & wrote to ABS
A delightful morning. Wind SE. bathed again. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. In the afternoon went to sea in the coble & got home at ½ past 9 o'clock. Caught only one mackerel.
A dull morning, rather thick, wind East. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. Cleaned up and turned out excessively hot. A little rain in the evening which brought the wind round to NW. Some lightning
A beautiful morning blowing fresh from WNW. Dined with I Tealey. The new vicar Mr Reed dined with us. Got £5 of Chapmans

A cold day wind N by E. Went to Newcastle. Much disappointed in finding the Hope would not be laden in less than a fortnight or three weeks. Dined with Mr Rt Airey & returned home in the evening by steam

A dull morning with rain. Wind from SSW to WSW. Attended morning service. Dined at home. Sadler took his dinner with me. At Tynemouth in the evening & spent an hour in the billiards room. A revolution in France

A fine morning wind SW. Very Squally with a heavy shower about 2 o'clock. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. Took wine with Allen & afterwards went to the Doctor's Garden. In the evening at Tynemouth again.
A fine morning blowing hard at WNW. Walked to Tynemouth with Webb. Dined at home. At Tynemouth again in the evening. Took coffee at I Finleys

A fine morning. Wind variable during the day W & SSE with rain in the afternoon. After hard fighting between the Parisians & the military where about 8 or 10000 were killed, the former drove the military out of the city & established pro: term: a provisional government & appointing the Duke of Orleans retired general of the kingdom which he accepted. Charles the X & his minions flown. The Lord Khoas where the French with much credit to themselves have effected the revolution without those outrages which characterized the former. Dined with Doctor Drourg. He & Richardson afterwards came & took wine with me.

A pleasant morning wind NW. Walked to Tynemouth with Allen & balled wine at houses. Remained in the town all the afternoon expecting Williams's arrival in the steam boat from London. Walked to Tynemouth in the evening. The boat arrived off the bar at ½ past 9 o'clock but being thick could not see her. The Shields Pafseeyer landed in the Haven & WBS got home about 11 o'clock. Received the rents & paid £70 cats chapmans on account of the Exors

A dull morning having been rain during the night. Wind N by E & the sea having risen put a stop to our fishery excursion. Dined at home. Hewes & Robert Harry came in & took wine with us. In the evening walked to Tynemouth. Suppered with H Harry
A fine morning. Wind NNW. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. Walked to Tynemouth again in the evening

A most beautiful day. Wind ENE. Attended service. Mr King preached. Walked to Tynemouth in the afternoon. An immense number of people there. Dined at I Finleys. At Tynemouth again in the evening. But it unfortunately rained a little & frightened the people away.

Another fine morning. Wind NE. Walked with WBS & Robert over Picston farm & returned home to dinner. Mary & Jane Carf dined with us & left for Newcastle in the afternoon. Walked to Tynemouth in the evening

Easter Another cold day with snow showers. Wind in the morning N by E & changed in the evening to S by E. At church in the morning. Walked to Tynemouth & called upon the Aldertones. Dined at home. The steam boat bought by S Cunningham & others arrived, intended to ply between Newcastle & Leith

A fine morning with a fresh breeze at E by S. I went to Newcastle in the steam boat. I dined at the rooms at a deueser geocor. Mr Hodgson then returned home. I stayed all night at Mr Aireys in Eldon Square. A wet day

WBS came up and meet me in Newcastle just as I was about to start for Shields. We with I Nicholson dined together at the George & returned to Shields in the evening by steamer. Turned out a very wet evening

A dull morning & blowing fresh from the SSW. Got up early and went to Newcastle by steam. Attended the courts. Dined with Mr Airy & in the evening attended the afsize bath which was a very good one, about 430 people them. Got home to Mr Airy at about 2 o'clock where I slept
A pleasant morning wind NW. A few showers during the morning. Attended the courts & walked about Newcastle the Tom Smith & until 2 o'clock when I got on board a steamer & returned home to dinner

A fine day. Went to Newcastle by steam. Met Tom Smith & Dixon & made arrangements for the payment of Mrs Scott's funeral expenses & our settlement with them as executors. WBS & I walked out to Benton with Dixon where we met Mr & Mrs Brown who had arrived from London in the afternoon. We dined & walked down to Shields in the evening

A fine morning, but during the day heavy showers. Wind very variable, from all quarters of the compass. Having taken a seid letz could not go to church. Wallked with A Harry to Tynemouth. At church in the afternoon. Dined at 5 o'clock. Walked to Tynemouth in the evening. Turned out very wet. Finished at A Harry's

A cloudy morning & appearance of rain. Wind NW. Received a letter from Stephenson dated Archangel 29th June & 3rd July. All well. Turned out a very fine day. A Harry & I walked to Tynemouth. J Tinley, C Meleur,AI & K Harry dined with us at 5 o'clock. Finished the evening & stayed all night at the Mulstrum
A Beautiful day. Wind NNE. Payed an averages Hope Club £10.2.1 Walked with J Tinley & WBS to C Milncras to dinner. Returned home in the evening

A cloudy morning. Wind NNE. Paid £16.10.3 from the money for Hope. At 12 o'clock started from the church with a large party. Picnic for Seaton Dilaual where ww dined in the garden, afterwards danced on the lawn having the band of the 82nd Regiment & spent a more delightful day. Drank tea at Holywell & got home before 9 o'clock

A beautiful day. Wind changeable. From the east. Went to Tynemouth races. A great concourse of people. Poor sport. Dined afterwards with small party at Spurriers J Tenley in the chair, R Peart, H Harry, H Nicholson, J Kieenlyside & self
A dull cloudy morning. A fresh breeze at NNE & sea upon the bar. A great many ships from Archangel & America passed yesterday. Dined at home. At the Duke in the evening.
A dull morning & blowing hard from the N with a heavy sea upon the bar. Dined at home at 5 o'clock. Expected C Milman to go to the concert, but he did not come. At the Duke in the evening.
Another dull morning. Wind NNE. WBS went to Newcastle. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home at 5 o'clock.

A beautiful day. Wind NE. Went to church in the morning. Mr Mark preached. Received a letter from Stephenson dated Archangel the 15th July of his boxing load & that he had brought 57 barrels of tar on ship account, but the merchant refusing to give him deck freight. The amount of the bill drawn £120.1.1. Wrote to J Chapman to sell the tar.

Walked to Tynemouth. A great many people there. Dined with J Huntly at 5 o'clock & walked again to Tynemouth in the evening when it unfortunately began to rain & dispersed the people.

A dull morning, having been a good deal of rain during the night. Wind west & NW. William & I walked to Preston to see Moor. A beautiful day. Emma Galbraith returned. Dined at home. In the evening walked to Tynemouth & had a glass of whisky toddy with H Harry at Bell Wails.
A fine morning after a good deal of rain during the night. Wind NW. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at the George with Mr Weatherby & Mr Barker, being licencing day. A very pleasant party.

A dull morning. Wind NW. Dined at home. An idle day. A good many light ships got down. Received a letter from Stephenson of his arrival in London , the ship having sprung a leak in a gale in the White sea. Made a great deal of water on her passage

A cloudy morning. Been rain in the night. Wind N to NE & WNW. Turned out a very fine day. Received a letter from J Chapman. William and I went out with our guns & walked to Marsden Rock by the sands. Got to the top of the rock, a man having made steps up. Got a lunch there & on our way home took a few glasses of punch with the sea breeze & Phasine Society who has this tent pitched on the cliffs.
A fine morning. A little wind at SE with showers. Mr Mark, William & I went in a chaise to Whitby Park & dined with Mr J Wright. Turned out very wet night
A fair day, but very cold & blowing strong from SSE & the dust very unpleasant. Took an early dinner & attended the races, better sport but not many people. Took tea at Tibbs

A wet morning having been a deluge of rain in the night & blowing hard from NE. Wind changed to NW & nearly calm. After breakfast turned out a very fair day. Emma came from school. WBS went to Newcastle to see D Dixon. Moor & his brother called, after a great deal of conversation, agreed to let him continue on the farm should he exert himself to pay off the arrears. His brother promised his abstinence & to continue his security. Emma & I walked round by the wells to Tynemouth. Dined at home at 5 o'clock. At the Duke in the evening.
A fine morning. Wind NW. Went to church. The vicar preached. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home at 5 o'clock. Walked to Tynemouth again in the evening
A fine morning. Wind NW. Showers during the day. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home.

A fine morning. Wind NW. William & I took our guns & walked with Mrs Tealey & his wife. Robersons to Marsden where the committee for the preservation for ship wrecks met & tried several experiments. We afterwards returned by steam to Shields. H Harry dined with us at the Mulstrum at night
A fine morning. Wind NW. Dined at home. William & I walked to Preston in the afternoon. At home in the evening

Been a great deal of rain in the night & still continuous heavy wind SW. Borrowed £300 of Chapman's upon WBS & I are named executors to pay bills & for Mrs Scott's executors, funeral etc. Dined at home. In the evening there was a total eclipse of the moon

A very boisterous day with rain & blowing hard from N by W to N & NNE which brought on a heavy sea. HMS Cordelia came in. William & I took the coach to Benton Lane & walked up to Dixons, but they were at Belford. Walked home to dinner. In the evening at a Quadrille party at J Tenby.

A fine morning & calmer weather. Wind NE. Engaged with WBS preparing for his departure. Emma Galbraith with us. Dined at home. WBS embarked at 5 o'clock on board the Ahoy of Edinburgh Steamer for London. Wind changed to SSE. At the Duke & Druries in the evening.
A dull morning. Wind WNW. Walked to Tynemouth. Attended morning service with the military. Dined at home. Drury & Sadler dined with me. H Harry came in afterwards. At the Mulstrum in the evening.
A dull morning. Wind east. Turned out a very fine day. H French & I walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. At the Albion in the afternoon. Drank tea with H Harry & again at the Albion in the evening.
A cold day. Wind SE with showers of rain. Dined at home
A rainy morning, blowing hard from the NE with a sea upon the bar. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home.

A beautiful day. Wind ENE. Went by coach to Newcastle to meet Dixon, but did not settle with him. Took the steam boat & landed at Walker. Saw Mrs Carr & child. Dined with them & returned to Shields by steam. In the evening at the Mulstrum.

A wet morning. Wind SSW. A great many ships got to sea. Dreadful weather for the farmers, being heavy all day. Harry Cunningham & I after dinner went to the George & enjoyed ourselves over a jug or two of punch & oysters. Called in at the Mulstrum.

A dull morning with the appearance of more rain. Wind N by W. Several ships got to sea. Walked to Tynemouth, caught in the rain. Dined at home. At Roddany in the afternoon & the Duke & Mulstrum in the evening.
A fine morning. Wind WNW. HMS Cordelia sailed. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home

A dull rainy morning. Very heavy rain during the night & blowing hard from the SSE. At church in the morning. Dined at home. H Harry & I walked to Tynemouth in the afternoon. Saw the Hope off Sonter. She soon got into the harbour. Went on board & saw Stephenson. At the Duke & Malstrum in the evening

A dull morning. Wind N by E. Got up early & went by steam to Newcastle. Fixed the Hope with Hindhaegh at 10/3 freight. Got home to dinner. Took wine at the George with French & Harry. Drank tea at H Harry's & in the evening at the Duke.

A fine morning. Been rain in the night & has the appearance of more wind SW. Went up to the ship. Walked to Tynemouth. Ordered a new square mainsail. Got the canvas of Bradshaw & to be made by Mrs Brown Polly of Wallsend. J Carr, H Harry & French dined with me. Spent a very pleasant day. At the Mulstrum in the evening

A beautiful morning. Wind SW. Walked up to the Hope alongside grane getting ballast out. Got her down up the shore at Metcalf dock to sink her to find out the peak. Walked to Tynemouth, saw Potts, who returned with me to Shields. He, Harry, French & I went to the Albion & Mulstrum

A fine morning. A fresh breeze from the West. The Hope upon the shore having been sank did not find any bad places of consequence. The buts ends bolts been in a great many places corroded & heavily worn was the principal cause of her making so much water. Employed getting new bolts put in & the buts ends caulked. Dined at Home. Spent the afternoon at Dr Drury's garden playing at quoits & the evening at the Mulstrum

An exceedingly fine day & mild wind W by S. Dined at the George Tavern. The dinner given by a party of married men consisting of J Dale president: Mr Clark vise: A Dale, J Tindley, W C Wright. R Peach, A Metcalf Bachelors: I Craig, Mr Horner, E Drurg, J Keilyside, A Harry

A beautiful morning Wind WSW. Went down to the Hope. The starboard side as bad as the other. A number of the bolts bad. Walked to Tynemouth. Saw Potts hounds run a trail. Dined on board the Hope. I Dale, Harry French & I took wine at the George & spent a pleasant afternoon at the Mulstrum in the evening

Another beautiful morning. Wind NW. Onboard the Hope. Got two keels of wqlaure down. Pain G Slop £3.11.3 wages up to today. Dined at home. H Henry & I on board the Hope to taste some brandy. In the evening at the Albion

A dull morning with a little rain. Wind SW, increased in the afternoon to a gale. Attended morning service. The vicar did duty & preached. Dined at home. Took wine with H Harry & tea in the evening at the Mulstrum

It has blown a gale of wind all night at SW & continuing. The Suffolk Hull steamer was driven upon the rock in coming in last night. Walked to the rock to see the Suffolk. No chance of getting her off. Afterwards walked up to Sadlers at the Point to dinner & spent a pleasant day at the Malstrum in the evening. Got our buf for the ship this morning
A rainy morning but calmer weather. Wind SW. J Drury & Allen dined with me on board the Hope. Got five keels down
A very fine morning. Wind NW. On board the Hope. 8 more keels came down. Dines at home. At the Duke in the evening

A rainy morning & blowing hard at SE. On board the Hope, got the remainder of her coals Dined at home. H Harry had pusieto on board the Hope. In the afternoon. Got the new mainsail on board & bent, fits very well. Stove out this evening to go to sea, but having a foul anchor was prevented. A pity being a fierce NW wind. At the Duke.

A fine morning with a fresh breeze at WSW. The Hope got to sea about ½ past 6 o'clock. At 7 o'clock turned out & walked to Tynemouth. Got £5 from Chapmans. Paid Pelors £1.15. & E Reed ¼ wages £1.8.6. Walked to Tynemouth to the sale of the Suffolk's stores. Dined at home. In the afternoon A Harry & I walked to the new Quay & afterwards called at the Pig & Whistle. Spent the evening at William Harrisons
A fine morning blowing fresh at NW. Emma Galbraith came down & spent the day with us. Finished the evening at H Harrys

A beautiful morning early, but about 9 o'clock a little rain. Wind WNW. Attended morning service & Mr Ficinifs from Pontaland preached. & gave us a very good sermon. Sadler dined with me & H Harry came in & took wine. In the evening with Mary Mactpreeson
A beautiful mild day. Wind WSW. Master R Jldesters and I dined on board the Hope & spent the afternoon
A dull morning & very like more rain. Wind SSW. Dined at home. After dinner walked with H Harry up to Tynemouth and took punch with J Cunningham. Suppered off oysters at the Marstrum
A dull foggy morning & every appearance of rain. Wind west. Attended a court at the George & lunched with Mr Hodgson. Dined at 4 o'clock with Inspector Dale & spent a very pleasant day

A beautiful morning. Wind NW. Took a long walk round by the heigh end of the town. Preston & by the fields to Tynemouth. Found Mrs Dixon waiting for me on my return. Dined & spent a pleasant day at H Dales. At the Marlstrum

A beautiful morning. Wind west. Walked to Tynemouth & had a warm bath. Dined at home. On board the Brodewick in the afternoon In the evening went to a concert at the theatre at which Miss Hughes sang a march, beautiful voice & fine execution. Suppered with Mr Tinley

A foggy damp morning Very little wind at W by S Received a letter from Stephenson on informing me of his safe arrival at Woolwich on Wednesday with a large fleet many of which have been at sea a fortnight. It lost anchors & cables. Dined at home. On board the Brodarick. Attended the first meeting of the whist club
A most beautiful morning. Wind at SE. Received a letter from B B Galbralth. Dined at home. Spent the evening at Dr Wiltons
A damp morning. Wind SW. A great many light ships off the bar. Went to church. Dined at home. Took wine with Mr Allen. Walked to Tynemouth. In the evening. Saw Ann. H Harry spent the evening with me.

A beautiful morning Wind NW. Sent & brought Emma Galbraith home. Mrs Man having died last night. Dined at home. Walked to Tynemouth & saw the 80th inspected by General Bouverie Spent the evening with H Harry. Wrote to WBS

A most beautiful autumnal morning & wind NW. Walked with H Harry round by the rocks. Tynemouth Cullercoats Sands & fields, home. Dined at home & spent the afternoon at Dr Drewy's garden. In the evening at the Mulstrum

A fine morning Wind NNW. Mrs Dixon came down before I was dressed & took Emma Galbraith to Newcastle with her. Dined at home. Allen fed with me. & we afterwards spend the afternoon on board the Broderick. At the Mulstrum in the evening

A fine morning. Wind WSW. Received a most distressing letter from Mr Vernon Rector of Carlow of the poor Bafer being very ill of a typhous fever. I therefore have determined to set off for carlow in the morning from South Shields at 5 o'clock by Pelot Leeds coach
Beautiful weather Wind NW. In the house all the morning having taken medicine. Dined at home. At Allens in the afternoon & in the evening at the whist club
A dull morning. Wind NW Dined at home. Spent the afternoon on board the Telemachus & the evening on the Mr Bradshaws
An exceedingly fine morning. Wind WNW. Walked to the new quay & round by Preston Lane. Dined at 3 o'clock with H Harry Miss R Fenwick, Metcalf & Drury there. Spent a pleasant day. Got £5 of Chapman

A dull foggy morning Wind WNW but little of it. Received a letter from WBS. The Hope was out on Friday & going to the chalk wharfs. Went to church. The vicar's brother preached. Gave a most excellent sermon for the benefit of the inadequate society. He a beautiful preacher

A beautiful morning Wind little at SE. Got up early & walked round by Tynemouth & Cullercoats, called upon Mr Hewetson & returned to breakfast. Received a letter from WBS with the Hopes coal freight account enclosing Metcalfrs & Drury's note for £79.18.2 Which I paid into chapmans. Took another long walk with H Harry & Peart round by the head of the town, Burdon Main, height Charton, Belly Hill & Preston & got home to dinner. Spent the latter part of the evening at Alderneys.

A dull morning rather thick. Weather having been rain in the night. Wind but little at east Walked to Tynemouth & Dined at home. Cunningham & H Harry took wine with me. Suppered with Allen & afterwards at the Mulstrum
A fine calm morning. Wind SE. Started at ½ past 2 o'clock & walked to Wallsend & dined with Potts, a large party there. Spent a very pleasant day. Walked home in the evening. At the Mulstrum
A beautiful morning. Wind SSE. Walked with Allen round by Whitley. Called upon Mr Wright & returned by Callercoat. Dined with H Metcalfe. At the Mulstrum

A fine morning but foggy which is clearing away Wind SW. Walked to Tynemouth Could not see the Hope. Dined at home At Dr Drury's garden in the afternoon & in the evening at the Albion & Mulstrum. Paid Mrs Brown £3.5.6 for making mainsail
Another fine morning again foggy. Wind about West. Walked to Tynemouth. The Hope not in sight. Dined at home. H Harry & Allen suppered with me in the evening
Dined with Mr T Wright of Whitley park. Met a very large party & returned to Shields at 9 o'clock & went to the Theatre. Very cold day. Wind SE. Sea high

A heavy fall of rain last night during the day showers & in the evening it came down in torrents. Wind variable from SS to NW. Not able to leave for Carlow, this morning being Sunday, coach doesn't run, but shall start in the morning. Dined at home. At church in the morning.

A continuance of most beautiful weather. Wind SSW. The Hope arrived last night & is laid upon the Lowlight shore. Did not go to church having taken a seidlity. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. Again in the afternoon walked to Tynemouth. Drank tea & spent the evening at H Harry's

A fine morning. Wind SW. Stephenson breakfasted with me & we afterwards went by coach to Newcastle. Freights being so low I fixed the Hope to Load Holywell on my own account. Walked round by Bentow, saw Mrs Dixon & proceeded to Billy Smith & dined with Charlton. A wet evening
Another fine morning. Wind SW. A little rain last night . The Hope got her chalk done Dined at the Mulstrum

A pleasant morning & a fresh breeze at SW Dined at home & afterwards went with H Harry & Elder in a sculler to the Point & ate oysters & spent the evening with Sadler. The Hope got 14 Keels today. A great many ships arrived

The fine weather continues with a fresh breeze at SW. The Hope finishes her loading & took 17 Keels & fine chal. The 3 chat over I took for the hours. Walked up to Benton to dinner. Had the beagles out & killed a hare. Dixon & J Jeutty comfortable P.S. average Hope club £2.19.2

A very thick rainy morning. Continued all day & prevented me getting down to dine with J Tenby, being engaged. Then dined with Mrs Braordlesy & Dixon being their last day as Lords of the manor, spent a pleasant evening

A beautiful morning. Wind WBW. Walked into Newcastle. Called upon Miss Robinson & fixed for Emma Galbraith to go to her school on Tuesday. Went to the quayside, took a steamer & got home to dinner. In the evening at J Tinlay, whist club

A fine morning. Wind WSW. Went to church. Dined at home unto ½ past 1 o'clock. Five companies of the 15th Regiment landed today. at the Lowlights from Jersey. Walked to Tynemouth. Spent the afternoon at Cunningham's. In the evening at the Mulstrum. The Lady Jane arrived with only 3 fish

A dull damp morning A little wind at West. Paid Premium bill Archangel voyage £12.13.8. Dined at home. Engaged in the afternoon entering the archangel voyage in the ships book. In the evening at the Albion & afterwards at the Mulstrum

A very fine morning rather frosty. Wind N by W. Went to Newcastle by steam. Saw Mis Dixon & Emma. The latter was taken to Miss Robertson's. I walked out with Dixon to Benton. Dined & stayed all night. Received a letter from Richmond
Got up this morning at 3 o'clock & left South Shields at ½ past 4 o'clock coach for Carlow. A fine day, arrived at Leeds at 6 o'clock where I stay all night

A cold morning. Wind NW Saw the Northhumberland fox hounds from Benton show off at Gosforth. Dixon & I walked upto Newcastle. Saw Tom Smith, walked to see the horses being fair team. Sold an old silver spoon cracked & gave five shillings in addition for a new one for Emma. Took the steam boat at 2 o'clock. Came home to dinner. Wrote to WBS expecting Miss Gauntley & Mary Carfs. Wrote unto C Richmond that I could not meet him at Dersham on Saturday. Albion
A dull morning after a good deal of rain in the night & blowing fresh from W by N Dined on board the Ruby with Mr Lewry & at the whist club in the evening

A Blowing hard from NW Cloudy with the appearance of rain. Drew on chapman for £14.1.5. for Mrs Brown making square mainsail £3.11 & for Bradshaw for canvas £11.4. Dined at home. At the Albion in the afternoon & finished at the Mulstrum
A fine frosty morning wind light at WNW. Employed entering Hope's 2nd coal voyage in the book. Dined at home. At the Albion in the afternoon & in the evening at the club held at Inspector Dales

Rather dull morning having been rain in the night. Blowing fresh at WNW. Having a bad swelled face, sent for the doctor who prescribed a dose of physic for me. Remained in the house all day. Blowing a gale of wind at NW

A fine morning blowing hard at West. Remained in the house all the morning. Robert went to Preston & saw Mr I Fenwick who agreed to pay an acknowledgment for the drain, the wall encroachment into Arthur's garden & also to take away the railing, thereby admitting the hedge to be the boundary line of which indeed there could be no doubt as to be once wish to make the railings the line which was only permitted to be put up to keep the cattle off the quicks. Dined at home & suppered in the evening with a party at there. A bet lost by Mr Sadler
A delightful morning wind about West. Took a walk with Peach there the town round by the turnpike Preston lane, by the fields to Tynemouth. Dined at home
A fine morning Wind west by South. At South Shields. Dined at home. On board the Choice in the afternoon & finished at the Malstrum Got £5 at chapmans

A most beautiful morning quite summers weather. Wind SW Walked to Tynemouth. Dined with Dr Welton Captain & Mrs Bellew there at the Whist club in the evening

xx

A fine morning Wind SW. Been a little rain in the night. Walked as far as Vrilly Mill & saw Pott's harriers. Returned home to dinner In the afternoon on board the Crises with A Nicholson & Webb. Afterwards at the fair & Malstrum Turned out a very wet evening

Much annoyed at finding I should not get to Liverpool in time to catch the Post Office packit for Dublin. Deceived by the people at the coach office. Left Leeds by coach at ½ past 5 o'clock. Outside a cloudy morning, soon began to rain & continued very heavy all day. Reached Huddersfield at 10 o'clock. I think where I had to wait an hour & change coach. Got to Manchester at 1 o'clock & found to my surprise & vexation the coach would not proceed until 5 o'clock. Kicked up a row at the office, got part of any money returned & fortunately caught a coach about to start for Liverpool where I arrived at 6 o'clock & immediately embarked on board the "Bereuenyham" steam boat which as luck would have it, was that evening going to start for Dublin. Wind WSW
A dull morning Wind S by W. Been a great deal of rain in the night with SE winds. Dined at home Wrote to WBS with accounts Rained the whole day with a gale at SSE & SE. H Harry suppered with me

The early part of the morning fine weather but began to rain again about 11 o'clock & continued showering all day Did not go to church Dined at home. Took wine with H Harry. At the Mulstrum in the evening
A fine morning. Wind west. Sent Robert to Newcastle to see Emma G Walked to Preston. Dined at home On board the Crisis & finished the evening at the Albion & Mulstrum
A dull morning with the appearance of more rain Wind WSW. Dined with Allen. Went to the assembly in the evening, a very poor one. Took supper afterwards & sat up very late

Another dull morning Wind blowing fresh at S by W From the fatigues of last night, did not awake till 12 o'clock Walked to Tynemouth. Caught there by a tremendous gale with heavy rain. Got home at 5 o'clock Tom Smith arrived. Dined and went to the theatre at ½ price
A very fine morning Wind SW. A few light ships off. The Hope's mast by wear. Robert engaged collecting rents Dined at home & in the evening Tom Smith & I attended the whist club

Rather fine day but cold. Wind WNW. The Hope arrived in the night. Went by coach to Newcastle Things very dull & could do nothing deferenced to let her lay for ten days Returned by steam & afterwards rode up to Benton with Tom Smith. Gave Stephenson £25

A very cold morning Wind fresh at S by E. Accompanied Mr & Mrs Dixon & Tom Smith in the coach To Newcastle. Saw Emma Galbraith & took The steam boat to Shields. Dined at home at 5 o'clock & afterwards went to whist club. A heavy gale

Been a great deal of rain in the night. Wind SW. Went to church. Walked to Tynemouth in the afternoon Dined at J Tealays. Captain Deans & two lieutenants of HMS Childers there. Received a parcel from WBS by J H Richardson, deeds for silver spoon

A fine cold morning Wind WSW. Received a letter from WBS with Hope's archangel account but not reliance the delivered very little more than good deals Paid Robert & Leadbetter their ¼ year wages £10.11/- draft on chapmans exor account Dined at home. Called on J Young Paid Mrs Wright for Emma Galbraiths education £13.3.9 at the theatre & Mulstrum in the evening

During the whole of last night we had a heavy sea & foul wind blowing WSW very hard, to contend with but fortunately a fine boat under us. As it was low water when we started, we overtook to steam Office packit at anchor, at the Rock not able to proceed for want of water, having left 2 ½ hours before us so that after all, I lost no time, no thanks to the rascally clerks at the coach office. We kept company all night & after a tedious passage arrived at the custom House quay, Dublin at 3 o'clock PM. Took my luggage to Mackens Hotel, Dawson Street where I stayed all night
Showery weather. Attended this magistrates meeting. Dined at home & went to a party in the evening at J Tenleys a quadrille

A beautiful morning, rather frosty. Wind west Walked up to the ship Took an early dinner on board the Crises. In the evening at the Albion & Duke of York.

Received a letter from Mrs Bagot Wishing Emma Galbraith to be placed under their mothers care

A showery morning Wind NE. Been a great deal of rain in the night. Sea high. Paid Gibson butcher bill ¼ of year £4.9/- also executors of Scott painer £3.8- for the home & £12.19/- property. Walked to Tynemouth & called upon two officers of the 15th regiment Hind & [ ] afterwards. Walked up & dined at the Point with Sadby. Attended the whist club in the evening & the Mulstrum

A fine frosty morning. Wind light at SW. Walked with Cunningham & A Richardson round by the fields to Cullercoats, returning by the jany & Tynemouth home to dinner. In the afternoon at the billiard room & at the Albion in the evening
Blowing hard from S by W with showers. Wrote to answer to Miss Bagot at Dublin about Emma Galbraith. Dined at home At the billiard room in the afternoon & the whist club in the evening at H Harry's
A fine morning. A little frost in the air. Wind SSW Went to church in the morning Dined at home & took wine at the north D Assens in the afternoon. In the evening at the Mulstrum

A beautiful morning. Wind NW. Went by coach to Newcastle & fixed the Hope to load Adams to be load on her before the 8th December. Returned by steam. Dined at Mr Harrison's the brewers & in the evening at the Theatre & Mulstrum
Another delightful day. Wind NW. Walked up to the point. H Harry & I dined with Sadler. Spent a quiet & pleasant day & got down again in good time. In the evening by atcre. Called at the Albion

A continuance of very fine weather. Wind NW. with frost. Walked with A Nicholson to Tynemouth. Called on Dr Drury for some cubebs having got c___d. Dined at home. At the billiard room in the afternoon & in the evening called at the Malstrum to inform Seaton of my disaster

A fine morning with a change of wind from SW On board the Hope, ordered new paul bits. Walked to Tynemouth Dined at home. Mr Herd of the 15th regiment with me at the billiard room & whist club in the evening

Sent Stephenson to Newcastle

Showering morning & blowing hard from SE. Stephenson called, could not prevail on Mr Walker to send us coal down tomorrow to ensure us an earlier turey. Dined at home. Got £5 of chapman Took wine with I A Richardson at the Albion

Wintery weather and blowing strong from SE. On board the Hope people engaged with the wind lafe preparing for new barrel & paul bits. On breaking the old barrel off, found the wind lefs sprung & rotten. Obliged to condemn it. Dined at home. In the billiard room afternoon & at the whist club. In the evening at the Duke.
A continuance of stormy weather. Still blowing a gale at ESE. Did not go to church. Dined at home. H Harry & Nicholson came in & took wine with me. Spent the evening at the Mulstrum

Stormy weather, heavy rain & blowing hard at SE Received a letter from WBS & answered it with an amount of rents. Dined at home. At the billiard room & the Albion in the evening Gave notice of the Hope having 7 Keels on board

The wind still present from ESE but both it & the sea much fallen. Gave gesheding a draft on chapmans for £8.6.8 an average Premium Club. Walked up to Coble dean, carpenters busy with wind cap. Got 7 Keels more down, making 14. Dined at home. At the billiard room in the afternoon & in the evening at the Albion

A continuance of SE wind but weather more moderate. On board the Hope. Finished her loading of Adairs Main pain us bad oneaseere having taken in 17 Keels & still have room for 3 ches more. Dined with Mr Wright on board the Mulgrave Castle & in the evening went to Bill Hill & suppered with Holroid.

Wrote to Mr Walker Adams Main for an allowance
Amore moderate weather. Wind S by W & very damp. On board the Hope. The men still busy with the windlass. Dined at home Attended the whist club in the evening

Still blowing hard from the SE. Received an answer from Mr Coulter with the cago both for my seguaturn & refusing to make any allowance. Retuned it & complaining of the enforshor Cunningham & A Nicholson dined With me on board the Hope. At the theater & Mulstrum in the evening

A foggy damp morning. Wind SSW. Gave Stephenson a draft on chapman for £10 being the balance of his archangel account 3.12.6 Tongues £1.18 & cash for present voyage £4.9.7. Dined with J B Wright at the Star & Garter Tynemouth at 5 o'clock & in the evening attended the whist club at Tibbe
A fine morning rather cold wind SSW. Several ships got to sea. Not very well. Did not go to church. Dined with H Harry & also took tea & in the evening at the Mulstrum & Abbey

A stormy morning. Been a great deal of rain during the night blowing hard from the ESE. Just as well the Hope did not get to sea yesterday. Gave Robert a draft for £5 for the house. Dined at home. At the billiard room in the afternoon and the Albion in the evening

Fine weather but stated blowing hard from E by S & a heavy sea on the bar. Several ships light & loaded came in. One a Scarbra oefsel from the Baltic in taking the bar at an improper time of teder, struck, knocked her rudder off & drove upon the Hurdsand. Dined at Mr R Fenwicks a party
Fair weather but still blowing fresh from ESE with showers of rain. On board the Hope Dined at home. At the billiard room A Nicholson came & took a glass of Toddy with me in the evening
A continuance of much the same sort of weather with the fresh from the E & E by S. Dined at home. At the billiard room in the afternoon & whist club in the evening
Been raining heavily all night & still a very damp morning. Wind changed to N by W. In the house all the morning. Dined at home. At the billiard room in the afternoon. Suppered with H Harry

A beautiful morning. Weather completely changed. A little sunshine at last. Wind W by N & WNN. A large fleet of ships got to sea but too much swell on the bar to allow the Hope to sail, although some nearly her draught of water veateered , but dowt down struck. Dined at home at the whist club at Reverand Richmonds in evening

Although it was a most beautiful night at the home I left Reverand Richmonds & frosty buk soon after 12 o'clock the wind got to NE & increased before daylight to a perfect gale, with heavy showers of sleet & a very high sea on the bar/over

Stayed in the home all morning. Dined at home. Went to the newsroom in the afternoon. Very strong with heavy showers of snow, hail & sleet. Guefal got upon the Herd. Spent the evening at home. Turned out a fine clear night & hard frost.

A fine morning & hard frost with a little snow on the ground. Wind NW. On board the Hope & the Lightning Government Steamer came down here with 150 marines for the garrison at Tynemouth. A beautiful copal of elegantly fit up.

Dined at home & in the evening attended the theatre with Hargraves beautiful & bespeake of the Bachelors of Noshules. Finished off at the Albion. Sleet and rain at night.

A very wet raw unpleasant morning. Wind W by N. The Hope got to sea in the afternoon without touching the bar, there being a great deal of sea on. Some had accounts of the ships that sailed on Saturday many struck very heavily on the bar & some in consequence the crew not being able to Kup them, foundered & all the people drowned. At least we had an account of one & another having run on shore. Dined at the Albion, a bed dance & a very good one, spent a pleasant day. In visiting Bradshaw & H Harry, chain & vince. 12 percent

A very dull thick & raining morning. Wind SW but little of it. Received a letter from WBS answered it informing him of the sailing of the Hope & Dined at home.

At the Albion in the evening, for the benefit of Mr Perrs, the vishrak as the bells started of the gents of the commercial newsroom but not more than three or four there. Called at the Mulstrum

HMS Childers came

Answered WBS's letter informing him also that chapman had agreed to service the note of £300 for four months. They carried £50 to my account remitted by WBS
A dull morning. Wind SW Dined at home. HMS Jacasacy came into harbour to lay as a guard ship. At the billiard room & whist club in the evening

In the night it began to blow very hard from the NNE. & continued pretty near a gale the whole of the day from that to NE with heavy showers of hail & snow & high sea. Another catic put in making two, live government steamers, a Green Boy, 28 gun frigate in the harbour. Attended a public meeting for the purpose of entering this resolution with regard to the Rail road. Dined at home. At the billiard & news rooms & finished at the Duke of York. Got £5 of chapman

it blew very hard last night from the NE with showers of hail & snow, but towards morning relented & at breakfast time wind NW. But at sea still apparently Easta of north. Paid Ed: Keids moshvo £1.13.9 ¼ years wages. Dined at home. Attended the whist club at Craigs in the evening. Frosty

More moderate & rainy weather. Wind W by S. A frost during the night. Did not go to church. Read the service at home. In the afternoon it came on to blow a heavy gale of wind at NW. Many ships got to sea.

HMS Chelders running to go to sea but at blowing hard with a heavy fresh in the river, the ships were quite unmanageable. The first officer on board the cutter & threw to the opposite side of the river & letting go her anchor prevented her going to shore. Some collecse there got foul of her & finally she was prevented going to sea & obliged next tide to move again in her old birth. Dined with J Tenley where the officer was expected but prevented coming.

10 o'clock pm calmer weather again

During the night the wind veered round to the NE. Blowing half a gale and a heavy sea came on. The HMS Childers moored into Peggy's hole again. Cunningham dined with me. At the billiard room in the afternoon. J Agusley got his discharge today from hews & billiard room having given himself up to drunkenness. At the theatre in the evening. The bespeak of the officers of the garrison.

P J Hutchison £2.16.3 averages
A fine morning, rather Cold. Wind W by N. Sea fallen. Walked up to the Point to dine with Sadler. Spent a pleasant day

Fine clear weather but blowing extremely hard at W by N & has been since last evening. The account of the Hope having got to London, she ought to have been there, ship that sailed the day after her having got up. Dined with Warl Wright on board the Merlin. Mrs Stephenson had a letter from her husband at Gravesend. The had very blowing weather. In the evening at the theatre & Mulstrum

A fine frosty morning, blowing hard from NNW. It must have been & no doubt no is at sea, from NNE. Such a human disaster sea, been upon the bar. Heavy showers of snow. Dined at home At the billiard room in the afternoon & in the evening at the whist club

A beautiful winter's morning. Most intense frost & NW wind, sea high. Received a letter from WBS of the arrival & sale of 126 chars of the Hope cargo at Wednesday day mackerel at 34/-. Mr C Wright & Mr L Loyd a dined on board the Lamaracy came & took dinner today. Attended the whist club in the evening at Fenwicks. A most intense frost

Xmas day After a most intense frost during the night, we have a heavy fall of snow. Wind NW. At the newsroom. Paris in a fearful state of excitement. The most fearing the decision of the peers well be in favour of the later. Herewith to WBS giving him an account of the weather here. Walked to Tynemouth & dined with J Cunningham, family party. Spent a very pleasant day

A continuance of frosty weather. A good deal of snow fallen in the night. Wind WNW. Did not go to church. Wrote to B B Galbraith. Received an account these H Harry, A Clark & Berges of the sale of 84 more than Hope coals at 35/-. Dined with J Tealey. The officers of HMS Samarang & Childers there & Goshing RA

A fine winters morning. Frost still continues. Wind wavering variable between SSW & SSE. Received a letter from WBS. HMS Childers sailed out in beautiful style. Dined at home. At Albion & Mulstrum in the evening. Received £1.15. for WBS. Herald hewop open

A dull morning but still frosty, although the wind is from the SE. Dined at home at 5 o'clock H Harry. Lieutenant Gostling, K A. Lieutenant Rudyard 15th regiment Tibbs & Dr Wilton dined with me. Had a very pleasant day & in the evening went to the Ball which was very well attended

A beautiful morning & continuance of frost. Wind SW. Walked round by the ridges, the ice so thickly covered with snow, the skating bad. Dined at home. At the billiard room in the afternoon & the Albion in the evening. At Theatre

A frost this morning but slight. Mark Webb & I set off to walk to Hartley with our guns, but by the time we reached Whetley it began to sleet & rain so heavy that we turned back but got wet before we got home. Dined at home & attended the whist club in the evening. Was engaged to supper at Cheston with Lowrey but being such a stormy night did not go.

A very unpleasant morning. Very thick & damp & from the heavy rain last night, the snow has quite disappeared . Wind SW. Dined at home. Spent the evening at Mr Richmond's & sat the new year in. Called at the Mulstrum

1831-10-10 The Hope spings a leak!
A slight frost during the night wind WSW. Walked up to Beaton. Dined and stayed all night. Mr Allinson and their daughters dined there. Emma Galbraith not very well and looking delicate.
A dull and unpleasant damp morning. Wind SW. Walked down to Shields. Dined with H Harry in the evening. At the Mulstrum.

Most unpleasant weather, damp & uncomfortable. Wind SW. Received a letter yesterday from Stephenson of the ship being out on Thursday delivering 282 char & expecting to get his ballast on Saturday. Received the Hope's afsales with a balance note for £93.7. which I paid into Chapmans & drew for £50 with which I paid the bells for the Archangel voyage viz: swan £___ sharp £___ & spares £___. At the theatre in the evening, Michaels benefit. A good house.
A damp day. Wind ___. Dined at home. The Saturday night whist club with me in the evening. Kept it up till ½ past 2 o'clock in the morning

A continuance of damp weather. Wind E by S. The Hope arrived, having had a quick passage, left on Sunday. Went to Newcastle but did not fix. Got home to dinner a 5 o'clock. Stephenson reports the ship as being very leaky on the London passage, so much so that they could hardly keep up. Desired him to get Sharks to examine her in the morning. At the Albion

Finer weather. Wind ENE & afterwards go to about N by E. Too much sea for the large ships to get out. Got up early & went up to the ship. Sharks on board examining her. Still of opinion she must be leaking in the stern which is certainly very bad & also under her counter. Sent for one of his men & a punt to endeavour to avoid entering into repairs at present. Took the steam boat to Newcastle but could not get more than 11/3 freights or upheld 10/6 & their only at two offices, things very dull, & as no light ships can get down with this wind, I returned home to dinner without fixing. Gave Stephenson a draft for £20 to pay wages. In the account of the whist club, paid subscription etc 22/- up to the end of ...

A fine frosty morning. Wind NNW. Thought of going to Newcastle, but received a message from Shanks that he wished to see me on board the Hope having found the stew in a very bad state. H Harry went with me, the stern certainly in a very damages & rotten state, but Shanks thinks he can cobble it up so as to be safe & enable the ship to go a voyage or two until the days get longer.

Dined with Dale & spent the evening at Mrs Dork Metcalf's where there was a large party. Received a letter from WBS enclosing a note at 4 months for £300 which I gave to R Spence & got the old one cancelled.

A fine morning & slight frost. Wind WNW. Went up to the ship. Shanks just left. Gave orders to do the stern up in the best way they could to enable her to go to sea. Walked round by Chirton. Dined at home. Attended the whist club at Tinley's in the evening.
A mild morning & blowing fresh from the NW. Did not go to church. Walked up & dined with Sadler at the Mulstrum in the evening.

A damp morning, blowing fresh from NNE. Went by steam to Newcastle. Fixed the Hope to load ords Redheught to be upheld 11/- freight go to WBS as factor, & all profit above 11/- to be divided. Returned by coach. Attended the annual meeting of the Eligible and United clubs to alter & receive the rules etc. Sat down a large party to dinner afterwards. At the Mulstrum.

Another damp morning but likely to be finer weather. Wind NW. At the George tavern a great part of the morning. Mr Ilderton there, with whom & a small party, I afterwards dined. Bob Ilderton & I called at the Mulstrum.

Hope got 3 keels down.

Left Dublin outside the Carlow coach at 9 o'clock AM. When I arrived at 4 o'clock in a state of anxiety impossible for me to describe, misery was in store for me & on enquiring of the servant "how my sister was?" to my insufferable horror I learned she was dead. The fever was so malignant nature could not struggle with it & and on Sunday last at 10 o'clock I lost one of the kindest & most affectionate of sisters & the town one of the best & most benevolent of human beings. I was doomed not even one last parting look at her cold remains for such was the rapidity with which decomposition took place that her remains were obliged to be deposited in the select tomb next to her dear husband yesterday. However upon ...

A very unpleasant foggy damp morning. A little wind lope at appears to be W.

Wrote to WBS giving him a copy of Chapmans book on. In the afternoon at the billiard room. Wrote to Tom Smith & sent him some tripe. Harry, Nicholas, Drury & Cunningham came home with me in the evening & played a rubber.

An unpleasant foggy morning. Wind NW. Shanks called & I gave him a draft on Chapmans for £18.18 his bill for new windless repairs to the Hope. Gave Stephenson a draft on Chapmans for £30. Dined at home. Attended the whist club in the evening. 5 keels came down. None yesterday.

A dull foggy morning but rather frosty. Wind West. Got the buf for the ship of Gibson. This voyage 6 ____ @ 42/- went on board with the buf. Gave Geo Stoss £2 on account. Five more keels came down this morning. At the billiard room in the afternoon & at the theatre in the evening. The last time of the company performing this season. Engaged to dine with J Telbs but did not go, rather unwell.

Another foggy morning. Wind about west. On board the Hope, finished her loading, but did not go to sea, the weather having such an unsettled appearance & wind so far from the southward. Dined at home. In the evening attended the whist club at Mr Gortlier R A at Tynemouth Place

A continuance of foggy weather. Wind SW. Did not go to church as Mr Burdan was to sit in our pew to try how he liked it before he would determine upon taking it. Dined at home. Dr Drury & friends came in & took a glass of wine with me. In the evening at the Mulstrum.

Still very unpleasant foggy weather. Wind SSW. Received a letter from WBS. Sent him a copy of Chapmans book for the last quarter, also gave him authority to apply to the Duke for a commission in the Northumbria Militia. Dined at home. Wind freshened at SE & every appearance of bad weather.

A very damp foggy morning. Wind fresh at SE & a good deal of sea. Dined at 5 o'clock with the Gastling RA Tynemouth Place. A very pleasant party. Got home before1 o'clock in the morning. Gave notes to the Premium & Hope clubs of the Hope being loaded. Leadbetter went to Newcastle

A damp & foggy weather. Still continuing with a SE wind. Signed the book for the Hope's cassign of oxd. Redheangh for £153.18.8 date 14th Jan at 60 days on WBS. Leadbetter not having returned from Newcastle. Robert & I dined on board the Hope. At the Albion in the evening. Leadbetter got home in the evening.

A very rainy & foggy day & blowing strong from SE & high sea. Sent the bill for the Hope's cargo by Dunn the coachman to Mr Heindhaigh. Received a letter from Margaret Scott of Crathorn, I having forgot to send her 20/- her quarters allowance. Sent it by return of post. Dined at home. At the billiard room in the afternoon & the whist club in the evening. Drew upon Chapman for £5

A dull morning blowing hard & has been all night from the E by S & ESE with a heavy sea. On board the Hope. Dined at home. At the billiard room in the afternoon & the Albion & Mulstrum in the evening. Gave Bess a turn, first time since
Dined with Mrs Scott & spent the evening at home. Wind & weather the same as yesterday

... upon reflection, I am resigned and convinced that I have been spared a great deal of painful feeling distress & misery by not having witnessed her suffering & tis a consolation to find that she has had so many kind & attentive friends about her, particularly one Mr Vernon, whose conduct both to my poor sister & myself I shall I trust never forget or be ungrateful for. He insists upon my staying at his house & his great anxiety id to console & make me comfortable. Poor little Emma has fortunately been at Captain Butlins at Broomville & the boys at school. Poor children, they are too young to be sensible of the irreparable loss they have sustained. But I trust that god the father of all will spare & enable me to supply the place of their dear parents they have lost. John J Baker came up to see me in the evening

A deluge of rain this morning. Wind about East with a heavy sea. Went by Dunn's coach to Newcastle. Dined & stayed all night at D Dixons. Mentioned to him my having applied to the Duke for a commission in the Northumbria militia of which he approved

Fine weather. For the first time for many days we have seen the sun. Wind ENE & cold with showers. Left Dixon's after breakfast took the steam boat & returned to Shields to dinner. Emma Galbraith looking much better. No letter from WBS, disappointed. At the Mulstrum in the evening.

A fine morning. Been a slight frost with a little snow during the night. Wind NW. Sea much fallen, so that I think many ships will get to sea.

Received a letter from WBS with copies of letters written to the Duke & Lord Beverley applying for a commission for me in the Northumbria Militia. Answered his letter.

Wrote to Bevor's brother to come down to Shields to make some arrangements with regard to the fasern after seeing J Tinley upon the subject.

Dined at home. Spent the evening & suppered with H Harry.

A fine wintery morning having been a very heavy fall of snow during the night. Wind WNW.

Received a letter from B B Galbraith. A bill for £6.0.10 drawn by Stodter of the Eligible club presented for payment, but I did not take it up having no notice. Dined at 5 o'clock with J Dale & in the evening attended the ball at the George which was the best we have had for a long time. Got home at ¼ past 3 o'clock

A continuance of sharp frost. Wind NNW. Very little additional snow fallen in the night. Went by Dunn's coach to Newcastle, there being a meeting of the leiabenantcy & saw Dixon who promised to speak to Captain Carlson respecting a commission for me in the military. Had some dinner with Emma Galbraith & returned by Duna in the afternoon.

Eat a couple of mutton chops at 6 o'clock & finished in the evening at the Albion

A dull morning & every appearance of snow or sleet & looking as if it would thaw. Wind about west. The ship preparing for sea. Received a note from D Dixon stating he had seen Colonel Coulson & that there are several commissions vacant & I must apply through Colonel Coulson.

Accepted a bill for £8.17 the prccuccia for the present voyage: due 27th April dated 18 Jan at 9 months.

Gave Mr Brown of the George Tavern a signature written notice to quit on the 1st Aug next.

On board the Hope. Got a steam boat which towed her to sea with fine NW wind.

Dined at home. At the billiard room in the afternoon & the whist club I the evening. The wind got round & blew hard from the NE & brought on a heavy sea & remained thaw during the whole of the day.
A very fine frosty morning. Wind NW. Wrote to Colonel Coalson applying for a commission. Took a walk round by Tynemouth. Dined at home. At billiard room latter in the afternoon & abbey in the evening

A fine winter's morning. Slight frost & been a great deal of snow during the night & appearance of more. Wind NW.

Went by Durrer's coach to Newcastle & took Robert with me. Tom, Ann & Bell Smith at D Dixons. Tom Dixon & I called at Leadbetters The attorneys & I settled with them as Mrs Scott's executor giving them a draft on Chapmans on WBS & JRS executors account for £108.19.5 which with other payments we have made, leaves only £702 due from us, of the £1000 left under Mrs Scott's will. Robert & Leadbetters received their legacies. Called twice on Colonel Coulson, not at home. Met him afterwards in the street & had some conversation with him as to my application for a commission.

Dined with Mrs Dixon. The whole party excepting myself went to a concert. I called & saw Mr Weatherly & by his advice afterwards called upon Mr Turnbull, deputy clerk of the Peace, but he was not at home.

Suppered at Dixons & slept at the Jessop Hotel

A fine morning & hard frost. Wind NW. Breakfasted at Dixons.

Afterwards called & saw Mr Turnball who wrote out my declaration of qualifications which I signed & which he will deliver to Mr Thorp the clerk of the Peace tomorrow.

Called upon & saw Colonel Coulson who was with Captain Bigg & told him what I had done & had some conversation with them. He of course will immediately apply for a captain's course for me which will most likely come down in the course of the work, as the military is to go into training immediately.

Returned to Shields by steam & dined at home at 2 o'clock. H Harry & Nicholson took wine with me in the afternoon & in the evening I walked to the Mulstrum. Received a letter from WBS

A frosty morning. Rather damp with a fall of snow. Wind NW. Dined at home. Received a letter from B B Galbraith & answered it & also WBS's. At the billiard room in the afternoon & Albion in the evening.

During the afternoon the wind got round to SW, S by W. At night blew fresh at S by E & still frosty.

A fine day. Wind about North. Much refreshed by a good night's rest. Received a letter from William. Wrote to Mrs Scott. F Falknes & Mr J Fitzmaurice called upon me. Took a long & retired walk upon the banks of the river Barrow with Mr Vernon, returned to dine. John J Baker dined with us

Such a winters day. Blowing very hard at ESE and frosty. Wind increased to a perfect hurricane with one continuous shower of snow all day. I fear we shall have bad accounts of the shipping, many vessels being upon the coast. Dined at home and in the evening at the Mulstrum

Storm abated & finer weather. Wind SE and a rapid thaw.

Many ships on shore. Two on the Herd Sand & one a wreck, two on the rocks and broken to pieces, three under the castle light house too scattered to pieces mesher & boy of one drowned a smack at Cullercoats, all hands drowned. Three or four near Whitley, two broke to pieces immediately on coming on shore at night & crews drowned. Walked round by the rock & Tynemouth. Dreadful destruction.

Dined at home. At the billiard room all the afternoon & in the evening Mr Lockword came home with me & drank a glass of punch. Paid an average bill Eligible Club by draft for £6.0.10. Came on to blow almost as hard as ever. Many ships got in today.

A calm morning. Very foggy. Wind S by W & a frost.

Attended a meeting of the Eligible Club & the members agreed to resist Mr Kings of South Shields claim as being unjust.

Dined at home. At the billiard room in the afternoon & whist club in the evening.

Received a letter from WBS of the safe arrival of the Hope & a copy of a letter received from the Duke of Northumbria in answer to his application for a commission in the military for me; very polite.

A very stormy morning. Blew a gale of wind all night from ENE with heavy sleet & rain.

Two ships have got upon the Herd Sand. One from America, the other from ____

Settled with Robert & paid into Chapmans on executors account £65 of rents & drew for £18.11.6 to pay Mrs Noakes, late Miss Robinson for Emma Gilbraith boards etc.

Another small light vessel got upon the Herd.

At the news & billiard rooms all the morning. No moving out such stormy weather. Dined at 5 o'clock with J Tinley, a party. Attended an evening party at the Messes Frenches'
It has been very stormy all night with showers of sleet & snow. Wind this morning got round to NW. Sea very high. One of the ships that got upon the Herd Sand ...

... yesterday gone to pieces.

The Magpie cutter being embayed was obliged yesterday to run for the harbour & providentially got in safe, losing before she took the bar, one of her boats & being obliged to cut away her square-sail, a sea having filled it and they could not take it in.

Sent Mr Leadbetter by Dunn this morning Rawling's valuation of wines etc & also Leadbitter the cook's receipt for her legacy. Dined at home. At the billiard room in the afternoon & attended the whist club at H Dales in the evening. Turned rather frosty. Received a letter from WBS & answered it.

A fine morning & hard frost. Wind NW. Did not go to church. Took a walk to Tynemouth after seeing the newspapers. Some light ships got in today from Leith Roads & also some laden ones passed for London.

Dined at home. At the Mulstrum in the evening. A heavy gale of snow & blowing hard, 12 pm

A dull rainy morning. Wind S by W & SSW. Such unpleasant weather prevented going to Newcastle as I intended. The same course kept me at home on Saturday. Dined at home. At the billiard room in the afternoon. Suppered & spent the evening with a party at Dr Drury's
A mild morning but rather dull; Wind SW. Afterwards turning out a fine day. J Cunningham breakfasted with me & we went up to Newcastle together by steam. Mr Gorthing RA ...

... accompanied us. J Cunningham left me to see captain Maun of the north, wishing to obtain a commission. I called at D Dixon & then went to Mrs Noaks & paid her £18.11.6 for Emma Gailbraith's ¼ year board etc. and also £2.2 entrance for training dancing & drawing. Gostling & I lunched at D Dixons afterwards played at billiards at the rooms & at 5 o'clock returned in a gig to Shields. The ice above the bridge having come away in immense quantities with the ebb tide prevented the steam boats plying.

A fine morning. Rather cloudy. Wind N. Wrote to William. J Harry & Mr Jamison called upon Mr I Called upon & saw poor old Miss Falkman who seemed much affected & grieved at dear Bopy's death. Took a walk to Clogrennane, coll Rockforts seat with Mr Vernon & the boys. Caught in heavy shower of rain on our way home got wet through. The boys dined with us

A very fine mild morning. Wind WSW. Several light ships got down. Went to Milburn Place to see Mr Stephenson respecting remitting £13.10 to London. Afterwards walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. At a party in the evening at Mr W Hewson's

Great confusion & I fear damage in the harbour tonight, the heavy fresh wind having driven the ships adrift.

A beautiful mild spring morning. Wind fresh at about W by S. A great deal of damage done last night amongst the shipping.

Lunched on board the Choice. Dined at home at 5 o'clock, being my birthday, had a party of friends consisting of J & H Dale, H Harry, Mark, H Nicholas & Drury & spent a very pleasant day.

A beautiful day. Quite spring weather. Wind WNW.

In consequence of late homes etc last night & did not breakfast ‘till 12 o'clock. Took a walk round by Tynemouth & dined at home at 5 o'clock.
A delightful morning. Quite spring, mild weather. A light air from about W. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. Attended the whist club at H Harry's in the evening
A continuance of mild weather. Wind SSW. At church in the morning. Dined with H Harry. Received a letter from WBS. In the evening at the Mulstrum.
A beautiful morning. Wind SW. Strolled about the town until dinner at 2 o'clock at home. At the billiard room all the afternoon & at the Albion in the evening

A fine mild morning. Wind SW. Dined at 1 o'clock with J Ridhard on board the Nautilus & in the evening went to a party at J Cunningham's. Wrote a note yesterday to D Dixon requesting him to ask Colonel Coulston if he could give me any positive information about my commission.

A damp morning having been rain in the night. Wind WNW. Received a note from D Dixon, having seen Colonel Coulston who says I shall be in the regiment in a few days for a captaincy. Dined again on board the Nautilus & at the Albion in the evening.

A fine morning blowing fresh at WNW. Went by the coach to Newcastle. Called at the club house to see Colonel Coulson who had left town in the morning. At D Dixons, saw Dixon & the ladies. Called on young Bigger who gave me the names of the trader men in London who have the regulation patterns. Walked down from Newcastle. Met Dr Drury & Mr Harrison near Mr Robson who were on their way to dine with Saddler at the Point & prevailed on me to accompany them. At the whist club & Mulstrum in the evening.

A continuance of fine weather. Wind WNW.

Received a letter from WBS & after breakfast went on board the Jane at his request to see Mr Brown to desire him not to clear the Harmony or of cleared to order the master to stop below Gravesend until after the 1 March when the coal duties are to be taken off.

Attended a meeting at the Commercial & entered into resolutions to be followed up by petitions against the proposed carecase of duty upon north American timber.

Dined at home. At the billiard room in the afternoon. Suppered with H harry

A pleasant day. Wind still from the North. Did not go to church. Read the service at home. Received a letter from William remitting a £50 Bank Post bill. Took a long walk with Mr Vernon along the Athy road & returned to dinner at ½ past 5 o'clock. The boys again with us. W W Fishbrown called upon me

A beautiful morning. Wind NW. Wrote to WBS to order all my clothes etc. for the Northhumbria Regiment immediately, should I be in the Gagelle which is expected. Took wine at the Albion with W C Wright etc. & attended the club at Dr Drury's in the evening.

Withdrew the £500 insurance on the Hope from the Great Premium Club & put it into the Eligible making £1000 in that club. Left a written notice with Bulmers clerk to that effect.

A good deal of rain this evening.

A fine day. Wind NNW. Must have been in the night NNE there being a deal of sea on the bar. Went to church in the morning. Sadler dined with me & H Harry came in & took wine with us. At the Multrum in the evening

A beautiful morning. Wind NW. Much disappointed at not finding my name in the Gazette. Took a long walk with Cunningham round by Preston, Whitley, Cullercoats & Tynemouth. Wrote to WBS with an account of units. Dined at Jebbs at 5 o'clock, a gentleman's party & spent a very pleasant day

Blowing hard half a gale from NNE & has been rain or snow during the night. Called upon the messrs Hdestorns at Mr Reeds. Dined at home & in the evening went to the assembly which was a very good one. About 68 there. Got home at 4 o'clock. Paid Brown 16/ my subscription
A fine frosty morning. Wind WNW. Received a letter from WBS. Walked to Tynemouth. Called upon & had lunch with Jibbs. Dined at 5 o'clock with H Dale & spent a very pleasant day

Another beautiful morning. Wind NW. Received a letter from WBS with his note for £95.10 enclosed. Dined at home. Mr Lockwood to his dinner with me. In the evening at the club. The Samarang frigate got orders to go to Chathace & take all the mariners

A fine morning. Blowing hard at WNW. The Samarang frigate sailed at 1 o'clock. Dined at home. Paid Twigell £2.14. tharp 15/ coates £1.15/ Tygack £1.8. all for the Hope. At the Duke of York & Mulstrum in the evening.

A dull rainy morning. Wind NE. Received the Hope's assales from WBS. Took the 11 o'clock steam boat & went to Newcastle. Called to see Emma Galbraith. Could learn nothing further with regard to our conversation. All as much in the dark & suspense as myself. Saw Dixon & the ladies in Westgate Street where I lunched. Received of the Hindhaugh £36.0.9 being the difference between what the Hope made & 11/- freight applied. Returned by steam by the 4 o'clock boat & came home to dinner. Attended the club at Tibb's in the evening
A thick damp morning. Wind SW. Did not go to church. Dined at home. In the evening at the Abbey & Mulstrums

A fine day. Wind still from the North. Engaged all the morning in examining Dear Betsy's books & papers. In the afternoon Mr Vernon, the boys & I walked out to Crossleigh to see the Herrings & also called upon F Falkener, went round by Old derrgy & home to dinner

A fine but cold morning having been a frost in the night. Wind NW. My name not in the Gazette. Received a letter from WBS stating the season that Lord Melbourn had not made up his mind as to filling up the vacancies. Gave Robert a draft for £5 executor's account for the house. Drew also for £6.9 to pay Mrs Dixon for sundries got for Emma Galbraith. Paid into Chapman on my own account WBS's note for £95.10 & £36.0.9 received of Hindhaugh = 131.16.9. Called upon Dr Drury & gave him a draft on C&C for his bills £11.4/- afterwards walked up to Craigs & took wine at the Mulstrum in the evening.

A very fine morning. Frosty & wind at NW blowing fresh. Called upon Captain Webb. He & I walked round by the high end of the town, Plett's Yard & Chesterton, home to dinner. In the afternoon at the billiard room & at the Duke of York in the evening.

A rainy morning. Wind fresh at W by N. paid Robert £2.4/ Walton the brewer bills 3rd & 4th coal voyage which will be given credit for as sent, be being in asseasy. Engaged today making up ships books. Dined at home. At the Abbey in the evening. The Hope arrived
A rainy morning & light air at SE. Did not go to church. Dr Drury dined with me & H Harry came in after dinner & took wine. At the Mulstrum in the evening

A most beautiful morning. Quite summer weather. Wind NW. Received a letter from WBS. Not yet gazetted. Bound Junior Hall Beal as apprentice for 6 years at £45. At the ship, carpenters still busy with the stern. Gave orders to build the cabin windows up & to put up bulk heads for a sail cabin where the after lockers were. Dined on board the Crives with A Nicholas. At the Duke of York in the evening. Received a letter from WBS

A fine morning. Wind S by W. Received a letter from Captain Crisp adjutant of the regiment stating the Colonel Coulson having received a notification from the Duke of Northamptonshire that my commission was preparing & that I must order my uniform etc & hold myself in readiness to join. Attended a meeting at the North aems, the room full, to petition both houses of parliament to pass the reform bill & setting forth our approval of the measure. Went up to the ship. Dined at home. Wrote to WBS giving him a copy of the above mentioned letter. At the Albion in the evening.

A beautiful morning. Wind NNW. Walked out to Whitley & called upon Mr J Wright & returned home by Cullercoats & Tynemouth to dinner. Dr Drury, Charlton & I had wine at Sears & finished the evening at the Mulstrum

Another beautiful day. Wind SW. Went to Newcastle by steam & ordered coals down on Monday. Enrolled H A Bealls interviews at the Custom House. Returned home to dinner. Dr Drewry & Chartson dined with me. At the club in the evening.

A very wet unpleasant day. Wind between SW & WNW. Could not get to the ship. Received a letter from WBS informing me of my name being in the Gazette, which I see in this days papers. Dined at home. H harry, Cunningham & and I took wine at the Albion & in the evening finished at the Duke of York

A fine morning and wind SW. Received a letter from Alnwick from the adjutant Crisp ordering me to join the Regiment. Walked to Tynemouth with the intention of taking a warm bath, but they are not yet open for the season. Returned & went up to the Hope. Repairs nearly finished. At high water they hauled her off the shore & dropped her down to Custom House Quay. Toward the afternoon it began to blow very hard varying between SSW & SSE & increased to a gale which continued all night. Spent the evening at home writing etc.

A continuance of the same sort of weather with the cool wind. Engaged all the morning with Mr Turner in examining & entering rents. In the afternoon Mr Vernon & I took a walk along the Kilkenny Road, returned home to drefs & took a family dinner with Mr Wen Fishburn who was exceedingly kind, but yet I should have preferred dining quietly at Mr Vernon's. Received a letter from William

A fine morning blowing fresh from WSW. Engaged at home all the morning packing up. Dined at home. Took wine with H Harry. A very rainy afternoon & blowing hard from SSW. At the Abbey & Mulstrum in the evening. Received a letter from WBS

A very fine morning. Wind S by W. Got up early & took gig to Newcastle. Joined the Alnwick coach at 10 o'clock & arrived there 3 o'clock. Found a box with by blue susloop etc at the White Swan. Got a billet at the Star with Potts & two Reeds. Reported myself to the adjutant. Dined at the Keep at 6 o'clock & in the evening went to the Theatre with Major Ogle. A very cold raw day. Heavy rain in the afternoon.

A dull cold evening. Appearance of rain. Wind SSW. Attended drill at 10 o'clock for an hour & half. Portmonteau arrived from town with my red coat etc. Attended drill at 2 o'clock again but for a short time in consequence of the rain. Turned out a very wet day. Dined at Messrs at 6 o'clock & sat rather late.
A very fine morning blowing a cool fresh breeze at SW. Attended parade & marched to the pasture to drill. Drill again in the afternoon. Dined at the mess. Turned out a very wet day.

A fine morning early but afterwards turned very wet. Wind SW. Attended parade, but could not march in consequence of the appearance of rain and the wetness of the ground. Captain Coulson arrived this morning. Drilled in the pasture in the afternoon. Wrote to WBS. Dined at the Mess. Captain Bigg met his company with 6 bottles of port & 3 of claret
A fine day. Wind NW. Parade morning & afternoon & dinner as usual at 6 o'clock

A continuance of fine weather. Parade & dinner as usual. Captain Bigg finished the meeting went late. Consequently did not get to bed until 4 o'clock with until late. Gave ½ dozen bottles of port & ½ dozen bottles of claret.

A change of wind and weather. Wind WSW with heavy rain which warmed the air. Engaged all the morning in taking inventory of furniture & packing up the linin that I intended to go to England. Dined at Coopers Hill. Spent a very quiet & pleasant day

Fine mild weather. Wind West. Attended church parade the whole of the officers & men. Went to church. Paraded at 5 o'clock in the afternoon. Dined at the mess. Captain Biggs finished withing his company. Kept it up very late. Did not get to bed till 4 o'clock in the morning. Received a letter from WBS

Weather continues very fine. Parade as usual at 10 o'clock in the pasture & again at 2 o'clock. Dined at mess. A large party, being stranger day. Mr Bussale of Broom, Pard & others there. Took tea with William Forster

A dull damp morning & rather cool. Wind SE. Did not march to the pasture having been rain in the night & ground very wet. Dined at the mess. Towsouille & others strangers there. Afterwards went to the Bull which was very gay & well attended. After the Bull, suppered with Potts
A very cold morning. Wind NE. At morning drill marched to the pasture & back. Wrote to WBS & attended afternoon parade at 2 o'clock in the pasture. Dined with Jn D Sucth

A fine morning but still cold. Wind NE. Attended morning drill in the pasture. Marched round with my company for the first time. Marched to the pasture again in the afternoon at 2 o'clock marched past slow & quick time & went through the manoeuvres. The two Richards & I went in chaise to dine with Mr Burrell BroomPark. Spent a pleasant day & got home at 2 o'clock.

A dull morning. Exceptionally cold. East wind with showers. Attended 10 o'clock drill, but did not go to the pasture. Received a letter from WBS of the safe arrival of the Hop at London, but not able to sell her coals, the proves quite light. Lunched with W Torston. At 2 o'clock parade marched to the pasture & went through the manoeuvres. Returned earlier than usual in consequence of the rain. Dined at the mess. A stranger day, but a small party. The band had a concert at the Town hall. I took a ticket but did not go.
