A stormy morning. Wind E but with heavy showers of rain & sleet. Continued raining very heavy all day, so that we could not have any parade. Dined at the mess

A beautiful morning. Wind NE. After breakfast got the Johnston's horse & rode to Togston stopping at Warkworth where I met the Smith's after church. Called upon Mr Clatterbuck. Mrs Watson there. Messrs Watson & Mr Burn. Dined & stayed all night at Togston
A fine mild day. Wind WSW. Engaged all day in finishing inventory he. Dined at Mr Vernon's with the boys.

Another delightful morning. Very warm. Wind NE. The Regiment had a field day. The colours out & went through the manoeuvres with great correctness. A great many people on the ground in the pasture. At 2 o'clock marshalled & the men delivered this army and accoutrements into the store. Dined at the mess & went to an evening party at Mr Carr's. Bondgate Hall
A damp day. Wind NNE. The men delivered their clothing out store. After which they were all paid what was due to them. I made ...

... my company a present of 1/- to each man, 2/ to the corpral & 21/- to the three sergeants:

Got my clothes etc all packed up & sent them home by Ellcots the Warkworth carrier. Dined at the mess & being the last we spent a very pleasant & jolly day all regretting that we were to separate but hoping that we shall soon be personally called out.

Robert rode one of Mr Potters horses home.

A very fine day. Wind NNE. Called & left my card at Mr Carr's, Bondgate hall.

Mr Potts having offered me a seat in his carriage, we all lunched together at 1 o'clock at Mr Spousers. The ladies having previously been to see the castle. Started between 2 & 3 o'clock & reached Mr Joblings in Newcastle between 7 & 8 o'clock. Had two glasses of spirits & water which screwed me. Got a gig & reached Shields between 9 & 10 o'clock. Called at the Mulstrum & stayed there till 4 o'clock in the morning.

A very cold day. Wind NE. Did not rise till late. Took a walk to Tynemouth. Dined at home at 5 o'clock. Attended the whist club in the evening. Paid H Dale my contribution, this being the last night of the season £1.4.6

A very cold day. Wind NE. Having been living so well for the last fortnight with the Regiment thought it necessary to take a dose of physic, therefore remained at home all the morning. Spent the afternoon with Dr Drury & in the evening called at the Mulstrum.

A fine morning but very cold. Lockerand breakfasted with me & we went up to Newcastle together by Duma coach. Called at Westgate Street, saw the Dixons and Emma Galbraith who was looking very well & is spending her Easter holidays there. Wrote to WBS. Dined with D Dixon at Tom Fenwick in Charlotte Square. Met a party there. Slept at Miss Willi with Bess

A beautiful morning, but cool wind East. Took the 12 o'clock steamer & got home to dinner at 2 o'clock. Walked to Tynemouth in the afternoon & Cullercoat Sands. All immense numbers of people there. H Harry, Cunningham, Jebbs & I took wine together at the Star & Garter. Returned to the Sands in the evening & had some fun there. Got home at 10 o'clock.

This day rather cooler. Wind NW with showers of rain. Engaged again all the morning in packing up & separating the books that I take to England from those for sale. Called upon Dr Reed & Dr Home. Dined at Mr Vernon's with the boys Received letter from fanny Smith

A most beautiful morning. Wind changed to WNW. Settled Robert's book & paid him £13.-1d my private expenses for the year up to this time. Looked into the Duke's court. Went to Tynemouth races. A great many people there. Dined at 4 o'clock at the Northumberland Alms with McBain & the jury. Called in the evening at the Mulstrum. Wind changed to east.

A very fine morning. Wind NW. Turned out rather showery. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined with Jibbs & afterwards went to the Sands to see the races. Lockerwood and Charlton gave us wine in the evening & finished off at the Mulstrum.

A cloudy morning & every appearance of rain. Wind changeable being raily in the morning from the west & afterwards NE. Received a letter from WBS. Called on Mr Robinson but got no money. The William Shand, Boswell arrived from Rotterdam. Dined at home. Walked to Tynemouth nut nothing doing. In the evening at the Albion & called at the Mulstrum.

A dull morning. Wind SW. Afterwards turned out a most beautiful day, wind a little to E of S. Wrote to WBS with a account of rents. Afterwards J Cunningham & I started & had a most delightful walk to Hastley where we dined with C Ridley & walked home again in the evening. But before we reached Tynemouth at 6 o'clock we were caught in a heavy rain & got thoroughly wet. After taking a glass of whiskey Toddy with JC to keep the cold out, made the best of my way home & changed my cloths & finished at the Mulstrum.

A cloudy morning with showers. Wind blowing fresh at SE. & suddenly changed to SW. With most beautiful spring weather. J Cunningham & I walked up to the Doctors garden & round by Preston when I had some talk with Moon. Dined at home. Dined at home. Took a long walk in the afternoon round by Tynemouth, Cullercoat Sands & at the Albion in the evening.

A dull morning. Wind S by W. changed to fresh breeze from SE. Wrote to WBS & also sent 20/- to Mayt Scott. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at 2 o'clock with Boswell on board the Low Shand. At the Mulstrum in the evening.
A fine spring morning having been showery during the night. Wind S. At church in the morning. Walked to Tynemouth in the afternoon & had a warm bath. Dined with J Tinley at the Mulstrum.

A beautiful spring morning. Been showers in the night. Wind WNW. Received a letter from WBS. Took a walk to Cullercoats with J Cunningham by the Sands. Had a party to dinner at 2 o'clock. H harry, Jebbs, Cunningham & C Ridley from Hartley spent a very pleasant day. E Charlton took wine with us. At the Mulstrum at night or rather in the morning

A most beautiful & mild morning. Quite a summer's day, not a cloud to be seen. C Redley having stopped all night with me, left after breakfast for Newcastle. Wrote to Robert Reed Brandon White House to say I would pay him a visit in a few days. J Cunningham & I again walked by the Sands to Cullercoats . On our return Bess B was waiting on the sands for me. J C went home & I joined & remained with Bess all the afternoon until ½ past 4 o'clock when I came home to dinner, after which I had another walk & finished at the Albion

A little rain in the morning. Wind WSW but afterwards turned out a beautiful day. Wrote to William. Called upon Mr Jameson. Had a very delightful drive in the afternoon to Broomfield. Found the Butlers & Emma quite well, a very affecting meeting, my feelings quite overpowered un & I blubbered like a child, but I could not help it.
A very rainy morning. Wind ESE. Dined at home. Spent the afternoon with Dr Drury & the evening at the Abbey & Mulstrum

A fine morning. Wind NW. The Hope arrived at 5 o'clock am. Went by Duma coach to Newcastle & fixed her to load Bell & Brown being the readiest time & all other collieries being off work excepting Wellington, Pontop & Jaasects. Wrote to WBS. Dined at the George Tavern being the annual dinner of the whist club.

A fine morning. Wind NW. Received the Hopes accounts & balance note £97.9/ = { balance accounts 47.9 : on account 50 } Received also a letter from Leadbottom, the introduction Newcastle w entry a statement of the account between us & Mrs Scott executors which I sent him.

Dined at home. On board the Harvy in the afternoon & went over the bar with: bound to Quebec. Finished off at the Albion & called at the Mulstrum

A fine spring morning. Wind NW. Took a walk with H Harry up to the Hope, taking out the dung at Smiths Crane, proceeded round by Burdon Main, Chirton & Dr Drury's garden. Home to dinner. In the afternoon again walked up to the Doctors garden. Played at Quoits & finished the evening at the Albion
A continuance of fine spring weather. Went to church & heard a most excellent sermon from the vicar's brother. Had a long walk in the castle yard in the afternoon & dined with Jebbs at 4 o'clock

The same sort of weather. Wind changeable. Went to Newcastle by Dunns coach. The collieries all off work, could get no coal. Took the Hope off Bell & Brown's list. Returned by steam. Dined at home. In the afternoon at the news & billiard rooms & finished the evening at the Albion & Mulstrum. H Harry wrote to Hull for a Wybung chailer for me.
Fine weather. Wind ESE. Walked up to the ship with H Harry & round by Percy Main the turnpike, home to dinner. Spent the afternoon on board the Tom Shand & the evening at the Mulstrum. Wrote to WBS

A fine but rather damp morning. Wind ESE. The charter for the Hope arrived by the post from Hull. The Merchants Messrs Wade Sons & Forster Wybury & Hull. 70/ for deals & buttons. The latter not to exceed 6/8. Ordered 3 casks or pork of Bradshaws & 5 loaves of bread of Walkerley & a new main topgallantsail. Dined at home & in the afternoon H Harry gave the Doctor & me some wine at the Northumberland Alms. Afterwards at the Abbey & Mulstrum

A dull cold morning. Wind NE. Paid into Chapmans the hote for £97.9. Gave Stephenson £50. Got the pork, bread etc on board. Had a few friends to dine with me at 5 o'clock. veg Tenley's Rudyard 15th Regiment Dick artillery J Wright & Boswell.

Got captain Hallam to moor the Hope securely by carrying an anchor out astern. Dined with Mrs Scott & spent the evening at Mrs Greenhours, met a large party, a regular squeeze; quadrille & broke up at 12 o'clock. It was cold with snow in the evening
A very wet day. Wind WSW. Captain Butler read the morning service. We afterwards took a drive between showers & returned to dinner

A beautiful morning but cool with a NE wind. Got a cask of rum on board the Hope. Ordered the men on shore as they refused to sign articles for less than £3 per month. Stephenson at Newcastle clearing.

Ministries in a minority of eight upon General Gascoyne's amendment on the reform bill respecting English members. Attended a meeting at the George tavern called in consequence of the minister being in the minority for the purpose of explaining their determination to support them in their proposed grievances & not to give any candidate a vote until he promises to support reform.

Finished at the Albion & Mulstrum.

A dull cold day & blowing fresh from NNE & sea coming on. Received a letter from WBS & answered it. Called at Chapmans, Mr Spence declines answering our note, but proposes continuing the loan on my giving a bill upon WBS to have his acceptance, the time to be afterward agreed upon when I secure WBS's answer. Walked up to the ship, all ready for sea, excepting wind. Towed her down to the low end of the town. Dined at home. On board the Mr Shand in the afternoon & at the Mulstrum in the evening.

A dull damp morning. Wind NNE & much sea. A good deal of rain during the day. An account this morning of there being having prorogued parliament in person. Dined at home. Took wine with the doctor & finished at the Mulstrum.

A dull morning. Wind NNE. Paid by draft on executors account ½ years taxes £14.7.11 & on my own account {premium £8.17, own account £10.15, WBS £5} £24.12. Dined on board the Hope, H Harry & Webb with me. Finished off at the Albion.

A foggy rainy day. Wind SE & SSE. Some ships went to sea amongst them the Geronimi. We could not get men & were therefore obliged to lay. Dined at home. On board the Mr Shand. Spent the evening at the Albion & Mulstrum

Another foggy & rainy morning & but little wind at SSW. Got our men this morning for £2.17.6 per month & have the ship out. Dined at home & in the afternoon the Hope sailed with a fresh breeze at SSE. Finished at the Albion. Received a letter from WBS

Finer weather but still dull & looks like more rain. Called and saw Mr Spear who agreed to take out joint note payable at neis. Leis for the loan of £300 at 4 or 6 months. Wrote to WBS to that effect. Dined with the Committees of the Eligible & United clubs. In the evening at the Malstrum.
A dull morning. Went with Lockwood by Dunn's coach to Newcastle & put up at the Turf Hotel where we also dined at the Wallsend Hunt dinner & stayed all night.

A very rainy day. Wind continues from SE. The election for Newcastle took place. I went to the Guild Hall but I could not get near enough to the hustings to hear any part of the speeches. For Mr Ridley & Mr Hodgson returned without opposition. Lucky fellows. Saw them chained. Had a lunch at the Turf & returned to Shields by Dunn. At the Duke of York & Mulstrum.

A dull morning & all the appearance of more rain. Afterwards turned out a fine warm spring day. Walked to Cullercoats Sands. Ed Charlton dined with me. H Harry & Sadler came in afterwards & took wine. Sadler brought the account from the committee room of the Bell having retired. Finished off at the Mulstrum.
A dull and damp morning. Wind the same. Left Broomville & reached Carlow without rain. Received a letter from William. Dined with Mr Vernon

Weather much the same. Wind about N by E. Tom Smith arrived this morning being his rent day. Walked with him to Tynemouth. Dined at home at 4 o'clock. Received a letter from WBS this morning. Called upon Mrs Robinson but she refused to give me an order on Chapmans for Mr R's debt. At the Mulstrum

A dull orning & damp heavy been a good deal of rain in the night. Wind SE. Lord Howielt & Mr Beaumont came into the town conducted by an immense crowd of people with bands & colours, whom they addressed from a hustings erected in front on the Commercial. Turned out a very rainy afternoon. H Harry dined with us at the Mulstrum. In the evening gave Jonny Smith £28.1.6 Int for his mother.

A fine sprint morning. A light breeze at NE. Tom Smith left for Newcastle after breakfast. Took a walk to Cullercoat Sands & dined with Lockwood & in the evening attended the theatre to see beam. At the Mustrum.

A very fine morning & at last a change of wind having got from the NW. Walked to Tynemouth & from thence by the sands to Whitley Park and called upon Mr J Weight. Wind changes to NNE with heavy showers of hail & rain in one of which I was caught & got nearly wet through. Returned home to dinner. Spent the evening at home.

A fine morning but cold. Wind NW. heavy changed from NE from which ash it has been blowing fresh all night with a heavy sea. Dined at home. At Dr Drury's in the afternoon & in the evening went to the theatre, but the house was so badly attended that Kean would not perform. Finished at the Albion

A very cold day. Wind NE. Received a letter from WBS enclosing our note for £300 at 6 months payable to Messrs Lees which I gave to Mr Spence. Went to Preston Main & his brother signed another lease for 3 years. Walked to Tynemouth & dined at 6 o'clock with Captain William Fanshawe Martin on board the Samarang frigate

A beautiful day but cold. Wind NE. Went to church in the morning. Dined at home. Drank tea at H Harry & walked to Tynemouth in the evening. Had a glass of whiskey toddy at Southerns & finished off at the Mulstrum

A most delightful day. Wind NE. Walked to Tynemouth. The mariners under arrears in case they should be wanted at the collieries. Dined at home. Drank punch on board the Douglas in the afternoon & at the Musltrum in the evening.

A fine morning. Wind ENE. H Harry & I walked by the river side through Howdon to Willington colliery and returned home by the turnpike. The men at work with detachments of the yeomanry & the 15th to protect them. Dined at home & in the afternoon walked up to Billy Mill & took wine with Charlton's. At the Mulstrum in the evening.

Another dull day with showers of rain. Wind WSW. Engaged in the morning writing and walked out with Mr Vernon, returned to dinner. Mr Jameson & Reverend O'Connor dined with us. Spent a very pleasant day
A beautiful morning. Wind SE. Walked to Tynemouth & Cullercoats. Met Bess!! Returned home to dinner. On board the Broderville in the afternoon & walked again to Tynemouth in the evening.

A most beautiful morning. Wind E by S. Ascension day. The Mayor Archibald Reed down in his barge. I breakfasted with him. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at the Albion with Bradshaw. Had an excellent dinner. At the Mulstrum
A dull morning having been rain in the night. Wind E by S. Dined at home. At the Northumberland Arms in the afternoon & walked to Tynemouth in the evening & afterwards called at the Mulstrum

A fine morning but cold. Wind NW afterwards changed to NE & SE. Walked to Tynemouth & Cullercoat Sands. Dined at home. Wrote to WBS sending him a account of may rents. Spent the evening with a party of officers at Lockerwoods
A pleasant morning but still rather cool. Wind WNW. Walked to Tynemouth & Cullercoat Sands. Did not go to church. Dined with H Harry. At the Mulstrum in the evening.

A beautiful morning. Wind NW. received a letter from WBS. Walked to the Doctor's garden. Gave H Harry £11.7.6 which he paid for me on Saturday to Junior Hall, Brokerage Archangel voyage. Dr Drury dined with me & H Harry came in & took wine

Beautiful weather. Wind S by E. H Harry Cunningham & I took a long walk round by Burdon & Percy Main collieries. The pitmen in a very disturbed state. Dined with Dr Drury & in the afternoon walked to Billy Mill to play a quoits & took wine with Charlton. At the Mulstrum in the evening

A delightful morning. Wind SE. Captain William Fanshawe Martin of the Samarang having hired a steamer I accompanied him & a party to Seaham with which we were much pleased and surprised at so vast an undertaking for one individual. Having taken one prog: etc with us we dined at the Prince & embarked again at ½ past 6 o'clock & reached Shields between 10 & 11 o'clock after having spent an uncommonly pleasant day. At the Mulstrum.

A continuance of fine weather, blowing fresh from the ESE. Dined at home at 2 o'clock. At Bradsham's roping in the afternoon playing at quoits & took coffee in the evening at J Tinley's. Wrote to ask R B Reed of Brandon White House to spend next week with me.
A beautiful summers day. Engaged all the morning packing up books then took an hours walk. Dined quietly with Mr Vernon
Beautiful weather. Wind ESE & high sea. Boswell & I walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. Took wine at the George in the afternoon & coffee at Mr Tinley's in the evening.

A cloudy dull morning. Wind NNE. Took a walk to Tynemouth both morning & afternoon. Dined at 6 o'clock on board the Samarang with Captain Martin & spent the evening with Mr Tinley. Rob Reed arrived this evening
A dull morning & blowing fresh from N by E with a sea upon the bar. Went to church in the morning. Walked to Tynemouth in the afternoon. Dined at J Tinley's & called at the Mulstrum at night.

A dull morning & rather cold wind NNE. Dined with Junior Richardson & afterwards went to South Shields races. Very good sport. Potts won the claret jug cards at the Mulstrum. Received a letter from WBS
Beautiful weather. Wind NE. Wrote to WBS. Dined at home. Lockwood dined with us & we afterwards walked over to Shields races. Mostly excellent sport.
Another beautiful day. Wind NS. Dined at home & in the afternoon again went over to South Shields races which were very good. Met Bess there & returned home with her.

A dull cold & unpleasant day. Wind NE. Took a walk round by Tynemouth. Dined at home & in the afternoon walked up to Billy Mill & drank wine with Charlton. Bess came up in the carriage & a pretty finish we made of it.

A dull morning & cool wind NE. Went by Dunn's coach to Newcastle with R Reed. Dined with him at the Half Moon House. He left by coach at 4 o'clock for Mr Ridley's near Chester-le-Street & I returned to Shields by steam. Had some whisky toddy at the Albion & afterwards called to see Bess whom I found very uncoale from the brecisex she accd the night before.

Paid Hope's mo mo £16.10

Another dull morning. The wind still from the old quarter NE. Walked to Tynemouth & saw the troops fire a salute at 12 o'clock in honour of the King's birthday. Returned & also saw the HMS Orestes gun brig do the same & man her yards. Dined at 4 o'clock with Mr Bradshaw in celebration of his wife's birthday, a very pleasant party & most splendid dinner & wines.

A fine morning rather dull wind S by E. Attended morning service. Dined at home. Lockwood took dinner with me. Walked to Tynemouth in the afternoon. Took wine with Tibbs & spent the evening in the castle yard & Lockwood
Another exceedingly fine day. Wind WSW. The boys having a holiday. Went fishing with them but had bad sport. Dined with the Jameson's
A most beautiful morning. Wind ESE. Received a letter from WBS. At Tynemouth all the morning. Dined with Griffiths, RM & Dick RA at the castle. At the Mulstrum in the evening.

A continuance of delightful weather. Wind E by S. Took a walk to Tynemouth & the Sands with Bess. Dined at 6 o'clock. At the Star & Garter. With Mit. Redhead who cosh the dinner by locking his pony to go to Eldon Square in ½ an hour. He did it in 33 minutes.
A most delightful day. Wind NNE & very warm, Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home
Beautiful weather. Wind ENE. Walked to Tynemouth. H Harry, Neill & I Walked up & spent the afternoon with Sadler. Returned in the evening & called at the Mulstrum. Received a letter from WBS

Another beautiful day, rather foggy at sea. Wind NNE. Walked to Tynemouth with Webb. Dined at home. H Harry & I together in the afternoon. Played at Quoits in the evening at the Doctor's garden. Called at the Mulstrum on our way home.
Still fine weather. Wind NE. Walked to Tynemouth & Cullercoat Sands with Bess. Dined at home. Walked again in the evening on the Sands with Bess

A fine morning. Wind NNE. Went to church. Walked to Tynemouth in the afternoon. Dined with J Tinley. At 5 o'clock met Captain Glasscost & Lieutenant Drickey of the HMS Orestes, Major Mitchell & Rudyard at the Mulstrum in the evening

A dull cloudy morning with slight rain & blowing fresh from N by E & good deal of sea on. Received a letter from WBS. Attended a meeting for the relief of the seamen out of employment, whose families are in great distress, subscribed a Guinea. Dined at home. Called at the Doctor's & walked up to his garden & spent the evening playing at quoits. At the Albion

A dull morning. Wind NW. Afterwards turned out a most delightful day & the wind again from the old quarter NE. Walked up to High Cheston & called upon Mr Robson as bridegroom. Dined at home. At Tynemouth in the evening.. Took coffee with J Tinley.

A dull cloudy morning. Wind NW. Glass fallen & more the appearance of rain. Received a letter from Emma Galbraith informing me of the holy days commencing on the 17th. But glad to see her so much improved in her writing. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. At Tynemouth again & Cullercoat Sands in the afternoon & evening. At the Albion.

Towards noon the wind got into the old quarter NE again & turned out a most beautiful day.

A fine spring day with a shower of rain in the morning. Wind SW. Mr Vernon & I walked out to_____ & dined with J Fitzmaurice. The house stands about halfway up the mountain & commands a most extensive & beautiful view of the surrounding country for many miles, bounded by the Wiklow & other mountains, taking in Carlow in north 10 miles or more off & other towns. We spent a very pleasant day. Received from & wrote a letter to William

A fine morning. Rather cloudy. Wind W by N. Afterwards NE. H Harry & I walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. Went again to Tynemouth in the afternoon. Saw Bess became friends again & had a long walk with her. Got to the Mont, trcien about 11 o'clock

At last a change in the weather, having rain, but wild & wind WSW. A fine growing day. Dined at home. Spent the afternoon with Bess at Mrs Woodham's. H Harry & I walked to Tynemouth in the evening. Called on our return at the Duke of York & afterwards at the Mulstrum.

A very wet morning. The rain will do great good. The country being much in want of it. Wind E by S. Dined at home. Spent the afternoon on board the Telemachus, with Mr Bradshaw. At the Albion & Mulstrum in the evening

A beautiful morning. Wind WNW but in the middle of the day again changed to SE. Did not go to church. Dined at home. In the afternoon walked to Billy Mill & took wine with Charlton. Walked to Tynemouth in the evening & afterwards at the Commercial & Mulstrum

A fine morning. Wind SE. Received a letter yesterday from Stephenson of his arrival at Wyburg on the 13th May & his lower-hold being full at the date of his letter, the 20th. Went by steamer to Newcastle. I walked out to Benton to dine & stay all night. Mrs Smith & Fanny just arrived from Togston & entered taking Emma Galbraith back with them on Saturday

A beautiful morning. Wind SW. Very unwell last night & all the day suffered from eating some salmon. Walked into Newcastle with D Dixon. Saw Emma Galbraith & took the steam boat to Shields. Dined with Doctor & afterwards walked up to his garden. Very unwell this evening. Took some tincture of rhubarb a couple of pills & went early to bed.

A fine morning blowing fresh at SW by S. Received a letter from Stephenson of his safe arrival at Hull after a fine passage of sixteen days from Wynburg (Cape Town). He has to lay 8 days quarantine.

Paid average Hope Club £9.17.6 & Mrs Brown sail-making etc. £5.15.6. Wrote to Stephenson. Dined at home. Went on board William C Wright's ship the Mulgrave Castle with H Harry, bound to Archangel. At the Albion & afterwards at the Mulstrum

A fine growing morning. Been a shower & the appearance of more rain. Wind SW.

Received a letter (post paid) from Harenan & Co, London, enclosing Stephenson's WyBurg bills of £50.5/ for acceptance. Accepted at by leave of Chapman's payable at Barketts & Co, dated 29th Aug & returned it by post. Lockwood dined with me. Walked round in the afternoon by the Doctor's garden to Tynemouth. At Tynemouth also in the morning. At the Albion & Mulstrum in the evening.

A beautiful morning. Wind about West. Received a letter from WBS from Carlow & clear Stephenson's letter from Wyburg of his being loaded. Wrote to WBS. Dined at home. Walked to Tynemouth in the afternoon with H Harry. At the Duke of York & Mulstrum

A dull morning. Wind SSW. A shower of rain about 1 o'clock. Lieutenant Griffin RM took his dinner with me & Webb came along afterwards. Walked to Tynemouth in the evening. Paid E Reid's mother £2.6.9 balance of gegarayers wages

Another fine spring day, very warm, with a few gentle showers. Wind SW. Engaged in the morning packing then called upon Mr W Fishbeam. Dined at Mr Vernon. The two Mr Cureys dined with us. Spent a very pleasant evening

A fine morning. Wind SW. Went to church. Walked to Tynemouth. One company of the 60th marched for Newcastle. Lockerwood, J Rudyard & Griffin dined with me at Tynemouth again in the evening & afterwards at the Mulstrum.

A fine morning. Wind about West. Gave Roberts a draft for £5 for the house. Got £5 of Chapmans on my own account. H Harry & I took the steamer to Newcastle & walked up to the course. The two last races very well contested. Very little company there ended & left from there usual. Dined at the Grand Stand. Walked into Newcastle again & returned to Shields which we did not reach until 11 o'clock having been agreed at St Peter's & 3 ½ hours in coming down. At the Mulstrum
A cloudy dull morning. Wind SW. Lunched with J Tinley who afterwards drove us up in his phaeton to the races. The racing as good as could be. Returned to Tinley's to dinner at ½ past 7 o'clock

A fine morning. Wind SE. received a letter from Stephenson informing us of the ship's being released from quarantine on the Monday before she took the ground as she delivered in the old harbour at Mr Eade's warf. Bathed for the first time this season. Dined at home. H Harry, Richardson & I went over the water to Bullocks & had some peanalary. At the Albion in the evening & afterwards at the Mulstrum.

A fine morning. Wind SE having been west at night. Lunched with J Tinley who afterwards drove me, Major Garthwest etc to the races which were but indifferent but attended by crowds of people. Got home to dinner at 7 o'clock in the evening. At the Mulstrum.

A fine growing rain & been showers during the night. Wind WNW. Glass fallen.

Paid £14 into Chapman's on account of executors. Dined at home. At the Albion in the afternoon & in the evening walked to Tynemouth. At the Mulstrum at night.

A dull cloudy day with showers. Wind variable between NNE & NNW. Received a letter from WBS from Dublin of his intention of being here tomorrow or Monday. Went over the water to enquire about the coach to York. Dined at home. Engaged writing etc. in the afternoon & at the Albion in the evening. A very rainy night.

A dull morning but fair. Wind fresh at N by E & NNE. Crossed the water & got on the coach for York westside at 8 o'clock where we arrived at 6 o'clock to dinner after a very pleasant drive without rain. Got an inside in the march at ½ past 7 o'clock & arrived at Hull at ½ past 12 o'clock. A beautiful moonlight night. Drank a glass of whiskey Toddy & went to bed.

A dull morning. Wind N by E. After breakfast went & Mr Garbertts, met Stephenson on the road. Afterwards walked to the ship & saw the merchant but would not freight until the ship is out. Dined on board. A heavy thunder storm in the afternoon & continued to rain all day. Stephenson & I in the evening walked round the docks etc & finished with a glass of toddy at the Ina

A dull & very sultry close morning. Wind N by W & NNW. Called upon Martin Orr at the Garrison. Saw Mr Garbutt but declined fixing a foreign mail being expected & the chance of freights being better. H French dined with me on board after having a long walk about the town. The ship out & cleared this afternoon. Wrote to Bess B. Martin Orr & his wife called upon me at the ship. Set H French part of the way home & amused myself the remainder of the evening by strolling round the town. Turned out a very rainy day.

A fine day but cold wind NW. Went to church in the morning & heard a very good discourse from Mr Vernon. Wrote a letter to Mrs Scott. Dined at the Mr Careys & spent an extremely pleasant day. Present Mr Vernon, Captain Warren (65th regiment), 2 Careys, Ed Butler & Mr Ballerely. Came into wine

A very rainy morning. Wind NW. Called at Garbutt's. Stephenson busy paying dock dues etc. & getting ships provisions on board. The rain & wind prevented the lighters working & we got no ballast today. Dined at 4 o'clock with J Bell. Mr Ward dined with us. In the evening walked to H French's house & spent it with nens & Fanny

Finer weather. Wind NNW. Breakfasted with Orr & his wife at the Garrison. Saw the armoury containing the arms of all the local militias etc of the district, about 20000. Walked up to the ship, a lighter up with 40 tons of ballast. At Garbutt's, Wade not having got the deal counted are unable to settle the freight. Dined on board. Walked about the town & docks in the afternoon & spent the evening with Orr. Wrote to WBS

A fine morning. Wind NNW. At Mr Garbutt's & on board the ship. Got the remainder of her ballast. Went out with Mr Bell to dine with his partner Junior Wood. At Hezzle (Hessle, Hull), met a party there

A most delightful morning. Wind SW. the Hope warped down to Southend pier & at high water sailed for Wyburg. Mr Garbutt settled the freight with the merchant & I settled his account for brokerage etc receiving a bill at 4 months, accepted payment at Glgme & their bills at 2 months for balance of first half freight smith to £50.4 & cash £1-9-9. Mr Garbutt's account £15.6.6

Dined with Mr Garbutt & in the evening H French took grog with me at the Cross Keys. Received of Mr Stephenson £8- to give the carpenter's wife £5 & the cook £3. Paid Stephenson £6.0.1 the balance of his Wyburg account due to him.

A fine morning. Wind SW. Started at 6 o'clock from the Cross Keys having taken an outside place & arrived at York at 12 o'clock noon. Saw the interior of the Minster & passed the afternoon in walking about the town & banks of the river. Dined at the Black Swan at ½ past 5 o'clock and mounted the Shields mail at 9 o'clock. A fine evening.

A most beautiful morning. Wind with the heat got to ENE. Arrived at Shields at 7 o'clock. Crossed the water & got home in time to go to the Low Lights & bath before breakfast. Dined at home. Being excessively sleepy, turned into bed for three hours. Walked after tea up to Preston through the fields to examine them & see moors. Went to the theatre in the evening & afterwards called at the Mulstrum to see Bess
A fine warm morning . Wind W by N & looks like showers. Dined at home. Walked to Tynemouth in the afternoon. At the Albion & Mulstrum in the evening

A most beautiful morning. Wind E by S. paid into Chapmans a bill at 4 months, Weider accepted on Hoarses for £175. Took a walk round by the rocks to Tynemouth. Dined at 5 o'clock With Mr J Metcalf & went to the theatre in the evening being thebespeak of the officers of the marines. At the Mulstrum
A fine day with a cool NW wind. The cattle fair at Carlow, town was crowded. Got the last trunk nearly packed with books, plates etc. Dined at Mr Vernon

A most delightful morning. Wind SE. paid Walnsley baker £9.3, Morris butcher £9, Bradshaws Irish pork 3 casks £9. J Tinley dined with us at 5 o'clock. Ben Galbraith & I walked to Tynemouth in the evening.

Beautiful weather. Wind SE. Went with WBS on board the City of Edinburgh to take his birth to London.

Bathed at 1 o'clock. Accompanied a party of officers to Wallsend and dined with Hotts a large party & spent a very pleasant day. He was so kind as to send his carriage for us. At the Mulstrum in the evening.

A fine day. Wind SE. Moor & his brothers with J Tinley with us. Foster Moor signed a document making over to us all his stack & crop etc & resigning the farm which we have allowed Mr Moor to take as tinanl. Walked up to Preston. People busy with the potatoes & turnips & clearing the hedges. Gave in a draft on Chapmans for £20 for WBS. Dined at 2 o'clock. Went on board the City of Edinburgh steamer with WBS & saw him sail for London. Ben & I walked to Tynemouth in the evening. A heavy rain about ½ past 10 o'clock

A fine morning after the rain, having been a good deal in the night 7 the appearance yet of more wind E by N & ENE. At church in the morning. D Dixon called but we were out. Dined at home. Took tea with Messrs Harry, walked to Tynemouth in the evening. Very foggy & damp. Finished at H Harry's with a glass of whiskey

A dull morning. Wind ESE. Very foggy. Ben & I got on board a steamer & went to Newcastle. Saw D Dixon. I walked with him out to Benton, dined & in the evening walked through the country to Shields. Called at the Mustrum

A continuance of foggy weather. Wind ENE. Paid Gibson butcher. Wyburg £8.6/-. Walked to Tynemouth & afterwards out to Preston & dined with Mr Wright. Walked home again in the evening. Called at the Mulstrum
A very unpleasant foggy & damp morning. Wind NE. Cleared away towards noon. I joined Mr Ilderton & ofserted in his canses also promised him my vote. Dined with him & party at the George at 5 o'clock

A cloudy morning with the appearance of showers having been showers during the night. Wind SE. Ben Galbraith & Robert set off in Dunn's gig to catch the Alnwick coach at Newcastle for Felton where Tom Smith's phaeton will meet them. I could not go having promised to continue my assistance to Mr Ilderton all day & very successful. Sat down to dinner at 5 o'clock. Called at the Albion in the evening.

A dull cloudy morning & been some rain. Wind ENE. A very heavy rain for an hour or so which prevented us beginning our canvas until near 11 o'clock commencing at the Wooden bridge & canvassed all the upper part of the town. Milburn Place etc and were very successful. Lunched at Mr Barkers & canvassed Tynemouth in the evening. Dined at 8 o'clock & spent a jolly evening.

A fine morning. Breakfasted early & took the 8 o'clock steamer for Newcastle & at 1 o'clock got upon the coach for Felton where I arrived at a little after 1 o'clock. Had an early dinner & afterwards borrowed a nod of Melrose & had a few hours fishing but little success. Walked down in the cool of the evening to Togston. Got there at ½ past 6 o'clock. Found the Clutterbucks dining there.
A very wet morning. Wind WSW & heavy showers of rain. Engaged part of the morning packing. Took a long walk with Mr Vernon & returned to dinner
A most beautiful day. Wind SW. Accompanied the family to church at Warkworth. We gin then amused ourselves strolling about until dinner time. Mr Burn came up to wine & spent the evening.
A dull morning. Wind SW with showers. Ioma Dixon, Baker Cmenon & I walked down to Amble. I had a little fishing but caught nothing. Dined a family party

A fine morning blowing fresh at SW. Tom Smith, Dixon & I after breakfast walked to Hauxley & with Major Clatterbuck rowed across in a coble to Coquet Island the first time of my being there much pleased with the trip. The island covered with thousands of birds of the tern species. Returned to Togston by the links & Amble
A delightful day & fresh SW breeze. Mr & Mrs Dixon left us for Benton. Walked to the Burches & Colleerg with Tom, Lady Smith & family of Tyleys. Called & took lunch. A family party to dinner

A dull morning. Wind SW. Baker Kop Snowdon & I walked down to waterside to finish, by the time we got there it began to rain heavily, which gave us a soaking. Had but poor sport. Killed about a dozen, not large but fine fish. Returned to dinner at ½ past 4 o'clock
Another dull morning, blowing hard from SW with heavy showers which prevented us going to the hermitage as intended

A most beautiful day. Ben Galbraith, Rob Snowdon & I after breakfast, set off to fish at the Hermitage. I however turned off to begin at the Granary but the tide had risen too high. Walked up to the mill streams & fished there all the morning. Fanny & Bell Smith & Emma Galbraith came down & joined us & we all dined together at the Hermitage Inn. Fished up the waterside & Morick streams in the evening but had very poor sport. Got home to supper after spending a most delightful day.
Dined with Mrs Scott. Spent the evening with the Whist club. Lost 4/-. Wind SE with frost. Wrote to Sir D Smith
A beautiful day. Engaged in the morning at the house. Left Carlow about 2 o'clock in a post chase with Mr Vernon for Broomville where we arrived at dinner

A continuance of fine weather. Tom Smith taken suddenly ill. Tom, Bea & I drove down to church, returned home after calling upon Mr Clutterbuck by Amble. Dined at 3 o'clock & took a walk with Emma Galbraith & Tom round the farm in the evening

Beautiful weather. After breakfast, Tom drove Ben & I into Alnwick being fair day. Called upon Ian W Smith who with others of the family being very unwell, we did not go in. Called upon Captain Wund Forster & got home to dinner at 5 o'clock.

Most beautiful weather. Wind SW. Walked down after breakfast to Amble & fish the Granary Stream but without success. Ben Galbraith & Rob Smith with me afterwards. Ben & I bathed & then joined Tom at Amble. Looked over his fields there. Turnips in a very bad state. Got home to dinner at 3 o'clock. Mr Ellenth dined with us. Mrs Scott much better.

Still delightful weather. After breakfast Tom & I set off for Newcastle in his jones Auisn. Stopped at Morpeth for two hours. Saw Shapton & got to Newcastle at 5 o'clock to dinner. Saw the High Sherriff, Mr Silvertop go out accompanied by a very numerous train of friends & carriages to meet the judges. The High Sheriff turned out very handsome. Took a gig in the evening & got home a little before 10 o'clock

A glorious day. Wind SW. Went up to Newcastle by Dunn's Gig in the morning. Saw & had some conversation about Mr Haig regagatted & placed below Lorain & Cleaning could make nothing of him. He evidently the friend of the other Party. went go up ...

... to London &see the Duke told Colonel Coulson it was my intention. Went to the courts, excessively hot, glad to get out again after strolling about with Tom Smith & Dixon. Returned to Shields to dinner at 5 o'clock. Attended Mr Alderton's Committee room in the evening. At the Albion & Mulstrum.

A fine morning but very hot weather. Gave a draft on Cols for balance of Premium and Hope clubs £4.7.1 also a draft for £6.15 momo to be paid tomorrow. Attended Mr Ilderton's Committee room and came after Lenskill Street. Dined at home. At the Committee Room again in the afternoon. A fine shower of rain in the afterwards. At the theatre & Mulstrum in the evening

A beautiful morning but very hot wind ESE. Had a cold bath in the sea before breakfast. Paid the people there mo mo £5.15/-. At the Committee Room & canvassing. Dined at home. Walked to Tynemouth in the evening. Finished at the Albion.
A continuation of most delightful weather. Wind from the S & E. At church in the morning. Dined at home. Lockerwood dined with me. H Harry came in & took wine. At Tynemouth & Mulstrum in the evening.
A most delightful morning. Wind WNW. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined & spent a very pleasant day with H Dale, I Dale Joe Hawkes & Mark there. Received a letter from WBS. Paid Cheghton for rum £4.6
A fine summers day. Amused myself with fly fishing, but had poor sport. Returned to captain Butlers to dinner. Mr & Mrs S George dined with us. Spent a very pleasant day

A beautiful day. Wind SW & ESE. Walked to Tynemouth. Ben Gailbraith went to Newcastle to see Emma. At Tynemouth again in the afternoon. Had a most delightful bath at the end of Cullercoats Sands & dined with Lieutenant Mitchel & Lockerwood at the castle. Bess met me on the mound, gave her a long lecture but query it has any good effect. Heavy shower of rain

A very fine morning. Wind NW. Bathed before breakfast. Engaged at home writing. Dined at home. Called and took a glass of wine with the Doctor. Walked up to Tynemouth. Called & spent the evening at the Castle. At the Mulstrum at night. Paid Brown Tarters 17/-

A fine morning. Wind NNE. Assisted Roberts in packing up my cloths. Drew on Chapmans £15 on my own account & £20 on executors account for BB Galgraith's expenses to London etc. Dined at home at 2 o'clock. Wrote to Bess B: & sent £5. Embarked at 5 o'clock on board the City of Edinburgh steamer & sailed a little after 6 o'clock, having on board about 40 passengers. A most beautiful evening's walk a little swell at sea which soon sent some of the crewmen along ...

A most beautiful morning. Wind from the N & E. Got up at 8 o'clock & breakfasted at 9 o'clock. From the noise & tremulous motion caused by the engine I got very little sleep. The boat off Scarborough at 3 o'clock in the morning & landed Mr J Brandling etc & passed Flamborough Head at 5 o'clock & the Dadgeon light about 1 o'clock. Dined at 3 o'clock & at the same time off Cromer. It was after 8 o'clock before we got through the Roads.

Turned out at ½ past 5 o'clock the vessel a little below the Nore light. A fine morning with a fresh breeze from the NW. Having a strong ebb tide against us, we did not reach Blackwell until about 1 o'clock when J Mitchell RM, Ben & I put all our luggage into a boat & rowed up to the tower stairs, took a coach & drove to Philpot Lane & therein to Nottingham place. Ben & I there walked out. Dined at 6 o'clock at Richmond, Mitchell & Bob Marsh dined with us. With the latter I became reconciled and friendly again he having explained his sorrow & shame at his conduct towards me. This reconciliation has contributed much to the pleasure of my visit to London together with a letter received from Colonel Foswell saying that he will pay his son's debt to me, which may be considered a god send; It will however enable me to pay my expenses & so enjoy my visit the more.
A dull morning with rain. Wind NNE. Did not go out till near 12 o'clock. Called upon MrWard & Richmond. Wrote to Bess. WBS, Ben Galbraith & I dined at the Blue Posts & afterwards went to Astleys

A most beautiful morning. WBS & I walked down to & called at Northumberland House. Saw and had a long conversation with Mr Boyle who thought that I had not been well treated. Called & sat with Bob Marsh, went with him to the court of chancery, afterwards had a long wait round by the west end. Towards dinner time we had a tremendous heavy storm of rain, thunder & lightening. Dined with Richardson at 6 o'clock, and in the evening took a boat at Westminster Bridge & went to Vauxhall but did not go in as there were no fine works. Returned & got into the gallery of the House of Commons where we sat until 2 o'clock in the morning. Nothing interesting going on.

A beautiful morning. Wind about N. After breakfast got upon a Paddington Stage & rode into the city to get my fishing rods. Surprised but could not find Kitchinman. The juaker, droked Lane having been cleaned away for the approach to London Bridge. Walked out of the city to the west end. Called upon & dined with Richmond. W Richmond & Miss Legg dinned with us. Got to Nottingham Place at 12 o'clock
A fine day. Got up at 5 o'clock to fish but had no sport. Tried again breakfast. Fished the whole of the morning but never had a rise, in consequence I suppose of the wind being from the east

A dull morning having been rain in the night. Wind fresh at WNW. In endeavouring to throw my portmanteau upon my shoulder, it being very heavy, I strained the muscles of my back very severely & I fear I shall not soon recover from it. Pain very acute. Got on the coach at the White Horse ally at 8 o'clock with WBS & BBG & started for Southampton where we arrived at ½ past 4 o'clock having had very fine weather & a pleasant journey, the dust being laid by the rain. My back very painful & with some difficulty got down to my lodgings & to bed. We got Mrs Sands lodgings, the same as when at Southampton before.

A fine day & blowing fresh from the WNW. I made an attempt to get out of bed this morning but my back was so bad I was obliged to lay down again. Breakfasted in bed. About 1 o'clock determined to make another attempt to get up & dress myself & with much difficulty & pain & the assistance of Ben I succeeded. After being up & walking a short time, found myself much easier. Walked down to the Pier & baths. Had a warm bath & Mr Lee afterwards drove me home in his gig. The remainder of the afternoon & evening found myself much relieved. About dinner time we had a very heavy squall with rain.

A fine morning but blowing hard from the N by E. got up & walked to Mr Lee's to breakfast. Walked down to the post office & pier. Mr Lee drove me down to Shirley to call upon the Lewis. Dined at Mr Lees
A beautiful morning . Wind fresh from N by E. Played at billiards. The Lewis's came in & dined at Mr Lees. Messrs Horsford & Hawksley came in the evening. My back much better.

An exceedingly fine morning. Wind SW. Wrote to Garbull & son of Hull to inform him when the Hope arrived etc. Dined at 2 o'clock at Mr lee's. The Lewis there & embarked at ½ past 5 o'clock on board the Ariadne steam boat at 6 o'clock. Sailed for Guernsey with a good many passengers on board. A most beautiful evening. Moon light & not a cloud to be seen. I walked the deck until we had passed the Needles & went to bed at 12 o'clock. R Marsh with us

A fine morning. Rather cloudy. Wind SW. Got up at 6 o'clock at which time we were abreast of the ____ with Alderney, Sark & Guernsey or St Peters Port in sight. Came to an anchor in Guernsey Sands about 8 o'clock & landed after a most delightful passage. The town of St Peter port is beautifully situated above the bay upon a rising hill & consists of a great many very excellent houses. It is of considerable extent but the streets are narrow. It however is rapidly improving and contains a great many beautiful private houses as well as public institutions, the collage the most striking ...

We put up at Mousehole Hotel which is near the harbour & the back bed room window commanded an exceedingly fine view of the sea adjacent islands. This hotel I recommend to all travellers both for the activity & attention of the landlady & her daughter Mrs ____ & their reasonable charges. There is a small harbour formed by piers which is dry at low water. The rise and fall is very considerable being I should think thirty feet.

Having changed our cloths & made ourselves comfortable we had breakfast. Much to our surprise met James Basher in the coffee room who agreed to join our party at dinner. After breakfast strolled out to see the town. Much pleased with the new market. Fish & butchers etc. It is the best & most perfect thing of the kind I ever saw or heard of.

Afterwards called upon Dr Proctor who was not at home. Went over & saw the interior of the collage, a very fine institution & apparently well placed & of it were not for the low heavy square towers in the centre would be a handsome building.

During the afternoon saw the presence feast of the town & walked up to the garrison which stands very high upon the south point of the bay which with the town, it & fort completely commands. In our rambles we met with old Charlton late of the firm of Scott & Charlton, who came & dined with us at 6 o'clock. He has lived about a year here. Saw Dr Proctor this afternoon. Much pleased with him.

Most delightful weather. Wind SW. Had a warm bath this morning. At 12 o'clock we all got into a four wheeled vehicle. Drove round the greater part of the island, excepting the north angles, but there is nothing very picturesque or beautiful to be seen. Got home to dinner at 6 o'clock. Ian Basnes dines out

A continuance of fine weather. Amused ourselves by strolling about the markets etc. William went & saw Dr Proctor again, but I being tired did not go. Having settled our bill, at 2 o'clock we again embarked on board the Ariadne & sailed about 9 o'clock. The vessel most uncomfortably crowded, being about 155 passengers on board. We could not get berths. Passed close by the Island of Alderney. A fine sight.
A dull morning with fine spring showers. Left Captain Butlers & returned to Carlow. Mr Vernon & I dined at Mr Butlins & met a very pleasant party

A dull morning. Wind SW. We arrived at Southampton at ½ past 5 o'clock, very much fatigued having been waiting to sleep or lay on deck all night. After waiting two hours & a half at the custom house, we were obliged to go home to breakfast without our luggage. Dined at the Lewises at Shirley. Colonel Ogilvie & Captain Cobb there.
A most beautiful day. Wind NW. Did not go to church. After lunch took a walk round by the Pier, the baths to the Itchen & crossed the ferry to see PearTree Green. Returned to dinner

A continuance of delightful weather. Wind SW. Passed the morning in walking about, playing at billiards etc. Wrote to the Duke of Northumberland at court requesting him to grant me an interview & complaining of my having been a second time passed for the purpose of Captains Loraiac & being placed over my head. Dined at Mr Lees

Another fine day. Wind SW. Again engaged much the same as yesterday. Received a letter from Stephenson as which both Roads dated the 24th all well. The Lewis' & Mr Carry dined with us. Major Falls of the 93rd & Colonel Ogilvie came in the evening.

A dull morning. Wind SW. Bob Marsh left for London. Received an answer from the Duke referring me to Colonel Coulson. The Duke tied up with the gout & not able to see me. Wrote to Stephenson, Major Falls, Colonel Ogilvie, William & I went to Shirley to dine. Amused ourselves in rifle shooting

A miserable cold morning. Wind NE. rained continuously all day. After breakfast packed up my cloths & spent the remainder of the day till dinner playing at billiards until Colonel Ogilvie, captain Lewis & Harry RM. The former of whom with Major Falls dined with us.

A fine clear morning. Wind NW but cool. After breakfasting with Mr Lee, got upon the Red Robin coach driven by Pearce at 10 o'clock & started for Town where we arrived at ¼ before 7 o'clock travelling a new & by far the more beautiful road, over the Hog Back. Here we had a drenching shower of rain & hail, through Guilford to town. Got to Nottingham Place at 7 o'clock. Had a cup of tea & went to bed at 10 o'clock
A fine morning. Wind NW. Walked into the city by Regents Street called at Oliphant's & got a new hat. Passed along the Strand & returned from the city & dined with C Richmond at ½ past 5 o'clock

A fine morning. Wind WSW. Breakfasted with C Richmond. He drove me in the afternoon around & called upon Mrs Fletcher alias Hoffman then through the park by Pimlico & Westminster to Greenwich. Called & saw George Watt and his wife, dined off whitebait etc. at the Crown & Sceptre & returned to town at 7 o'clock to tea. Got home in good time
A beautiful summers day. Went to Free Church in the morning & afterwards walked to Crossleigh with the boys. Dined at the Jamesons

A fine morning. Wind SW & warm. Took the Paddington Stage into the city. Went to the office, nothing there, at the Coal Exchange. Saw there Brown & Fenwick. Walked out of the city. Called upon Bob Marsh, strolled round by Pall Mall, St James's Street & Piccadilly to Richmond's to dinner.

Got to Nottingham place at ½ past 10 o'clock & found WBS Mary & Lee had arrived.

A fine day. Rather close. WBS went out the city. Arrived myself in the West End of the town all the morning. Dined at ½ past 5 o'clock with Junior Wright at Blackfriars, a small party there. Crg Richmond, G Walters, Mr Gordon, G Kain & two Miss Jobling's of Austlery

A dull unpleasant morning. Heavy showers all day. Wind SW. Took a walk & called upon Mr Lenskill & Mr Ward. Met Captain Shepherd in the Burley Tea Arcade who has got appointed to the HMS Melville 74 & going out to the East Indies with admiral Sir John Gore. Dined with Richmond at 6 o'clock to meet Mr & Mrs Hoffman alias Mary Fletcher, his sister & J Wrights

A fine morning. Wind SW. The town all alive & on the move towards Charring Cross, Pall Mall etc. to see Coronation Procession. After breakfast I went out but could not see the procession, so great was the crowd. It appearing however to be near the United Services Club House after it had passed I saw major Falls who asked me in & upon I had a very fine view of the whole of it on its return. A most splendid & magnificent sight it was. Saw there Majesties very distinctly. Unfortunately there was a great deal of rain which they were in the Abbey which made the streets very dirty & dampt the pleasure of the people no doubt very much. Dined with Bob Marsh & in the evening saw the illuminations which passed good

A very unpleasant day. Rained incessantly. Wind NW. Did not go out until 2 o'clock. Called upon Beverley who was not at home. Left my card. Walked down to Bob Marsh and Richmond's. Got a letter from Stephenson who will not be cleared so soon as expected. Answered it & told him I should not be at Hull & of my intention to leave town on Tuesday by the city of Edinburgh steamer. Called at Hawtry the dentists & got my teeth cleaned. Dined at 6 o'clock at Nottingham Place. Richmond & Bob Marsh dined with us.

Still damp unpleasant weather & appearance of more rain. Wind NW. Called a little earlier upon Lord Beverley who had again gone out. Returned to Nottingham Place. At 2 o'clock walked down to Charring Cross & there got upon a stage & went to the Elephant & castle & thence walked to George Harry Apollo Buildings, Walworth & saw Henry H. who I found laid up, being much bruised & injured by the upsetting of a Blackwell Stage. Returned by stage & dined at ½ past 5 o'clock with Richmond. Walked home early in the evening.

A continuance of dull cloudy weather, wind NNW & every appearance of more rain. William, Emma & Lee went to church. I did not go being obliged to take some Cuberts. At 3 o'clock walked through the Regents Park to the Zoological Gardens with which & the collection of wild beasts. I was much pleased. Returned home & dressed & went to dine with Mr Leaskill at 7 o'clock, a small party, only Captain Greg & myself there

A fine day but rather cloudy. Wind NW & NNW. After lunch walked down to St James street & saw the nobility etc. go to court. Her Majesty holding a drawing room.

Dined with C Reibarud. J Griffith & WBS there.

Mary Scott (daughter of WBS) went to school

A very fine morning. Wind N by W. Wrote to Robert Snowdon. Lee Scott went to School. Walked down to St James Street. His Majesty holding a Levee went along the Strand & called on Bob Marsh. Returned & saw the company come from the Levee. Walked with WBS in Regent Street at 6 o'clock dined alone at the Blue Ports & afterwards went home.
A fine day engaged all the morning in preparing for the sale. Dined quietly at home, wrote to A Fitzmaurice

A beautiful day. Wind from the N & E. Wrote a letter to Lord Beverley & afterwards called upon him & found him at home, very graciously received. Entered into a long account & related to him all the inconsistencies respecting any complaint about being regazzetted etc, but he could not interfere at the same. Explained himself as not surprised at my feelings & regret that it should have happened, but that he thought no further change could be made. Took a Paddington stage into the city. Called at the courting homes & thence walked down to Mrs Carr's. Saw Boswell the Decgttonte and dined there. Spent the evening & returned by stage at night.

A most beautiful morning. Wind N by E. Remained in the house till after 1 o'clock expecting Boswell, but he did not come. Walked round the inner circle of the Regents Park & thence to Bob Marsh's & WBS & I afterwards walked up by Regents Street home to dinner. Found that Boswell had called after I had left home.

A most beautiful morning. Wind from the north. Wrote to Lord Beverley requesting him to present one to His Majesty at the Levee on Wednesday next & left the letter at his house. Thence walked down Regents Street. St James's Street round the park & there to Richmond's. Walked again up Regents Street & dined with Richmond at ½ past 5 o'clock

Another delightful autumnal morning. Wind north. Received a note from H Harry to say they called upon me this morning. A little after 1 o'clock, he, Miss G Hurry & Miss Fenwick called & we drove to the Zoological Gardens. Afterwards to the Coliseum with which we were much delighted & astonished & most particularly with the Swiss Cottage & arcade. Thence we drove to Walworth & I dined with them. Walked home in the evening where I found a note from Lord Beverley saying he will have much pleasure in presenting me to His Majesty on Wednesday next.

A fine morning. Slept in the house all the morning. Richmond called at 3 o'clock & drove me out in his gig. Went round by Highgate & Hampstead & returned by Regent & Hyde Park Home to dinner. Bob marsh also dined with us.
Another fine morning. Rather cloudy. Wind SW. Expected Boswell up but he did not come until after I had started for the city. Went ...

... to the office. Received a short letter from Bess, very angry for not writing to her. Called at Harman's about the Hope's Wyburn bill which has been lagging at the docks agent for my acceptance. Wrote to Robert Stephenson to send it up. Called at J Chapman. Took a cab & drove direct to St James. Called at the Lord Chamberlains office. Saw Mr Master who was very polite & introduced me as to how I am to act at the Levee. Left a card with him. Walked home & wrote to Bess blowing her up for her saucy letter. Dined at home

A very fine autumnal morning. Wind WNW. Been a little rain in the night. Took an omnibus into the city. At the offices. Called upon Messrs Harman's statement they had sent the Hope's Wyburn bill to Shields for above. Walked down to Miss Carr. Boswell gone down to Maldon this morning to the ship, which it appears, arrived there a fortnight ago, but he had not heard of it. Returned to the office & WBS & I walked out of the city together. Called at Bob Marsh's who afterwards joined is in Regents Street & went to Nottingham Place to dinner

A rainy morning. Wind SSW very unfortunate, having to go to the Levee but hope it will clear up. WBS returned from the city at 1 o'clock. When I dressed myself in full fig & drove in a hackney coach to St James Palace & was presented to the King. The Levee was not numerously attended, being nearly all naval & military ...

... decorated with all their orders, it was a very splendid & magnificent sight. I thought I should have been very nervous, but was not at all so. I was nominally presented by the Earl of Beverley, but in fact by the Lord in waiting who was I believe was Lord ____ Earl of Gosford I had the honour of kissing the Kings hand. Lord Beverley found me out in the ante room & was particularly polite & attentive. After leaving the Levee, WBS & Bob Marsh were waiting for me & we walked along Pall Mall & I got a coach & drove home where I exchanged my dress & returned to Richmond where I dined

A beautiful and hot summers day. Received two letters from Mrs & Miss Scott. The sale commenced & good prices said to be obtained. Mr Vernon with his unreal kindness & consideration asked a party to dine with us consisting of the two Careys, E Butler, Fishebourne, O'Connor & Captain Ballesby. Spent a pleasant day.

A fine morning. Wind NW. After breakfast WBS & I went into the city & at 11 o'clock embarked on board the Brocklebank steamer with an immense crowd of people & preceded to Woolwich to see the HMS Thunderer 74 a round ship launched. An immense concourse of people present. The King & Queen arrived about 2 o'clock & soon afterwards the Thunderer slid into the river in most beautiful style, the best launch I ever saw. Afterwards it was a grand & imposing sight. Returned to town & dined at the Blue Ports at 6 o'clock

A beautiful morning. Wind about W by S. After breakfast walked into the city. At the office, received a letter from Bess B & one from Rob Stephenson by mistake, instead of Stephenson, Wyburn bill enclosing the merchant's bill and notes for the freight.
