Paid Kitchenmein for repairing fishing rods £1.0.6.

Met H Harry & walked with him down to the Catherine docks to see Hy Nicholson who we found on board & had a lunch with him. His ship out exupting lathwood. He expects to get away about Wednesday & offered me a passage which I think I shall accept. Saw Messrs Harrison & explained Rolt's mistake in sending the freight bill instead of the Wyburn bill. Wrote to Bess. Walked back to Nottingham Place to dinner. Met WBS & Bob Marsh in Regent Street. The latter dined with us.

Another fine morning. Wind WSW. Hy Harry called upon me about 12 o'clock. After lunch we went to the Baker Street Bazaar to look for a gig for Sadler, but did not purchase. Got into a cab in Oxford Street & drove to the Pantechnicon in Belgrave square, a very splendid large building lately erected for the sale of Carriages etc. etc. An immense number of vehicles of all sorts. One of which a new dennilt we brought for Sadler for £30, a very cheap bargain all that it will want will be two or three coats of varnish in a few months. Returned to Nottingham Place to dinner. H Harry left us a little after 8 o'clock in an omnibus.

I took suddenly unwell & at bed time took a couple of camomile pills.

A continuance of beautiful weather. Wind SW. Swallowed a black draught before breakfast which, with the pills, have had the desired effect.

Did not move out until near 3 o'clock. Then took a walk to the Zoological Gardens & thence to Hyde Park & home to dinner, where I found Richmond had come to feed with us

A dull morning having been a little rain. Wind difficult to make out, appears to have got from the east. Took an omnibus to the city. Called at the office. The Hope sailed from Shields on Friday. Walked down to Whitechapel to Stirling's the chemists for a bottle of the essence of cubebs. Thence to the St Catherine docks & dined with H Nicholson on board the Crises, Henry & Sam Hurry there. Left the docks at 6 o'clock & walked to Nottingham Place.

WBS received letter from Colonel Farwole

A dull damp morning. Wind SE. Did not go out till late. Walked down by Regents Street & called at Richmond's, thence to the Temple & left my card at wwards chainpers,. Returned to Regent Street at 6 o'clock with Richmond. G Taylor, Bob Marsh, WBS & self there

Been some rain this morning. Rather dull & excessively close & sultry. Wind for the ESE. Took an omnibus into the city. Called at the office. Accepted Stephenson's Wynberg bill for £44.5/- due 8 Nov payable with WBS & left it at Messrs Halmgons. Went down to the St Catherine dock & dined on board the Crisis. Tea at Lodlins. A heavy fall of rain with lightning at night.

A fine morning & cooler weather after heavy rain last night. Wind SE. Sat in the house until after 1 o'clock. Called & had a lunch at Miles Forsters offices in Wimpole Street & sat some time with him. Walked in Regent Street till dinner time. Richmond dined with us
A fine day. The sale still going on. Wrote to Mr I Robert about a chain cable for the Hope. Dined early. John & I took a long walk to fish but had no sport

The early part of the morning dull & thick, afterwards cleared away & turned out a fine day. Wind SSE. Got all my luggage into a Hackney coach & down to Philpot lane (there saw Stephenson, the Hope being at Greenwich got up to stone stairs) down on St Catherine dock & the Crises having got out, I proceeded & left all my luggage at Lodlings. Walked up again to Phillpotts Lane, accompanied WBS to Guildhall and having got a Beef Steak at Jewps on WBS, Lee & I walked down to Mr Carr's & drank tea. Called at Codlings & saw H Nicholson who had got the ship down to Duke Shore & expecting to get away in the morning. I determined to accept Mr Carr's offer of a bed. Set WBS part of the way up the Commercial Road. Returned with Nicholson to Lodlings & got to Mr Carr's a little after 10 o'clock. Rained very heavy with a great deal of lightning. Part of the Hope sold today.

A fine morning after a very heavy fall of rain during the night. Wind SSW. Afterwards changeable between N & S by E. After breakfast went to Codlings, Stephenson met me there & we got all my luggage on board the Crisis & about 12 o'clock having got all her ballast in, she weighed anchor & dropped down to Greenwich where we were enabled to sail down the reach & we got to Woolwich between 2 & 3 o'clock. The tide here low we took the ground & there remained until 10 o'clock at which time I had gone to bed but the ship got under way & beat down to earth & brought up between 1 & 2 o'clock in the morning

At anchor off Erith. A cloudy morning with showers. Wind fresh from SSW after washing the decks & trimming ballast, the ship having been by the stern, we got under way at about 11 o'clock & beat down to the home light where we brought up at 6 o'clock. The wind having changed during the day to S by W: S: & S by E blowing fresh. Turned after a glass of grog between 8 & 9 o'clock

Turned the hands up about 5 o'clock being low water & the wind at SSW I got up before 6 o'clock. The people busy getting the anchor & setting sails. Had a fine run during the day down swin, studding sails set but not much wind which varied between SE & S by W. At ½ past 8 o'clock at night off Aldeburgh & beautiful clear weather but a strong flood tide against us. Turned in about 9 o'clock

Turned out at 12 o'clock am. The ship then running with a fresh breeze at SW for the Newrope light which we passed about 1 o'clock & ran through Hasbrough Gateway. Turned into my crib again before 2 o'clock I awoke or rather disturbed at 5 o'clock by a tremendous squall at SW a little to the south w of Cromer with heavy rise. It took us suddenly & without any warning & therefore with all sails standing that they had great difficulty in taking them in. However they succeeded at last in taking them without losing anything, which considering the violence of the squall was fortunate. When they had double reefed the topsails & made all snug I again went to bed. Got up at 8 o'clock still blowing hard from the WSW. We were then abreast of the Dadgrow floating light. It continued to blow fresh all the morning varying between WSW & W by N. After dinner Nicholson & I turned in & had a good snooze until ½ past 4 o'clock where we found Flamborough in sight distant probably about 15 miles. Wind & sea very much fallen, but still a fine light breeze from about WSW. All reefs out, top gallant sails set & fore topmast studding sails set. Passed Flamborough Head at 8 o'clock, a most beautiful night. At 9 o'clock we had a glass of grog & I afterwards walked the deck with Nicholson till 12 o'clock when we turned in.

We were disturbed again this morning at about 3 o'clock by a heavy squall with rain from the SSW which increased. I & Nicholson immediately turned out, the ship being off the Tees by the time we got upon deck, they had got the top sail & missen stowed & top sail reefed, lay the ship too soon afterwards left with the head to the land, between Seaham & Hartlepool, the squall gradually subsided & at day light 5 o'clock fine weather again. Ran the ship in for the land & between 7 & 8 o'clock got a piolet on board. Lay off the harbour until the tide flowed sufficiently for us to run the bar, which we did at 11 o'clock, working up to the narrows & then dropping up to the Lenickeln shore where I landed & came home. Robert got my things on shore.

I dined with J Tinley & in the evening called & saw Bess, got home before 11 o'clock

A damp morning having been a great deal of rain at an early hour, blowing fresh at SSW. Paid Robert. Borrowed of him £3 for child 8 weeks £1.16 & settled his book in passages etc. £3.5.3

Dined at the Northumberland Alms being the Dukes court day, the cooks on recorder of Newcastle proceeded there for the first time. At the nefs room ...

A fine morning but still blowing hard from the SSW. Several light ships got down & must have had a good run. Lockwood & I walked round by Tynemouth. H Nicholson & Mark dined with me at 3 o'clock. In the evening attended Aldertons Committee room & afterwards with Bess

A very fine morning. Wind SW & still looks like more rain. Walked to Preston to see Moor's brother who had not come down. Dined on board the Crisis with A Nicholson. In the evening we walked to Tynemouth at night with Bess

A continuance of fine weather. Wind during the day varying between SE & SE. At church in the morning. Saw Mr Spencer yesterday who agreed to renew our bill upon our rubbing off £100 or £150. Wrote to WBS. Dined at home. Walked to Tynemouth in the afternoon. Called at Cunningham's Dr Drury there & had some excellent glenlivet with them. Called afterwards at the castle, sat with the Marines & at night again with Bess
Rather a dull morning. Vernon & I left Carlow by coach. Found it afterwards extremely hot & dusty. Got to Dublin at 5 o'clock & dined with Sir C Vernon. Put up at Mackens Hotel

A letter from WBS

A mild morning. Wind SW. A party of us went to Cullercoat Sands & found ourselves at Rifle & Pistol shooting at a target. Lunched at the castle & at 4 o'clock dined with J Redhead & Lockwood at the lodgings. I sent them a pair of soles. At night with Bess

This days papers brought an account of the Reform Bill being thrown out of the Lords by a majority of 41. The debate did not conclude till ½ past 6 in the morning. Much excitement in London.

A rainy afternoon & night
A beautiful morning. Wind W by S. Dined with H Nicholson on board the Crisis. J Wight, J Redhead & Lockwood there. With Bess at night

Fine weather. Wind WSW. Went up in a gig to Newcastle. Called & saw Emma Galbraith who was looking well. Payed Mrs Noakes for Emma G's board and education up to June £39.10/-. Afterwards walked out to Benton where I dined & stayed all night. Dixon Clark there, he slept in Newcastle to take the coach in the morning for Oxford. Tom Smith left them in the morning for Togston

Beautiful mild weather. Wind in the morning SW. Changed in the afternoon to SSE. Left Benton directly after breakfast & walked out to Newcastle to meet Stephenson who arrived yesterday, fixed the hope to load Bell & Dixons Walls, but won't get coals for upwards of a fortnight. Took the steamer to Shields.

Found a letter from WBS with the Hopes freight account but no note, brokers commission being changed which WBS thought an error. Paid an average Eligible Club £14.9.3 & gave Stephenson £20 to pay wages. Dined at home at 5 o'clock. At the whist club in the evening & with Bess at night. A rainy & blowing night

A fine morning but blowing hard from the SW. Gave Robert a draft on executors account for ½ years taxes £9.5.2. Paid £20 in executors account from my own. Money advanced me by WBS. Walked out & called on Mr Robson. High Cheston. Dined at home at 5 o'clock & with Bess at night.

Fine weather. Wind SW. Afterwards WNW. Went to Newcastle by steamer, called at Chapmans about their £300 bill which they had negotiated upwards of a month ago. Returned by steam. Wrote to WBS. Dined with H Nicholson & with Bess at night

Fine weather. Wind W by N. After a breakfast walked to Tynemouth. Called upon & lunched with William Laidlers. Lounged about the Castle Yard all the afternoon. Dined with J Readhead & Lockwood & with Bess at night
A dull morning blowing fresh at WNW. Went across the water to Shortridge's Glass works to order some claret glasses for Mr Lee according to patterns
A most beautiful morning. Wind WNW. Went again to South Shields & ordered 2 dozen claret glasses. Played at billiards. Made up the Hope's Wyburg voyage. Dined at home & with Bess at night.

A very fair morning. Wind from SW. Got up early & took Dunn's gig to Newcastle. Took a place in the Alnwick coach at 10 o'clock. Got there before 3 o'clock where most of the officers who intended dining at the mess had arrived. Sat down to dinner at 6 o'clock. Spent a very pleasant & jovial evening & kept it up until 4 o'clock in the morning.

A dull morning but turned out exceptionally hot. Called upon Messrs Ryan & Parkinson respecting Nuvn Fitzmaurice bond who said they were wise endeavouring to raise money to pay off all his debts. To my great surprise I met Char Hurry who I found had been residing in Dublin for 18 months. Dined at Mackens. Went today to see the Rotunda

Did not rain till late. A fine morning. A fine morning. Walked about Alnwick. Left my card at Sir D Smith's. The Jefson held the day. The heapesteutes dined together. I dined with William Forstes. A party there consisting of Chater MP, captain Forster & Justies Hodgson MP etc. They all in the evenings event to the Ball & I dressed in my uniform having no other cloths with me with the intention of going but finding at the door that all the officers, even those who had promised to be in uniform were in plain cloths. I returned to the Inn, had a glass of brandy & water & went to bed

A very fine morning. The air rather frosty. Wind NSW. Left Alnwick by the Wonder coach at 10 o'clock, got to Newcastle before 3 o'clock, took a Shields gig & got home in time to order dinner at 6 o'clock when Charles Redley came & stayed all night. I spoke to Colonel Colson yesterday respecting the second gazetteer stating that I still considered myself very unhandsomely treated. I showed him the Dukes letter but could get nothing out of him

A dull cloudy morning blowing hard from the SW.

Redley & I walked to the newsroom, thence to Preston where we parted, he going on to Hartley. Saw Moore & urged him to thrash & sell everything. Dined at 5 o'clock alone. Stephenson called & informed me the Eligible Committee had been on board surveyed the stores etc. & reported the ship complete. Had got the dung out, the ship upon the shore to look at & clean her bottom. Found her in good order, only a butts and or two wanting caulking.

With Bess in the evening

A dull morning with showers & SW wind. Did not go to church. At the newsroom all the morning. Dined at ½ past 6 o'clock. Ed Chesterton dined with me. Lockerwood came in in the afternoon.

With Bess at night

Fine weather blowing fresh from the SW. Lockerwood & I walked up to Wallsend & breakfasted with Potts. The hounds after breakfast were taken out. Charlton offered me his horse but I declined it. Laid the hounds on a bag fox. Returned home. Dined with Readhead & at night with Bess

A dull morning. Heavy SW wind. Called at Chapman's & settled for WBS to take up the £300 note in London. They to give the executors account credit for £200 & take our note at 6 months for it. Wrote to WBS in answer to his letter received yesterday about it. Dined at home at 2 o'clock & Lockwood & I walked up afterwards to Billy Mill & took wine with Charlton.

At Bess in the evening

Got £5 of GH

A fine morning continues blowing hard from SW. Called upon Jobling at the George. Walked up to the ship, returned & rode up with Jobling in his cart to Tynemouth. He & his brother dined with me at 4 o'clock. In the evening at Mr Atkinson & with Bess
A beautiful morning. Wind SW. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. At the whist club & with Bess at night.

A beautiful morning. Wind SW. A great many ships sailed. The Hope came down below to load. Got some damage done by the painter. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined with Tom Jobling at Mrs Atkinson.

Quarrelled with Bess
Another beautiful morning. Wind SW. Took a long walk with Mark to Tynemouth, Cullercoat Sands & dined with Joblings at the George at 4 o'clock

Dined with Mrs Scott Went to the theatre in the evening. The bespeak of the Bachelors of North Shields for the benefit of Miss C Scsuton. A good house £59.16/-. Play The Haunted Tower with Registers Officer & High life below stairs, a very good company. Wind SSE. A heavy fall of snow, the latter part of the evening it thawed. Sea fallen

A beautiful morning. Called upon Mr Syms & Mr Grey, respecting the Athy property. But got no information. Mr Syms who was not at home. Went to the catholic association to hear O'Connell & others speak. Was disappointed. Dined with Char Hurry. Young O'Connel dined with us. A heavy fall of rain [in] the evening

A continuance of mild weather. Wind SW.

After breakfast took a walk to Tynemouth & went to church in the afternoon, again walked to Tynemouth. Jobling dined with me at 5 o'clock. Reconciled with Bess

A very fine morning. Wind West. After breakfast walked to Tynemouth & with others. Amused ourselves on Cullercoat Sands practicing ball firing. Dined at home at 5 o'clock.

Wrote to Mr Archer last night the owner of the planter to meet me at 11 o'clock on Tuesday morning to survey the damage.

With Bess at night.

A very fine morning blowing & has been all night hard from the SW. Ob board the Hope. Mr Archer did not come to survey the damage but sent a letter with an estimate, offering me £1.10 & the old boom etc. Walked up & saw him but did not agree, however afterwards determined to take it with an 18 inch plank.

Dined at home.

Rather a dull morning. Wind fresh from SW & little rain.

Sent Stephenson up to & he settled with Mr Archer. Received 30/0 & a deal plank. The ship got her beef on board. Sent WBS a round up. Walked up to Tynemouth. Saw Rifles march for Manchester. Dined at home at 5 o'clock. Lockerwood came in & took a glass of toddy with me.

With Bess in the evening

A damp morning having been showers in the night. Wind WNW.

On board the Hope. Her loading not completed by two keels, thereby prevented getting to sea. Walked to Tynemouth. The two keels came down in the afternoon. Lockerwood came & dined with me. At the whist club in the evening & with Bess at night

A fine morning. Been showers in the night. Wind NW

The Hope got to sea this morning's tide. Walked to Tynemouth and round by Whitley Park and called upon Mr J Wright. Dined with A Dale at 5 o'clock to meet the bridal party from Whitley park. With Bess at night

A cold damp morning. Went to Newcastle by steam. Signed the Hope's cargo bill £211.12.1 on WBS. Called at Angus about the carriage. Returned by steam. Dined with J Tinley & in the evening at the whist club & with Bess at night
Been showers in the night. A cold morning. Wind SW & S by W. Did not go church. Walked round by Tynemouth. Dined at home at 2 o'clock. Wrote to WBS. With Bess in the evening. A very wet night

A fine morning but all the appearance of more rain. Glass very low. Wind WSW. Blew in heavy squalls during the day with showers. Made the Hopes last or 3rd coal voyage up. Dined at home at 5 o'clock, drank a glass of toddy with Lockwood & at night with Bess

A fine autumnal morning. Fresh breeze from the NW & WNW. Walked to Tynemouth with Lockwood & afterwards to Preston. Dined at home & spent the evening at Bess.

Worse accounts from Sunderland, several new cases of cholera & deaths

A very foggy damp morning. Wind East. Got up early & went by the steam boat to Kingstown to see Tom Thompson on board the Royal Charlotte Yacht. He was much surprised too when I went on board. I spent the day & dined with him & returned to Dublin by steam in the evening. It turned out a fine afternoon

A beautiful morning. Air frosty & glass high. Wind NW.

Received a letter from Wilkinson & Angus saying they could not purchase the carriage.

Walked with Boswell to Tynemouth. Jobling arrived & agreed to stay with me. He dined with me at 2 o'clock. At the billiards room in the afternoon & with Bess at night.

Ordered 2 gallons of whiskey for one of which Jobling paid.

A raw damp & cold morning. Wind WSW. Two ships got upon the herd in coming into the harbour. Received a letter from Harry & G of Yarmouth informing me that the Hope had sprung a leak on Sunday night off Orford & got a boat with 14 men to assist in pumping & could scarcely keep her with both pumps going. They however had got her to Yarmouth close to the bar where they were lightening her to get her into the harbour. Laid the letter before the club who sent instructions to Messrs Hurry. I wrote to Stephenson & WBS & also sent a copy of the letter to the Hope Club at Newcastle.

Dined at 2 o'clock. At the whist club in the evening & suppered with Bess. Jobling with me

A fine morning. Wind NW.

The two ships got off the herd.

Received a letter from WBS with our note to Chapman for £200 dated the 9th Nov. Jobling left for Seghill. Tom Smith arrived from Togston. Dined at home.

A fine morning. Wind NW. Received a letter from Messrs Hurry & Co & Stephenson of the ship having struck upon the bar in going into Yarmouth. Wrote to them to deliver & sell the coals, get the leak stopped & return to Shields. Wrote also to WBS. Went across the water & saw Mr Potts who is to send me a copy of the Harmongs protest on Monday. Tom Smith & I dined at home at 5 o'clock & had the whist club in the evening. A pleasant party. Jobling returned late

A fine but cold morning blowing hard from the NW & NNW.

Tom Smith & I walked to Tynemouth & he afterwards drove up to Benton. Jobling & I dined at home at 4 o'clock.

At night with Bess

A cold raw damp morning. Frosty during the night. Wind W & W by S.

Gave Spencer our note for £200 at 6 months dated 9th Nov to be placed to the credit of the executors & paid £85 rents to their credit also Jobling & I dined at home at 2 o'clock. I refused an invitation to dinner at Mr Reeds. At the billiard

A fine frosty morning. Wind W by N. Received two letters, one from Hurry & Co, the other from Stephenson stating the ship to be still very leaky requiring 6 extra men to pumps. They had got her about ¼ of a mile up the way up to the quay. Laid the letters before the club. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home at 2 o'clock. At the billiard room in the afternoon & with Bess at night.

Received a letter from WBS

A comfortable winter's morning. Been a heavy fall of snow during the night. The country covered. Wind NNW. Thawing.

Dined at home. With Bess at night.

Sent Robert over the water to Mr Potts who let me have the Harmony Protest in the evening for which I paid £1.11-6

A sharp frost in the night having been a thaw yesterday. The streets this morning a sheet of ice & dangerous walking. Wind WNW. The clubs received a letter from Messrs Hurry's stating they had sold the remainder of the coals to be taken out of the ship in two days. Wrote to WBS & sent the Hairmongers protest with a copy of Chapman's book & an account of rents. Attended the whist club. Boswell came home with us in the evening to join us in a glass of toddy. Took physic

A fine frosty morning. Wind WNW. Having from cold I suppose, the back of my neck & head much affected & sore. I this morning took a black draught & lay in bed till 1 o'clock. Charles Redley called from Hartley. Dined & spent the afternoon with us. He left us at ¼ past 9 o'clock to walk back being a fine moonlight night. I went along & slept with Bess. Robert yesterday paid Philipson Mason his bill £37 & today paid into Chapman's £15 more rents

A beautiful day. Mr Vernon & I left Dublin at 9 o'clock & got to Carlow at 4 o'clock. Dined at home at 6 o'clock. Called upon Mr Price who informed me he had got about £150 by the sale of the furniture which is much more than I expected
A heavy fall of snow last night again. A complete thaw with sleet. Wind E by N. Paid average Eligible Club £12. Dined at home. At the billiard room in the afternoon & at night with Bess
A beautiful winter's morning. Hard frost & wind NW. At the newsroom in the morning. Dined at home at 2 o'clock. Spent the evening with Bess. Jobling there.

A thick damp morning having been rain with a SSE wind during the night. Wind now SW. Received a letter from WBS. Transferred from executors account at G's Ho to mine £150. Dined with Mr Tho Wright, Whitley Park, a pleasant day.

A mild day. Wind about west. Walked to Tynemouth with Boswell. Received a letter from Messrs Hurry & co. The coals being all out on Saturday & that they had found the leak to be in an open trennail hole between the timber under the starboard for chain about two feet below the light water mark. Had plugged it up & after heaving down & driving a new trennail, expected she would be able to return to Shields without the necessity of being docked at Yarmouth.

Dined at home. At the billiard room in the afternoon & with Bess at night.

Mild weather & fresh breezes from WNW. Wrote to WBS with a list of ships that sailed before & after the Hope. Dined at home. At the billiard room & at night at Bess's. Jobling, H Hurry & Boswell there.

A continuation of mild weather. Wind WSW. Received a letter from Stephenson of his having got the leak stopped. The ballast alongside & expecting to get away the next day. Gave a draft on Chapmans for £5 account for self. Dined with Mr Harrison the brewer at 3 o'clock. At the whist club & at night with Bess. Jobling went to South Shields

A very wet morning. Wind SW. gave a draft on Chapmans for £9.10 average Hope Club. Wind changed to SE. A great many ships got down. Dined at home. At the billiard room in the afternoon. With Bess at night. Lockwood there

Fine weather but cold and wind SE. A great many light ships arrived ravenjot this. The Hope from Yarmouth quite light. Went to Newcastle & fixed her to load Bell& Brown again to be loaded in 3 weeks,. Returned home to dinner. At the billiard room in the afternoon & attended the club. At night at Garthays

A fine morning. Rather cold & frosty. Wind SW. My head still being bad from cold, T this morning breakfasted in bed & got up at 12 o'clock. Went to church in the afternoon. Afterwards walked round by Tynemouth. Dined with Tinley at 5 o'clock, Jobley & Captain Cuthbert 15th there
A cold morning, rather frosty. Wind SW. Walked up to the ship. On board the Crisis. Dined at home. At the billiard room & in the evening at Mr Jarvis

A fine day. Called upon Mr Price in the morning, who gave me a list of the goods sold, with the prices & £90 on account. Had some conversation with Mr Walker with regard to administrating etc. Took a short walk with the boys & returned to dinner. Received a letter from William

Cold weather, rather frosty. Wind WNW.

Paid Beall apprentice in advance £1. Received a letter from Hurry & Co Yarmouth with their accounts & a bill for balance at 2 months for £59.9.

Walked with H Hurry & Richardson up to Sadlers & dined with him

A very wet unpleasant morning. Wind NW by W. Received a letter from WBS. Engaged mitcalf dock for the Hope. Walked up & gave orders to bring her down, hauled into the stream. Dined at home at 5 o'clock. Tinley, Gostling, Captain Cuthbert, H Dale & Jobling the party

A damp unpleasant morning. Wind WNW. The Hope got down to the dock gate. Took a walk & Tynemouth. Got the Hope into dock at 2 o'clock, high tide.

Dined at Home. At billiard room & in the evening attended the whist club

Thick cold weather wind WNW. The committee of the Eligible & Mr Whcatley as a member of the Hope Club committee, went on board the Hope & surveyed her & found her much strained & they readily agreed to give her a caulking, if I were willing to accept it & not strip her etc. two warps a trwlinge & studding sail continued. Set the men on to work after dinner.

Wrote to Messrs Hurry & Co. of Yarmouth acknowledging the receipt of these accounts & vouchers.

Dined with a party at Gordons at Tynemouth Place at 5 o'clock

A very foggy unpleasant morning. Wind WNW. At the dock the men 21 busy caulking. Stephenson & the carpenter found the ship in good order & not at all broken. Wrote to WBS. Dined at home. At the billiard room. Called to see Bess & at night at the club at Drury
A very foggy morning. Afterwards cleared away & turned out fine. Wind W by N. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home at 2 o'clock. H Harry came in after dinner & took wine with me & at night with Bess.
A fine morning. Wind SW. Walked to Tynemouth. Jobley, Boswell & H Harry dined with me on board the Hope. At Mr Atkinson's in the evening & with Bess at night.

A fine morning, after rain & blowing very heavy from WSW. Went to Newcastle by Dunns coach, called on bell & Brown to let them know when the Hope would be out of dock. Saw Emma Galbraith who was quite well. Returned to Shields by steam. At the ship. Dined with Dr Drury. At the billiard room in the afternoon & with Bess at night.

A very wet morning. Been a great deal of rain during the night & blowing hard from SSE. Delivered Hurry's account & vouchers onto the Eligible Club. Down at the ship, the caulking to be finished & ship out of dock in the evening. Dined at home. At the billiard room in the afternoon & with Bess at night

A fine morning. Wind W by S. Received a letter from WBS. Attended the Eligible Club, but the committee did not meet. The secretary halveoir told me they would advance me money on account. Left papers with them. Dined at Mr Reeds at 5 o'clock. A large party, went in the evening to the whist club & finished off at Mr Atkinson

A dull unpleasant day. Engaged the principle part of the morning with Mr Walker in reading over Bessy's marriage settlements etc. Paid Lamb £51 being the balance with interest of his bill of £100. Wrote to William asking him to act as sole guardian to the children
A fine morning after a great deal of rain during the night. Wind WSW. Dined at home. At the billiard room & at night at Bess

A raw cold morning. Wind from SW. Went by Dunns coach to Newcastle. At Bell & Browns ofein. The ship will get coals on Monday & be loaded on Wednesday. Saw Mr Anderson, Hope Club, to let him have the average papers on Tuesday. The committee having a meeting on Thursday to settle Hopes etc. Called & saw Emma Galbraith found her quite well. Returned to Shields by steam to dinner. At the billiard room & at night attended the whist club at H Harry's
A rainy morning. Wind South. Did not go to church. Dr Drury called. I called upon & sat some time with J Dale who has been extremely ill. Dined at 2 o'clock with Dr Drury. With Bess at night.

A rainy morning. Wind fresh from SE. Gave Stephenson a draft on Chapmans & Co for £30. Got the accounts & vouchers of Salvage etc. from Mr Stoke to give Mr Anderson of the Hope Club. Dined with Ben Wright.

A boisterous morning. Blowing hard from the W by S with showers. Went by steam to Newcastle. Two hours & a half in going up. Gave Mr Anderson all the papers for the Hope Club to settle the average. Returned by steam. Dr Drury, Mr C Wright & Ben Wright dined with me at ½ past 5 o'clock

A fine morning. Wind WNW & rather frosty. Being rather tired from last night's debauch, did not rise till near 12 o'clock. The Hope got her beef on board today, a quey takes of thoor. Dinner at home. At the billiard room in the afternoon & with Bess at night.

A fine morning & frosty. Wind WSW. Accepted a bill for balance of premium (182). Great Premium Clun £7.6.6 due 14 March. On board the Stokes, the remainder of her coals (4 keels) came down & she finished her loading. Dined at home. At the billiard room in the afternoon. The whist club in the evening. Called in at the widows at night & saw the Hope go to sea at 1 o'clock in the morning.

Wind WNW

A fine morning. Wind WSW. Paid the Hope's piolet £1.16 & to 3 men for getting the ship chain hawser which she was obliged to ship & leave behind & for placing it on shore 7/6.

Gave a draft on Chapman's & Co for self £5

Dined at home. Joblings brothers with us.

At the theatre & with Bess at night.

In the evening blew a gale at SSE

A cold morning, but fine weather. A fresh breeze from WSW & SW. Went by steam to Newcastle. Signed the Hope's cargo bill £216.10.6 at 60 days from the 14 Dec.

Saw Dixon Dixon. Returned by steam. Wrote to WBS. Lockwood dined with me at ½ past 5 o'clock. At the whist club with me at Ben Wrights
A fine morning. Wind SW. Engaged most of the morning in the house writing. Dined at home at 2 o'clock. Jobling stayed confined to his room. At the Doctor's in the afternoon & with Bess at night.
A fine summer day. Engaged writing all morning. Took a walk with Mr Vernon. Returned home to dinner. The two Careys dined with us

Fine weather. Wind from the WSW. Paid Hadawary Roper for a twice laid warp 82 fathoms at 28/- £7. Walked early out to Murton to see the Wallsend Harriers. Had but poor sport. Dined at 3 o'clock with Charlton at Billy Mill. Sat down 12 or 14 to an excellent col round of beef & roast potatoes, drank a great deal of wine, had a quarrel with Craig who behaved like a blackguard. Got to Bess at night.

Paid Red's Mother balance of ¼ years wages £2.9.3

Found myself at Bess's this morning. Where I remained all day. Went home a little after 5 o'clock. Showed myself at the newsroom. Had two glasses of toddy with H Harry & Charlton at the Albion & returned in the evening to Bess's
A fine morning after rain. Wind about west. Walked to Tynemouth & back to dinner at 2 o'clock. Jobling got down today. At the billiard room in the afternoon & with Bess at night.

A raw damp morning. Wind South. At the news & billiard rooms. Dined with J Tinley at 6 o'clock to meet Colonel Creagh, an officer sent down by government to establish Boards of Health & the precautions against the cholera. Captain Lenthbest & Gosling there

A fine morning. The wind at last got to the NW. the warps & towlines of the Hope were sold yesterday. Dined at home. At the billiard room. In the evening took wine with ben Wright. Went to the theatre & afterwards with Bess.

A fine morning. Wind WSW. Sent J Anderson of the Hope Club an account of the voyage made by the Hope from the 10th May to 20th Dec. Received last night from WBS from India silk pocket handkerchief.

Dined at home. At the billiard room.

Saw Bess. Spent the evening at the Albion & the windows
Xmas Day. A very fine morning. Wind SW. Walked up to Benton & spent the day at Dixon Dixon's

A foggy damp morning. Wind NNS. Walked into Newcastle with D Dixon. Called at the Hope office & came down to Shields by steam. Dined at the George with the Joblings & at the theatre & with Bess at night

A fine morning. Wind NW.

Variously employed during the day. Dined with Lockwood at 6 o'clock. Called at Bess's & went to the Ball in the evening. Not numerously attended. Did not get home till 6 o'clock in the morning.
Did not get up until 2 o'clock. Dined & went along to the billiard room. With Bess at night.

A fine day. Wrote to Mr Digan about the house in Dublin Street that I could give him no decisive answer. Hired a car & drove up the mountain & saw H Fitzmaurice about the bonds, who promised as soon as he could raise money upon his estates to pay them & that on Sunday sennight he would give me some money on account of the interest, perhaps sooner. Returned to Mr Vernon to dinner

A fine morning. Wind NW. Went up to the new quay with Drury. Afterwards walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. At the billiard room in the afternoon. Attended the whist club in the evening. Called at Bess's but slept at home.
A damp morning. Wind N by W. Been a great deal of rain in the night. Dined at home. At the billiard room & with Bess at night. Charlton dined with us
A fine morning. Wrote to WBS. Dined at home. At the billiard room. Spent the evening with Bess. Boswell & Nicholson there.

Highlights

1832-01-05 JRS is free from disease!!!

Note

The following note appears at the front of the diary which appears to be a bet on a result in the 1832 General election

2/1 This Mr Bell is returned for the southern Division of the county the next election

A Richmond, Bank

Mr Webster bets him the same

 

5/5 This Mr Bell is returned for the southern Division of the county

A C Wright

 

Nov 1832

Mr Richmond has has half his bet

An exceedingly fine frosty day with a SW wind. Gave Robert leave to go & spend the day at Benton. Went to church. Dined at home with Jobling. Had junior R. Maxwell along to see him. A fine boy.

H Harry came in & spent the afternoon with us in the evening. We went to window Atkinson & at night I was with Bess.

An exceedingly fine frosty day with a SW wind. Gave Robert leave to go & spend the day at Benton. Went to church. Dined at home with Jobling. Had junior R. Maxwell along to see him. A fine boy.

H Harry came in & spent the afternoon with us in the evening. We went to window Atkinson & at night I was with Bess.
A fine frosty morning. Wind SW. A holyday in the town. Walked to Tynemouth etc. Dined at home. At the billiard room. At night at the Albion & theatre. A very good house

A cold damp morning. Wind ESE. A good deal of rain & sleet. Wrote to WBS & remitted him two promise notes £142.15.6 & £71.2.2 to take up the Hopes cargo bill of £211.12/-. Gave a draft on Chapmans for the amount of the bills. Dined at home. At the billiard room in the afternoon & suppered with Lockwood

Engaged to dine with Charlton at Billy Mill at 2 o'clock. Thick foggy morning & frosty. Wind WSW. Did not go to Charlton being unwell. Received from Eligible Club £____ in notes at 2 months date 30 December which with Hurry & Co's bill of £59.9 making £228.5/- I paid into Chapmans. Dined at home. Received an Brt Andersons acceptance at 2 months from 4. I am on account of average for £50. I am on account of average for £50

With Bess in the evening
A heavy fall of rain during the whole of the day. Had some conversation with Mr Walker respecting the administrating to the property. Dined at home.

A hard frost & foggy. Wind SSW but I should think from the east of sea. Wrote to Mr Anderson acknowledging the receipt of the £50 bill

Dined at home. At the billiard room in the evening attended the whist club, With Bess at night who had submitted to be examined by Dr Horsley who pronounced her quite well & therefore I must be free from disease

A fine winters morning. Wind from the S & E & hard frost.

Lunched at home. Dined at 6 o'clock with junior Redhead at Tynemouth.

With Bess at night

Paid the £50 bill into my account at Chapmans

A dull damp morning. Wind E by S & ESE. Been blowing very hard all night. Dined at home at 2 o'clock. Tibbs eat his dinner with us. At the billiard room in the afternoon. Called at Bess & attended the whist club at night at J Tinley's
Finer weather. Wind SE & heavy sea upon the bar. Having taken a couple of pills last night I did not go to church. Lockwood dined with us at 2 o'clock. Spent the evening at Bess
A dull damp morning. Wind SE & heavy sea. Did not get up till late. Lunched with the Doctor at the billiard room in the afternoon. W C Wright dined with us at ½ past 5 o'clock. With Bess at night.

A foggy morning. Wind W by N & WNW. At the News & billiard rooms. Jobling, B Wright, J Redhead & I went out in the street chariot & dined with W C Wright at Muston House. Walked home in the evening. With Bess who came out as far as Billy Mill to meet us
A damp morning. Wind WSW. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home at 2 o'clock. At the billiard room in the afternoon & spent the evening with Bess
A dull damp morning. Wind SSE. Dined at home at 2 o'clock. Jobling dined out. In the billiard room most of the day. At the south Kitchen. Attended the Whist Club & with Bess at night
Another cold and damp morning. Fresh breeze from the ESE. Dined at home. H Hurry, Boswell Elder & I took some punch together at the Albion & I suppered off oysters at Bess

A fine morning. A slight frost. Wind NNW. Went to N Castle by Steam. Called & saw Mr Armstrong for WBS & wrote to the latter not to sell the Hope. Saw Angers about the carriage, who can neither buy or sell. Returned by steam. Dined with Dr Drury. At the Billiard room. Attended the Whist Club at Tibbs. A fine moonlit night. With Bess
A beautiful day. Attended Divine Service both morning and evening at Carlow church Dined at Mr Jamesons
A very fine morning. Wind WSW. Glass as high as set fair. Walked up to Benton. Dined & stayed all night. Found them all well
A beautiful mild morning. Wind WNW. After breakfast walked down to Shields. At the Billiard room in the afternoon & with Bess at night
A fine morning. Rather thick. Wind WNW. Dined at home. At the billiard room in the afternoon & spent the evening at Lockwoods & suppered with J Redhead at Tynemouth
Beautiful weather. Wind from the west. Dined with Lockwood & spent the evening at Miss Alkinson
Exceedingly mild fine weather. Wind WSW. Took a walk to Tynemouth & Cullercoat Sands. Dined at home & went to the Whist Club in the evening

A beautiful morning & rather frosty. Wind SW. Started after breakfast with my gun & had a most delightful walk to Hartley by the coast. Jobling met me there in Wards gig. Charles Redley dined with us & I drove Bess home at night, leaving Jobbing there. Suppered at Lockwoods.

A continuation of most beautiful weather. Wind SW. Wrote to WBS & sent him copies of the rent & chapenaus book up to the end of the year. Dined at home. Drury & Lockwood took some dinner with me. Called at Bess & at night attended the Whist Club at H Hurries

The fine weather still continues. Rather frosty with SW wind. Read a letter from WBS. Took a walk round by Tynemouth & Cullercoats. Dined at home. H French looked in in the afternoon & at night with Bess

Beautiful weather. Wind SW & SSW. The Wallsend Harriers threw off at Tynemouth lodge H harry & I went out to see them. Found a hade in the plantation which they ran round by the dean & lost in Hoggs garden. Dined at home, Gostling lunched with us. At the billiard room in the afternoon & at night at the Albion & with Bess

Another fine morning. Wind SW. Went out to South Shields. Called and left a pamphlet for Mr Hartley. Attended the court at the George. Mr Carr of Newcastle convicted of a breach of the coal turn act & fined £5. Dined at home. At the billiard room in the afternoon & with Bess at night
An exceedingly wet & unpleasant day. Made up Mr Jamesons account by which it appears there is a balance of £50.9.3 due to him. Dined at home Mr O'Connor with us

Fine weather. Wind WSW. Took a most delightful walk with J Cunningham & Mr Boswell to Tynemouth along the sands to Cullercoats & saw the fishing boats come in well laden. Returned home to dinner. At the billiard room in the afternoon & spent the evening & suppered at the Albion. With Bess at night

Most delightful weather and frosty. Wind WNW. Dined at home. At the billiard room in the afternoon. In the evening a sudden change in the weather came on a very heavy fall of snow & sleet & a gale of wind from the N & E. Attended the whist club. Called at Bess but slept at home

A fine winters morning. Frosty with showers of snow. Wind abated & now from N by W & heavy sea upon the bar. Paid Mrs Brown £6.1. by draft on Chapmans. Dined at home. Took wine with H French & a party at the Albion & went to the Theatre. In the evening with Bess

A fine morning. Wind WNW. Received the Hope's average papers from the Hope Club with the statement in very angust one, not having allowed one the caulking to £12.4.10. Dined at home. At Bess in the evening & afterwards at the Whist Club at Mr Fenwicks, Northumberland Square
A fine morning. Rather frosty. Wind NW. Took a walk round by Tynemouth, the Sands & Cullercoat. Mr Evington & Lockwood dined with us and in the evening we went to Bess.

A fine morning. A little frost in the air. Wind WSW. Walked up to Me Edwards dock to see Mr Evington & the Alexander. Returned home to dinner. At the billiard room in the afternoon. Spent the evening & suppered with J H Richardson, a pleasant evening

Beautiful weather wind WSW. Took a walk to Tynemouth. Dined at home. Wine with Boswell. At the billiard room in the afternoon. Called at Bess & left Jobling & Boswell there. Attended the assembly at the George at night. A very good one. 70 persons there
Rather a dull morning. Wind SW. Took a walk round by Tynemouth. Dined at home. At the billiard room in the afternoon & at night with Bess

A fine morning. Rather frosty. Wind SW. Wrote to the secretary of the Hope Club about the caulking requesting the committee to give it to me. Called at Bess. Attended the whist club & spent the evening at J Tenlies
A fine morning. Blowing fresh at W by N. Went by Drew's coach to Newcastle. Attended the Hope Club annual meeting & dined. Returned to Shields at night in a gig with Mr Harrison. At Bess'

A foggy unpleasant day & the thaw continuing, excessively wet and sloppy Received a letter from Dixon stating the impossibility of his assisting me (Promises much easier made than kept). Wind W&SW. Sea fallen & ship & sailed

A fine day. Settled with Mr Price for the sale of the furniture & after paying his charges & received from him a bill on Mr Conolly for £18.17.6 at 2 Nov, payable at no 1 Upper Orsmond Quay Dublin & £13.5.8 cash for balance. Dined at the Careys. Met Captain DeLacy & Mr Nugent of the 30th & went to a pleasant dinner at E Butlins in the evening & kept up until after 2 o'clock in the morning

Fine weather. Wind WSW blowing fresh. Wrote to WBS with a copy of the Harrisons policy got from Mr Car yesterday. Dined at home. Had some punch at the Albion with Richardson, French, Nicholson on Boswell. Called at bess. Spent the evening at the Albion with the above party.
A fine morning. Blowing fresh at SW. Took a walk to Tynemouth. Dined at home. With Bess at night. Began to blow very hard from the SSE

Dined at the Albion at 3 o'clock. Dinner given to H French by the party. A dull morning. Blowing hard & has been all night. Nearly a gale from the SSE. Spent a very pleasant day at the theatre and the evening accepted J Tinley's bill for £39 at 4 months.
Dined with H J Metcalf at 5 o'clock. A fine morning. Wind NW. Walked round by Tynemouth & the fields home. Spent a very pleasant day at Metcalf's

A fine morning. Wind SW at the news & billiard rooms. Dined at home. At the Billiard room again in the afternoon & with Bess at night. The Bachelors Bespeak at the theatre this night but I did not go, not approving of the farce
A fine morning after a good deal of rain in the night from NW. Dined at home. At the whist club in the evening & finished off with H French before he crossed the water for heck at the widows

Most beautiful weather. Wind NW. Took a long walk round by Tynemouth, the Sands & Cullercoats home by the fields to dinner. Being my birthday, H Hurry & Boswell came in & took wine with me. With Bess at night
A fine morning. The wind got roundto the SE. Received a letter from WBS. Dined at home at the billiard room in the afternoon at the whist club at J Duke's at night
A dull morning having been with a NE wind during the night. The wind now NNW & changed during the day frequently to SSE & E. Dined at home. With Bess at night.
A fine morning. Wind E by S & ESE. Attended the Eligible Club annual meeting & dined at the Commercial. At the theatre in the evening & afterwards called at the widows

A most delightful & beautiful day we have had this summer. Engaged the whole of the morning with Mr Turner in examining & taking down the particulars of the original & sub-leases. Dined at home quietly
A dull morning. Rather cold. Wind SW. Walked with H Hurry & Boswell to Tynemouth, Cullercoat & Whitley, home to dinner. At the billiard room in the afternoon & with Bess at night
A fine morning & frosty. Wind WSW. Dined at home. At the billiard room in the afternoon. The Albion in the evening & also with bess

Fine weather & Kean fresh wind SW. paid into Chapmans rents on account of executors: £30. Drew on my own account £5. Dined at home. At the billiard room in the afternoon. At the whist club in the evening & with Bess at night.

Beautiful weather. Rather frosty. Wind NW. Walked up to Jkcuth dock & dined on board the Crides with H Nicholson. At the theatre at night.

Got £43.10/ of Cs & co on executors account to pay E Galbraith's Buaisd & tomorrow

A fine morning & sharp frost. Wind WNW. Breakfasted with Tinley. John drove me up to Newcastle & back again to dinner with him at 5 o'clock. Charles Mallory came & attended the whist club at Goslings in the evening. With Bess at night.
A fine morning. Fresh breeze at SE. Went to church in the morning. Dined at home. Spent the afternoon at the Doctor's & the evening with Bess
Beautiful weather. Wind SSE. Walked up to the dock with Marks. Dined on board the nautilus with J Redhead & spent a pleasant day at the widows & with Bess in the evening
A foggy morning. Rather frosty. Wind about W by S. At the billiard room. Dined with J Tinley & a party & afterwards attended the ball at the George which was a very good one
A fine morning. Wind SW. Dined with Mr Harrison the brarier with a party. With Bess at night
Fine weather. Wind SW. Walked towards Tynemouth. Met Sadler & a party, returned with them & went up to the Point to dinner. Came down in the evening to the whist club. At home at night

A fine day. Received a letter from William & Mr Digan about the house. Answered this letter. Dined at Mr Coopers. Cooper Hill, met a party. Paid Drs Reed & Stone £5 each for their attendance upon my poor sister
Most beautiful weather. Rather frosty. Wind WSW. Went over the water, called at Mr H Wright with an average bill for £3.3.8 not at home. Dined at home & at Bess at night

Northumbrian Regimental dinner at the Turf at 6 o'clock. A fine morning. Been a shower of rain. Wind WNW. Went to Newcastle by steam. Dined at 6 o'clock. 23 officers at dinner & strangers. Mr Beerrall of Broom Park, D Dixon, I Cockson, Pollard, Lambert, Reed & Small. Spent a pleasant day & left the party before 1 o'clock in the morning. Some remained till 5 o'clock

A damp cold unpleasant morning. Wind SE. Slept at D. Dixon's all night. Attended a meeting of the officers to pay the dinner bill & exact fines. Took the steamer at ½ past 2 o'clock & returned to Shields at 5 o'clock to dinner. With Bess at night
A dull morning and cold. Wind SW. Dined at home. Paid a average bill Hope Club of £14.10/- & received one of £3.3.8. I spent the evening with Bess. Jobling & Boswell there

A thick foggy morning & frosty. Wind W by S. After breakfast, H Hurry, Boswell & I took the steamer to Newcastle, attended the court & heard the trial of the Liberty and plunter when the Club of North Shields got a verdict against the latter. We afterwards dined at the Turf with Mr Richmond & witnessed. I slept there all night.

Fine weather. After breakfast went down to the Towns Court & heard part of the trial in which H Wheatley was the defendant & a verdict was given against him. Walked about the town. Dined at the Turf & returned to Shields by the ½ past 5 o'clock boat. Spent the evening with Bess

A dull morning, having been rain in the night & appearance of more. Wind SW. Went over the water to see Mr Wheatley. Dined at home. At the billiard in the afternoon. Called at Bess & in the evening attended the Whist Club

A fine morning. Wind S by E, afterwards SW. Walked to Tynemouth round by Cullercoats, home to dinner at the billiard room in the afternoon. Called on Bess & went to the theatre in the evening. Slept Eastward

A dull morning and blowing fresh from the SW with rain during the day. Dined at home. Called at Bess' in consequence of what I had heard & the someward have of her innacsome. Went to the whist club at Tom Wrights in the evening, Wrote to WBS
A fine mild morning. Wind W by N variable during the day, got SW & SSE. Settled at SW blowing a gale with rain. Walked to Tynemouth in the morning. Dined at home. With Bess at night.

A fine day. Rather windy. Engaged writing the greater part of the morning. Dined at Mr Stones & met a larger party. Won at whist 18/- wrote to Ryan Parkinson respecting the debt of H Fitzmaurice estate & also a letter to Tom Tinley
A very fine morning. Wind N by W. Dined at home. In the afternoon with Mr Hearson & H Hurry at Harrison. Stopped at the Doctor's & finished off with Bess
A stormy morning blowing hard from SW with showers. Very tired & breakfasted in bed. Got up at 1 o'clock. Dined at home at 5 o'clock. Went to a dance at Miss N Fenwick. A pleasant evening

A fine morning. Wind W by S. Got two average bills returned for non-payment. Two on Mr Richmond = £3 & one on Mr Spence Newcastle for £1.4. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. W C Wright came & drank a bottle of wine with me, a bet. Spent the evening with Bess
A fine morning rather frosty. Wind NW. paid Beal's mother ¼ years wages £6.8.9. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at town at Harrison's. Called at Bess & in the evening at the whist club.
A beautiful morning & frosty. Wind NW. Walked round by Cullercoats & Tynemouth. Dined at home. At the billiard room in the afternoon & with Bess at night

A continuance of fine weather. Wind variable between NW & SW. Got up early & went to Newcastle. Received £1.4. of Mr Spencer, Hope's average. Returned to Shields to dinner but obliged by a letter from WBS to start for Newcastle again to see K Bend. Got the bills returned to Shields & sent them off by post to WBS. At the whist club at Doctor Drewy's
Beautiful weather. Wind WSW. Leadbottom attacked by the cholera. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at 2 o'clock with Doctor Drewry. Leadbottom doing very well in the evening. Slept with Bess.
A fine day. Wind about S or S by E. Remained with Bess all day. Jobling came to dinner. Got home & went to bed before 9 o'clock

A beautiful spring morning. Wind SW. Leadbottom going on favourably, was down stairs last night. Determined not to dine with J Tindley or go to the Ball in consequence of the cholera. Dined at home. At Harrison's after & with Bess in the evening

A fine morning. Wind WSW. Attended two meetings at the library. One to fix upon a returning officer under the new reform bill, the other to partition the Duke to appoint two resident magistrates. Dined at home. At Harrison's in the afternoon & with Bess at night.

Received a letter from WBS
A pleasant day. Engaged in the morning writing. Took a walk with the boys. Dined at home. My Jameson with us
A fine morning. Wind NNE. Wrote to WBS. Dined at home. At the billiard room in the afternoon. Attended the whist club in the evening & with Bess at night

A continuance of fine weather. Wind WSW. Dined at home. Went to the theatre in the evening being the last night & Mr Beverley's benefit, a good house. They performed Masanvill's uncommonly well & the scenery was beautiful
A fine morning, been a little rain in the night, blowing hard from the WNW. Dined at home. At Harrison's in the afternoon & at the widows at night.
A fine morning, blowing hard from NW. Walked to Tynemouth & round by the fields. Lunched at Home with Jobbling. At church in the afternoon. Dined with J Tinley & at night with Bess.

Showery and blowing hard from the NW. paid E Reads mother ¼ years wages £2.7.3. Dined at home. At Harrisons in the afternoon & with bess at night.

Waed declined giving more than £60 for the George
A fine morning, blowing fresh from the NW. Dined at home. At Harrisons in the afternoon & in the evening H Hurry & Nicholson went with me to Bess

A fine morning blowing hard from the NW & W. Beeing the fast day I went to church twice & heard excellent sermons from the curate & Mr Mark, never saw the church so full. W C Wright dined with me at 5 o'clock. H Hurry came & took wine with Bess at night

A fine morning & still blowing hard from the W by N. H Hurry & I walked to Tynemouth castle yard. Wrote to WBS. Dined with Rudyard of the 15th regiment at 5 o'clock & he accompanied me to the clerk in the evening. Called at Bess
A fine mild morning. Wind W by N. Walked to Tynemouth Castle. Dined at home. At Harrisons in the afternoon & with Bess in the evening.
A cold morning. Wind NW & NNW blowing fresh with snow. Got round to the N by E & NE blowing a gale of wind. Dined at home. At the whist club at night at Ben Wrights

A fine morning. Received letter from William & Ryan & Parkinson that H Fitzmaurice estates were not sold, but that they were going to raise money upon them to pay off all debts. Did not go to church in the morning. Engaged in writing to William etc . Dined at Mr Jameson
A fine morning, blowing fresh from the NW. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. Called upon the Doctor in the afternoon & with Bess at night.
Beautiful weather again. Wind NW. Walked with H Hurry up to Edward's dock South Shields to see the Albiona & returned home to dinner. Walked up to Tynemouth in the afternoon. With Bess in the evening
A dull morning after rain. The wind got round to the ENE. Walked to Tynemouth with Mr Mark. Dined at home. At Harrisons in the afternoon & with Bess in the evening
A beautiful morning wind SW. A large fleet of ships arrived. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. At Harrisons in the afternoon & with Bess at night.
Beautiful weather. Wind NW. Walked round by Burdon main & Chirton. Dined at home. In the afternoon. Walked up to Saddlers with H Hurry. Attended the whist club & called at Bess

A fine morning. Wind SW

Dined at the Albion at 5 o'clock. The whist club dinner spent a very pleasant evening.

Beautiful weather. Wind S by W. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined with Doctor Drewry.

And at The whist club with me in the evening. Received a letter from Lockwood with a £5 note to pay for some small debts
A fine morning. Wind NW. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. With Bess at night.
A fine morning blowing very hard from the WSW. Received a letter with a note for £65.10/ from WBS. Dined at home. Wrote to WBS. In the house all afternoon & called at Bess in the evening
A beautiful morning. Wind variable. Dined with h Dale & went to the Fancy dress ball in the evening which was well attended. 137 there. A great many excellent characters. Suppered with Mr Weatherty's

A cloudy day with heavy showers of rain. Had some conversation with Mr Walker. Determined upon going to Dublin to administer to the amount of sale of furniture only & take out letters of guardianship. Received from Mr Cleer £1.11 for whisky & malting. Dined at home Finished my letter to William & put it into the post. Ordered a car to be with me at 7 o'clock in the morning if fine to go to Athy to see Mr Pope
Most beautiful weather. Did not get up till 12 o'clock. Walked round by Preston. Dined with Drury. At Bess at night.
Beautiful weather. Wind from the N & E. Walked to Cullercoats, Tynemouth & dined at home. At Harrisons in the afternoon. The Duke of York in the evening
A continuance of most beautiful weather. Wind from the NNE. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. On board the Crisis in the afternoon & with Bess at night. A thick fog set in

A rainy morning. Wind NE. The Hope got into the harbour at 10 o'clock am. Gave £15 draft to Stephenson. Paid into Chapmans the note for £15.10/-. Dined at home. At Harrisons in the afternoon & at the whist club at H Beeles in the evening.
A dull morning. Wind ESE. Went to church. Saddlers dined with us. H Hurry came in & took wine. At Bess in the evening

A dull cool morning. Wind ESE. Got up at 4 o'clock & went by the coach from South Shields to Stockton, got there at ½ past 9 o'clock. Walked to Middlesbrough & saw Mr Harris about fixing the Hope. He is to send me a charter. Returned by the 2 o'clock coach & got to North Shields at 8 o'clock. With Bess
A dull morning & cool wind ESE. Dined at home. At Harrisons
Cold weather & wind from the NE & SE. Went to Newcastle by steam & returned to dinner. Could not do anything for the Hope. With Bess in the evening

A cold morning. Wind NE. Mr Bird breakfasted with me & came back for dinner. I signed a charter for St Andrew & sent it to WBS.

Benton agricultural show. Dined with Charlton at Boggins. Did not go. Received a charter from the tees Co but refused it. At Bess
Another cold day. Wind ENE. Gully called & lunched. Drury & Charlton dined with me on board the Hope. Called at Harrisons. With Bess at night. Received a letter from WBS

Left Carlos at ½ past 7 o'clock in a car & went to Athy to breakfast in 1 ½ hours being 11 ½ miles. Saw Captain Pope respecting the property there, but could learn nothing satisfactory. He said it was a divided property. His father having 2/3 one of which he sold & the other 1/3 was the Galbraeths & to prove it was a divided property he said the Galbraiths had granted a lease of their part consisting of an old house now in ruins & a tanyard in the rear. He further said that the original lease had somehow or other got out of his hands, but that I could see it at Mr Warrens, Jarvis Street Dublin. That he would be glad to give me every information & assistance & allow me to see all papers that are in his possession. Returned to Carlow in the afternoon. Dined alone. Mr Vernon having gone to Coopers Hill & went to a pleasant quadrille party at Mrs Whilliam Fishbourn. We kept it up until 3 o'clock
A fine morning. Not quite cold. Wind E. Wrote to WBS. Dined at home. Spent the afternoon playing at gravitas with Bradshaw, also spent the evening there
Fine weather. Wind NE. Went to church. Dined at home. Went over the bar with H Nicholson who sailed from Copenhagen. At W Lawton's Tynemouth in the evening & with Bess at night.

A dull thick morning. Wind NNE. Received a letter from WBS advising me not to accept Birds charter. Wrote to Bird. Dined at home. On board the Choise in the afternoon & had some punch. With Bess at night
Beautiful weather. Wind from the WSW. Went to Newcastle by Dunn's coach but could do nothing for the Hope. Returned by steam. Landed at the point & dined with Sadler. With Bess

Fine weather but blowing very hard from the SSE. Went again to Newcastle but did nothing. Returned by steam. Authorised H Hurry to fix the Hope for Wyburg & Hull at 3.2.6. Dined at home. On board the Choice in the afternoon & with Bess. A large fleet arrived. Rain at night
A dull damp morning. Rained all night. Wind NW. Dined at home. At Tynemouth in the afternoon. At the Albion & eastward at night. The Choice sailed for Wyburg
A dull rainy morning blowing fresh from the SSW. Brought a bullock for the Hope off J Swan at 46/-. Dined at home. Called & sat with J Richardson in the evening. Afterwards with Bess
A beautiful morning. Wind WNW. Dined at home. Attended the whist club at N Fenwick
A fine spring day with a few showers. Wind SW. At church in the morning. Dr Drewry & I walked out to Preston & drank with W C Wright. With Bess at night

A dull morning. Blowing hard from the SW. Went by steam to Newcastle & fixed the Hope to take coals out to Swinemsend at £6.6 per keel. Returned home to dinner & afterwards went to Tynemouth races which were very bad. Turned out a wet day & spoiled the sport. At Bess at night

A very wet day. Quite a deluge of rain. Confined to the house all the morning by the wet. Engaged in covrtey for wrote a letter to Mr Buther of Athy. Asking to whom he pays rent for the tanyard. Dined at home with Mr Vernon

A rainy morning. Wind NNW. Went to Newcastle and returned home to dinner. Dr Drewry dined with me. Went to races in the afternoon. Pretty good sport for the cup which was won by Holroyd who entertained a large party at Smithson's. Spent a very pleasant evening. A deluge of rain
Been a deluge of rain all right & still continues without intermission. Wind NNE. Received a letter from WBS & answered it. Dined at home. At Bess at night.
Fine weather. Dined at home. H Hurry & I walked up to the Point & spent the afternoon with Saddler.
A fine morning. Went to Newcastle. Came home to dinner. At Harrisons in the afternoon & with Bess at night
A fine morning. Wind SW & variable during the day. Went to Newcastle. Dined with the Doctor. At Harrisons in the afternoon & with Bess at night
A fine morning. Wind SE. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. Took wine with H Hurry. Walked again to Tynemouth & called at Bess's in the evening

A fine morning. Wind E by N. Received a letter from WBS & answered it desiring him to fix the Hope at £3.7.6 Petersburg to London. Dined with Eligible Committee at the Commercial & in the evening with Bess. Tom Smith came
A fine morning. Wind NE. Walked twice to Tynemouth. The Hope went up to Heaton Spout. Dined at home . Tom Smith with us. At Bess in the evening.
A rainy morning. Wind SE. Went with T Smith by steam to Newcastle & afterwards in the carriage with Mrs Dixon to Benton to dinner & to stay all night
A very wet morning. Wind NNW. Walked from Benton to Heaton Spout. The Hope will only get 12 keels & to come to Shields at high water. Walked from there to Shields to dinner. With Bess at night
A wet day. Heavy showers Dined with Mr Vernon, the two Careys dined with us & Mr Moor. Spent a pleasant day. Agreed to let the house to Mr Dugan at £35 a year when appointed guardian
A fine morning. Wind ENE. The Hope got remainder of her coals. Dined at home. At Harrisons in the afternoon. Walked to Tynemouth in the evening & with Bess at night.
A cold morning. Wind SE. h Hurry, Cunningham & Charlton dined with me on board the Hope. With Bess at night
A Beautiful mild day. Wind SW. Went to church. Dined at home. Walked to Tynemouth in the afternoon. Called at Bess

A fine morning. A fresh breeze from the WSW. The Hope's charter & despatches came for Wyburg & Hull at 60/ for Wades Flo. Dined on board the Hope. She could not go to sea being too much swell on. Called upon Nelacd the baedegream

A beautiful morning. Wind NW. the Hope sailed with a fine breeze. During the day the wind got round to the N & N by E. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined with the Eligible Committee at the Commercial. Called at Bess at night
A fine morning. Blowing hard from the N by E with a heavy sea. On the bar. Dined with J H Richardson. With Bess at night

A fine morning. Still blowing hard from N by E & a heavy sea. Received a letter from WBS. Dined at home. Wrote to BBG (Benjamin Baker Galbraith) Went across the water with the Doctor. At the George and at night with Bess
A continuance of fine dry weather. Wind N by E. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. At Harrisons in the afternoon & with Bess in the evening

Cold weather & blowing hard at about N by W. Sea high. Dined at home. Walked in the afternoon with Charlton & Doctor Drewry to Billy Mill & had wine. Signed a bill to Chapmans for £150. At Bess at night.
A fine morning. Wind still from the N by E. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. At Tynemouth again in the afternoon. Took wine & spent the evening at Tibbs. Called at Bess

After a blowy and rainy night, on rising this morning, found the snow nearly dissolved. Wind E to ESE & very heavy sea upon the bar, a few ships arrived. Another disappointment! Received a letter from Sir D Smith stating the Dukes inability to comply with my request for a loan. Every person poor when you want assistance! Adversities the time for trying friendship, in prosperity you have professions enough. I've oft been told, but I have now ascertained it's a d-d selfish world we live in; every one for himself. ‘tis almost a crime to be liberal & kind hearted
Left Carlow for Dublin to take over letters of guardianship. A showery day. Got to Dublin at 5 o'clock

A fine morning with a cool NNW wind. Afterwards got to NNE. Went to the coach to Newcastle& got settled with the Hope Club and allowing a calking. Called and saw Emma Galbraith. Got home to dinner. With Bess at night.

Heavy shower of rain & hail
A dull cloudy morning but wind still from the NE. A heavy rain. Dined at the Doctor. Afterwards & in the evening had a crab supper at Mr Harrisons. With Bess at night

A beautiful morning, but still cool with a NNE wind. Walked round by the high end of the town to the Doctors garden, there to Tynemouth & home to dinner. At Harrisons in the afternoon & with Bess at night

A fine morning. Wind NE. J Cunningham breakfasted with me & we afterwards went to Sunderland to look at the Harmony. Returned home to dinner. The Reformers had a procession this evening. Received a letter from WBS. With Bess at night

A beautiful morning & much warmer. Having slept with Bess did not turn out till late. Took a walk to Tynemouth. Dined at home. At Harrisons. Walked to Joganodsout in the evening. At the Duke of York & called at Bess
A fine morning. Wind NE. Wrote to WBS. Dined at home. At Harrison's & the Doctors in the afternoon & with Bess at night
A beautiful morning. Wind SW & SE. Walked up to Benton & spent the day
A fine morning & warm. The first summers day we have had. Wind SW. Walked from Benton to Billy Mill & dined with Charlton. With Bess at night
A beautiful warm weather. Wind West. Walked to Newcastle. Dined at Harrisons at 3 o'clock. At Bess's at night. Drew £16 of Co & Co to pay Moy Mr B

A fine morning. Wind NE Walked to Tynemouth with Webb, Captain Potts & his son. Cleaned with and went across the water with him in the evening to his brother and drank tea. Finished off at the George & home

The first thing in the morning called upon Mr Carmichael but being engaged made an appointment with for 1 o'clock. Walked down to see the guard returned at the castle. Much to my surprise, met captain flu ie Butler. At 1 o'clock saw Mr Carmichael & then went to Mr Stocks the Proctor who filled up a form for the children to sign that they are willing. I should administer (in my opinion very inconsistent), sent it off by post to Mr Vernon. Dined at Mackens
A fine morning. Wind W by N. Walked to Tynemouth through the fields with Webb. Dined at home. At Harrisons in the afternoon & with Bess in the evening
Beautiful weather. Wind NNW. Engaged in the house writing. Dined at home. Paid average bills £80.1.10 into chapman's & drew out £10 for self. At Holroyds, Billy Mill in the evening. Came home.

A fine morning. Wind NNE. Went to Newcastle by steam. Called upon & took Emma Galbriath out to walk. Returned home by steam to dinner at 5 o'clock. Jobling went to Durham. Received a letter from WBS. With Bess at night
A beautiful morning. Wind E by N. Went to church. A chastity sermon for poor living in woman by her arraohing. Dined with H Hurry. Walked to Tynemouth with H hurry in the evening

A very heavy rain during the whole of the morning. Which kept us in the house. Dined at 2 o'clock. Went out to fish in the evening but could catch no fish, the rain having had no effect upon the river. Wind NE
Another rainy morning. Wind from the N & E & cold. Dined at 8 o'clock. Could not fish being so wet & the river flooded
Still wet damp weather. Rained in the morning. Wind NE. Dined at 2 o'clock. Went out after dinner & fished in the Pow Burn & caught several trout with worm.
A fine morning. Fished again with worm in the Burn & had good sport. Sent a basket of trout to Doctor Drewry. Dined with Mr Davison of Brandon White house
A dull morning. Wind NE. Started after breakfast & went up to Ingram to fish but had very poor sport. Drank tea with Mr Duncan there & got home about 10 o'clock
Still cool weather. Wind still prevailing from the NE. Very poor sport fishing. Only caught a few. Dined at 2 o'clock

A beautiful day. Went to see the guard relieved & afterwards attended morning service at the castle chapel. The interior very beautiful & chaunting good. Called upon Charles Hurry. Walked out & afterwards dined with Him
A fine morning. Wind NE. Walked out after breakfast to see Reeds hrrkeout at Grays. Davison & Duncan dined & spent the day with us.

Still cool damp weather. Wind SE. had two hours fishing before dinner, better sport. Dined at 2 o'clock & at ½ past 7 o'clock go upon. The Highflyer & came to Newcastle & thence by gig home. With Bess at night. Very wet and stormy
Rainy morning. Wind SE. Dined at home. At Harrisons & Doctor Drury's in the afternoon & with Bess at night

A fine morning. Wind SSE. Walked to Tynemouth & had a warm bath. Dined at home & in the afternoon went by water with H Hurry to Saddlers with whom we had a bottle of wine. Attended Ilderton Committee. With Bess at night

Fine summer weather & warm. Wind SW. Came afsed the low town until 11 o'clock & then went to Newcastle. Saw Emma Galbraith. Sold the carriage for £12. Got home to dinner a little after 4 o'clock. Wrote to WBS. At the committee Room. Also at Webb's & at night with Bess
A fine morning. Wind fresh from WSW. Continued the whole of the day. Dined at the George
A continuance of fine weather. Engaged cherussing all day. Tynemouth & Tenby, W Lenghall & Reed dined with me at 6 o'clock
A dull damp morning. Wind SE. Went to church. Walked Tynemouth. Ilderton dined with me. Walked to Tynemouth in the evening. Called at Bess

A beautiful morning. Wind ___. After breakfast Reid & I went by the steamer to Newcastle. Walked to the Racecourse. The running very bad. Dined at the stand. Walked back to Newcastle in the evening & returned to Shields by steam. With Bess

A rainy morning. Wind variable. Ceased raining during the day but very dull & close. Woke at 11 o'clock by steam to Newcastle. Walked to the course, better sport than yesterday. Returned in the evening by a gig. At Bess

A fine day & very warm. Engaged with Mr Carmichael & wrote to Mr Vernon for leases etc. Received the documents which I sent by post on Saturday for the children to sign. Dined at Mackens. Much fatigued with my days work. Received a letter from William

A very fine morning. Wind NE. Went up to Newcastle by steam & walked to the course. The racing better today. When there had a heavy thunder storm which made it very wet & uncomfortable. Returned by steam on the evening & had supper at home having had no dinner

A beautiful day. Went again to Newcastle by steam. Dined with Mr Dodds & afterwards walked to the course. Poor running. Both cups won easily. The GoO by Mary Cleveland & the silver by Captain Potts. Returned to Mr Dodds & got home by steam at 1 o'clock in the morning

A rainy day. Wind SE. A draft on Chapmans for Mr Mid £16 Pduct on Hope's bill for coal freight to Swenmundr £38.11.10 dated 5 June at 60 days.

Sanderson Ilderton MP came down. I dined with him at the George & he in this evening, addressed the electors.

With Bess
A fine morning. Blowing hard from the SW. Ilderton came down from Newcastle & we were engaged canvassing all the morning. Dined at the George tavern at 6 o'clock. Ilderton came home with me to sleep
A fine morning & blowing hard from the SW & NW. Went to church in the morning. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home at 5 o'clock

A fine morning but cloudy. Wind NW. Engaged canvassing the whole of the morning with Ilderton. Dined with him at the George at 6 o'clock.

Suppered at Barkers.

With Bess
Delightful weather. Engaged all day in canvassing Tynemouth, Cullercoats etc for Mr Ilderton. Dined at home at 6 o'clock. Spent the evening at Mr Barkers

Beautiful weather. Very warm. Went over the water & attended Mr Fairles funeral which was followed by a long procession of gentlemen from all parts. I canvassed for Mr Bell. Dined at 4 o'clock & with Bess at night

Murder of a Senior Magistrate

The funeral of one of South Shields' senior Magistrates, Nicholas Fairles Esq, took place at St Hilda's Church on Wednesday 27th June, 1832. He was well respected within the town and also within the church community and so the mourners, led by his wife, included many of the town's dignitaries.

There was a strike at a local coal mine and, as its owners were expecting further trouble, Mr Fairles had been in attendance. From the mine he set out to visit Mr J A Foster, a viewer who worked at Jarrow Colliery, but on his way across Jarrow Slake he was stopped by William Jobling, who was quite intoxicated. Jobling took hold of the reins of Mr Fairles's horse and begged for money for more drink, which of course was refused by Mr Fairles. Jobling was then joined by Ralph Armstrong who also worked at Jarrow Colliery.

Whilst Jobling retained his hold on the reins of the horse, Ralph Armstrong struck Mr Fairles on the head with a heavy stick, knocking him from his horse to the ground, whereupon there was a violent struggle. Armstrong beat Mr Fairles about his head whilst Jobling stood and watched the attack, doing nothing to help the victim. By the time help arrived, Jobling and Armstrong had both left the scene of the crime. Shortly after, Mr Fairles died of the injuries he had sustained, but before that he did manage to say that William Jobling was not his attacker.

Jobling was soon caught, on South Shields beach; a reward was put out for Armstrong.

Jobling pleaded his innocence at Durham Assizes but was found guilty and sentenced to death by hanging for the murder of Nicholas Fairles. He was hanged in front of Durham Gaol and his body was then taken to Jarrow Slake, where it was gibbetted within site of the scene of the crime. William Jobling was to be the last man to be publicly gibbetted in this country, but in fact that gruesome process did not last as long as had been intended, as the body mysteriously disappeared very soon afterwards. It is said that some of Jobling's friends rescued it and gave it a decent burial in a place which remains secret to this day (or does it? - there are some in South Shields who can tell you where it is!).

To this day no-one really knows the truth of what really happen on that fateful day. It is said that Armstrong fled to Australia but, who knows, maybe he did or maybe he didn't.

A fine morning. Wind NW. At Bells Committee Room. Dined with Ilderton at Barkers.

At Bess
A summer day. Attended Mr Stock & did what was necessary at the Prerogative court in making the affidavit & got the leases by coach from Carlow. Dined at Mackens

A beautiful morning. Got up early & walked up to High Cheston & breakfasted with Mr Robson who afterwards drove us to Newcastle to attend Mr Bells meeting. Dined at Mr Robson. Benjamin Baker Galbraith arrived. Suppered at J Tinleys
Beautiful weather. Wind NW. Walked down to Preston & saw Moon. Wrote to WBS. Dined at home at 5 o'clock. Attended the Bells Committee room. With Bess at night
A beautiful morning. Wind NNE. Went to church. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at 5 o'clock. Walked to Tynemouth in the evening.

A Beautiful weather. Wind SE. Began to canvass with Mr Bell & continued at all day & finished the town & Tynemouth. Dined with Mr Robson at 8 o'clock, a large party including Mr bell. Spent a pleasant day.

Bathed this morning for the first time

Most delightful weather. Wind SE. Bathed again this morning. Walked to Tynemouth. Mr Harrison & his friend Mr Lagcook dined with us at 5 o'clock

With Bess in the evening
A dull damp morning. Wind SSE. Walked down into the low town. Dined at 4 o'clock. Attended the Committee room & afterwards with Bess

A dull morning. Wind NE. Gave a draft on G & Co for £10

Walked with Reed round by Cullercoats & Tynemouth. Dined at 4 o'clock. Attended Ildertons committee room
A dull cold morning. Wind NE changed in the afternoon to SE & rain. Reid left this morning to return home. Dined at 2 o'clock. At Harrisons in the afternoon & with Bess at night

A dull morning. Wind NE. Engaged in the house making up the Hope's book. Received from the Eligible Club £44 & Paid averages to the same £ ____. Dined at home. At Harrison's in the afternoon & at the committee room & Mr Tinley's in the evening
A dull damp morning. Wind SSW. Went to church. Dined at 2 o'clock. Walked to Tynemouth in the evening & walked with Bess
A hot day. Attended at Mr Stocks again & Mr Carmichael. Dined at Mackens
A fine morning & blowing fresh from the W by N. Been a great deal of rain in the night. Walked to Cheston. Dined at home at Harrison in the afternoon. Attended the committee in the evening & at home

A fine morning with a fresh breeze at SW. Took a carriage out to see with Cunningham in the Bomits. Returned at 2 o'clock & had a mutton chop at Harrison's.

With Bess in the evening.

Heavy rain
Heavy rain all night & appearance of more. Wind NW. Dined at home. Out fishing in the evening. With Bess

A fine morning. Wind SW. Paid Sharp grocer £5.5/-. Harrison between £ 1.15 & Spencer £5.2.6. AT the George Tavern. Dined at home at 3 o'clock.

Went out fishing with the Doctor in the evening & suppered with him.

Heavy rain at night
