A very wet morning. Been raining heavily all night. Wind NE. Cleared up after breakfast. Went to sea with Cunningham. Got becalmed & could not race tide. Got a steamer which towed us there. A heavy sea pooped breeze. Dined at Maltrevans. With Bess

Been heavy rain all night. Called upon Jon Laing.

Dined at home

At Harrisons

Walked to Tynemouth in the evening.

With Bess at night
A fine morning. Wind NW. Went to church. Dined at home at 2 o'clock & evening at Tynemouth with Jobbs
A fine morning & fresh breeze from the WNW with rain. Dined at home at 2 o'clock. Walked to Tynemouth in the afternoon & with Bess in the evening
A fine morning but blowing hard from the WNW. Cocnot out boat sailing, returned before 5 o'clock. Adjourned to Malthouse & had some toddy. Took coffee with Mr Tinley

A fine morning. Blowing hard from the NNW. Took a long walk round by Tynemouth, Cullercoats, Whatley Park through Tynemouth and home to dinner. At Doctor's & Harrisons in the afternoon. With Bess at night

A hot day. At the courts in the morning getting petition drawn out. Went to Mr Stocks & signed a bond & to my dismay was told it was also necessary I should also have two friends to give bond, for where am I to find them, being a stranger in Dublin. Paid for Bond stamp 20/- fee to council 21/- & advanced Mr Carmichael £5 Dined at Mackens

A fine cool morning with a strong wind at NNE & sea high.

Wrote to WBS. Dined at home. At Harrison's.

At the committee rooms in the evening & afterwards at J Tinleys

Fine weather but still blowing fresh from the NNE cold & sea high.

Engaged in getting voters to pay fees & taxes. Captain Webb & Mr Rippon dined with me. At the committee rooms & at night with Bess.

A letter from Stephenson

A cold morning & NE wind. Received a letter from Harman & Co losed one with Stephenson's Wyburg bill for aucblane dated the 30th June at 3 months for £51

Dined at home. At Harrison's in the afternoon. At Bell's committee room in the evening & with Bess at night
A fine morning but cool. Wind NNW. Returned the bill for £51 to Major Harrison& Co. Took a walk to Tynemouth. Dined at home. At Tynemouth again all the afternoon & evening with Bess at night.
A dull foggy morning. Wind WNW. Engaged the whole of the day canvassing with Mr Bell. Dined at Mr Robson at High Cheston at 8 o'clock. A rainy night
A fine day. Went with a party to McDowarty came to Blg the races. Dined there. Good running. Holroyd won the cup & we brought it home with us & suppered at the Albion & got infernally drunk
A fine day. Wind SSE. With Bess all day
A beautiful day. Wind SSE. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home at 2 o'clock. Attended the committee room in the evening
A continuance of fine weather. Wind NNE. Robert & BBG set off for Togston. Went to sea with Cunningham. Attended the committee room in the evening & walked to Tynemouth

A beautiful moon. Wind ENE. Went to sea with a fair brig but as usual we were soon becalmed & brought up off the Castle. Had sport fishing drove into the harbour with the tide & got to our moorings at 4 o'clock. Dined on board. Called at Malthouse. At the committee room

A fine summers day & very hot Engaged during the morning at the four-court in preparing petition & in the afternoon went down by steam to Kingston with Mr Gale to show him the yacht & to see J Thompson with whom we dined & returned to Dublin in the evening
A dull morning. Wind N by E. Went to church. Dined at home Walked to Tynemouth. At Cunningham's & drank tea

A beautiful day. Wind from the E. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined with Bess & Jobling at June Laptons. Walked to Tynemouth gave us the afternoon & spent the evening & night with Bess in the barracks having taken lodgings there for a few days

Beautiful weather. Wind in the morning SW changing to SE. Went out to sea with a fine breeze which lasted all day. Very poor sport fishing. Got home in the evening & went up to the barracks for the night
Most beautiful weather. Wind SE. Got up & bathed. BBG & Robert returned from Togston last night. Drank with BBG. I went to Newcastle & drank with D Dixon & came home by steam in the evening
A very rainy day. Wind SE. Dined at home. Wrote to Stephenson having heard of the Hope being on the coast. Widow brown died. At Bess's in the evening. Rained all day

A dull rainy morning. Wind E by N. Received a letter from Stephenson of his arrival at Hull.

Dined at home

At Bess in the evening
A dull morning & little wind from the east. Did not go to sea as intended. Mr Ilderton down today. Charles Ridley dined with us. At Bess at night
A very heavy rain. Wind SW. Stopped in the house & made the Hope's 1st coal voyage up by which I lost £87.11-. Walked to Tynemouth in the afternoon. Dined with J Tinley

A Fine morning. Wind from the NW & NE changeable. Went up to Jarrow to see Jobling gibbetted for the murder of Mr Fairles. Dined at home. Received letters from WBS & Stephenson & answered them. For the latter to go seeking. With Bess in the evening

Beautiful weather. Wind NW. Went out boat sailing at sea all day & spent it very pleasantly. Got in at 9 o'clock.

With Bess
A fine day engaged as usual. Dined at Mackens Received a letter from Mr Vernon saying that he & Mr Turner would come up to Dublin to sign the bonds
Fine weather. Wind SW. I canvassed with Mr Ildeston. Dined at home. At the Bayars
Most beautiful weather. The castlerg, Horse & Foot soldiers marched from Newcastle to Cullercoat Sands for exercise & spent the morning in bathing & answering Meenston

Most delightful weather. Wind S by W & SSW. Went out to sea with the intention of going to Seaham, but could not get further than Souter Point. Brought up at Marsden Rock & dined, went onshore & spent two or three hours & got back in the evening. At Macherr's & with Bess
Fine weather. Wind blowing fresh from the SW. Walked round by Graiger Garden. Dined at home. At Harrison's in the afternoon & with Bess at night.
A beautiful morning. Wind SW. At church. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined with J Tinley & walked to Tynemouth in the evening.
A fine morning. Wind WSW. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. With Bess at night

A beautiful morning. Wind west. Went to sea & had a most delightful run to Seaham. Got our dinner on board & afterwards spent a couple of hours on shore. Started at 4 o'clock & turning quite calm. We did not get home until 2 o'clock in the morning

A dull morning with rain. Wind ESE. Turned out fine. BBG left us & went by the steamer to Stockton there to take the Majestic for London. Dined at home. Wrote to WBS at Harrisons & with Bess in the evening

A dull foggy morning. Wind N. Received a letter from Mr Garbull with the Hope first account & bill of Wades at 4 months dated the 11th Jan for £153.6.3 & paid it into Chapmans. Paid Bradshaw's bill for £39.8. Dined at home. At Harrison's with Bess.
A dull morning & little rain started up. Wind variable. Went to sea, dined at Marsden Rock & got home in the evening. At Mathwens & at night with Bess.
A beautiful day. Went in the morning to Christchurch & delighted with the fine chanting. Dined at Mackeners
A dull morning. Rainy morning. Wind SW. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at 5 o'clock with J Tenley a party. Called at Dixon
A fine morning after a very heavy rain in the night. Wind WSW. Went to church. Walked with Sadler up to the point & dined with him. With Bess at night.
A fine morning. Walked into Tynemouth. Dined with Mr Bells Law Agents at the Albion. Later at Bess

A fine morning. Went with J H Richardson with the Mrs Thompsons of South Shields & Messrs Bonas to see, ran down to the south of Sunderland & afterwards joined Mrs Richardson & a party to tea at Marsden Rock.

At Bess

A fine morning. Wind WSW. Cunningham & I went to sea & were joined by others at the Haven. Light showers but a beautiful breeze all day. Landed at Marsden Rock. Brought up under the castle until lunch cyssed & got home at 8o'clock. With Bess
Premium club bill due £9.10.6 paid. A fine morning & fresh breeze at WNW. Dined at home. Walked to Tynemouth. Cunningham & I called & drank a glass with Captain Mann. With Bess

A beautiful morning. Wind fresh from the Westward. Went over the water & fished for hornests & was successful. Cunningham dined with me & J H Richardson came & took wine of which we had rather too much. With Bess at night.

A fine morning & blowing fresh from the NE. Went out hornect fishing but too much sheets to catch any. Dined at home. Rather stormy & wet evening.

With Bess
A dull morning with showers & blowing hard from the NNE. Did not go to church. Walked to Tynemouth called upon captain Potts & dined with him at 3 o'clock. With Bess

A fine morning. Wind SW. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. After dinner went to fish for hornets. The tide too strong at Mathewsons.

With Bess at night

A wet unpleasant day & a gale from the east, with a heavy sea on the bar, snow at heights. Dined with the associated clubs at the George Tavern. A very handsome dinner & nearly two hundred sat down. Looked into the theatre in the evening
A fine day. Mr Turner came to town. Attended Mr Carmichael & the four-courts. Dined at Mackens. Mr Vernon arrived in the afternoon. At the gardens in the evening

A very rainy cold morning & blowing hard betwenn ENE & ESE. Dined at home. In the afternoon a severe gale & deluge of rain. Confined to the house all the afternoon. Wrote to WBS. Called at Bess in the evening & got home at 10 o'clock
Been torrents of rain all night & blowing hard from the NE. A heavy sea. Dined at home. At the Doctors suppered at the Northumberland Alms & spent the evening at the Widows

A very wet morning. Been torrents of rain all night. Wind NE. Engaged all the morning with Mr Rainsey making a list of furniture for sale. Dined at home. A letter for WBS, the Hope passed the sound on the 21st July. With Bess
Again raining all night & a wet morning. Wind NE. Engaged all the morning again with Mr Rainsy making out inventory. Dined at home. At the Northumberland Alms. With the Doctor. With Bess
Finer weather. Wind SW & looks like more rain. Engaged all morning fishing the catnlsgun. Dined at Northumberland with a party. For rain
Fine weather. Wind N&NE. Engaged making an inventory of the Castle. Dined at home. Walked to Tynemouth. With Bess
Wind NE & a rainy morning. Sent the inventory to the printers. Dined at home. At Bess

A fine morning. Went fishing for hornects. Dined with the Major Wates.

At Bess

A fine morning. Out fishing. Dined at home. At Matthews.

At Bess

A delightful day. Went to sea & had a fine breeze all day. At Marsden Rock. Got in between 5 & 6 o'clock.

At Bess
Attended the Consistory court. Mr Vernon & Mr Turner gave bond, which settled for the administration. Dined at Mackens
A fine day. Wind ____. Engaged all day assigning & numbering the lots. Dined at home. Walked to Tynemouth in the afternoon & took coffee with Messrs Tenbury

Beautiful weather. Engaged all the morning as yesterday. Dined at home at Messrs Harrison's

With Bess

A beautiful morning. Wind WSW. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. Walked to Tynemouth again in the afternoon & remained there in the evening.

With Bess
A fine morning after a shower of rain. Wind W by N. Received a letter from WBS. Sale of furniture in the house. The whole day. Dined at J Tindeys. Walked to Tynemouth in the morning.

Most beautiful weather. Wind NW. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at J Cunningham's. Walked to Cullercoates in the afternoon. Drank tea with Boswell. A beautiful moonlight walk home. Called at Bess. Sale continued
A beautiful morning. Wind SW. Sale continued & finished & resulted £____. Dined with J Tindley. Called at Bess

A fine morning. Rather cool. Wind fresh from the W by N. Walked to Tynemouth & Cullercoates & dined with Boswell.

At Bess

A heavy rain at night
Fine weather. Cool and blowing fresh from the NW. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined with Jebbs. With Bess at night.
A beautiful autumnal morning. Wind NW. Went to Newcastle by the coach. Called to see Emma G. who was not at home. Wrote to WBS. Walked out with D Dixon. Dined & stayed all night at Benton
A beautiful morning blowing hard from the W NW. Walked from Benton home to dinner. The Hope in the sent out at Petersburg on the 28 Aug. At Tynemouth with Jobling in the afternoon. With Bess
A fine day. Returned to Carlow. Dined at Mr Jameson

A dull cloudy morning blowing hard from the W by S. Dined with Jobling at Tynemouth.

Wind Bess
A dull morning & blowing hard from the NNW. At the George Tavern. Dr Drewry & Jobling dined with me. Went to Holdwyr's Kira supper & spent a pleasurable evening. Got home at 4 o'clock
Very much fatigued & did not get up till 11 o'clock. Dined with Doctor & with Bess in the evening
A fine morning. Walked to Cullercoats. Dined at home went with H Hurry to Tynemouth who in consequence of conveyance the St Ledger hollesy gave us a supper. With Bess
Beautiful weather. Wind NW. Dined at home
A Continuance of fine weather. Wind from N & W. Went to Newcastle by steam. Saw Emma G & paid Mrs Noakes. Dined at the Ordenary. I Indian knives. Returned by steam. Took tea & at Sadlers. With Bess
Most beautiful weather. Wind NW. Walked up to Benton to breakfast. Went to church. Dined & stayed all night. Saw Greenwell there.
Extraordinary fine weather. Wind NW. Walked to Newcastle from Benton. Returned to Shields by steam. Found & canvassed with Mr Ilderton. Dined with him at Tynemouth. With Bess at night
Fine weather. Wind NE. Wrote to BBG. Dined at home. Took wine with A Hurry & Boswell at the Albian. There winners of the St ledger lottery. With Bess
Beautiful weather. Began a letter to WBS. Paid boys ways. Jobling & Captain & Ilderson drank with me. Saw the Doctor & went to Bess

A fine day with a few light showers of rain. Mr Walker received the Lord Chancellors orders from Mr Carmichael & served Mrs Falkener with a copy & notice. Entered into an agreement with Mr Digan to grant him a lease when legally authorized of the house in Dublin street & gave him possession upon his paying one year's rent in advance reg:£35 less £2 allowed him for the difference in time between the 30th May the day the lease is to be taken from to this day. Dined with Dr Reed

Mild weather. With rain. Wind SW. Turned out exceedingly hot. With Ilderton & he, the Captain & Jebbs. Dined with me at 2 o'clock. Canvassed again. Walked to Tynemouth. Finished at Barkers. Called at Bess
A dull morning. Wind ENE. Went to Cullercoates & had a chop with Boswell & afterwards attended a pigeon match on the sands. Adjourned to Southerns & finished the evening
A foggy morning. Wind SE. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. At Harrisons in the afternoon. With Bess in the evening
A dull morning having been rain & appearance of more. Wind SW. Chased up. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. A Hurry & I went to Charlston at Billy Mill. With Bess
A beautiful morning. Wind WSW. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. Walked to Tynemouth again. With Bess & took a walk with her in the evening. Paid Wyburg bill £57

Most beautiful weather. Wind W by N. At the court. Dined with H Hurry with the committee of the united.

With Bess in the evening

A fine morning blowing fresh from the SW. Walked to Tynemouth & Cullercoats. Dined with Jobling took whiskey with H Hurry & Boswell at Southerns & attended Cobbetts Return at the theatre at night. At the Albion

A fine morning. Wind SW. Went across the water to look at a fine Danish vessel of 466 tons, the Preciosa. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at 4 o'clock at Mr Metcalfs . Received a letter from WBS. The Hope left Petersburg on the 19 Sept
A fine cool morning after rain. Wind South. Paid average Eligible club £23.10. with Ilderton. Dined at home. At the Northumberland Alms in the afternoon & with Bess at night. A rainy afternoon
A fine cool morning having been rain in the night. Wind NNW. Wrote to WBS. Saw Moor. Dined at home. At Harrisons in the afternoon & with Bess at night
A fair day. Not particularly engaged. Received a letter from William & answered it. Dinned at College Hotel
A dull cold morning having been rain. Wind SW. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. At the Doctors in the afternoon & with Bess at night
A fine morning after a heavy rain. Wind SW. Took plyegic. Dined at home. At the newsroom etc. after dinner, but in the house all the morning and evening.

A fine morning. Wind NW. Got £5 from Chapmans. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. The Lord Gambier arrived from Davis Shaily, a full ship fish. At Harrison's in the afternoon & with Bess in the evening
A beautiful morning wind NW. Walked to Tynemouth & thence to Cullercoats & dined with Boswell. Walked home in the evening. A very wet night.
A dull morning after having been raining all night. Wind WNW. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at 4 o'clock at the George being Mr Ward's opening dinner. With Bess in the evening
A dull morning with showers. Been a heavy rain all night. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined with Jobling. Called at Bess
A fine morning. Went by coach to Newcastle. Spent the day there. Dined with Dixon at the Metcalf & stayed all night in Westgate Street

A beautiful morning. Wind W. After seeing the yeomanry go to church. Left my card upon the Major & sheriff & returned to Shields by steam to dinner. Received a letter from WBS and answered it. Report of the Hope being waterlogged.

With Bess at night
After rain during the night a most beautiful mild morning. Wind WSW. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. Walked to Tynemouth again round by the sands. At Harrison's * at night with bess
More rain last night & a dull morning. Wind SW at the court. Dined with Mr Pew at 4 o'clock & with Bess in the evening
A fine morning. Heavy rain towards afternoon with thunder. Took walk with the boys & got wet through. Dined at Cossays
A dull damp morning. Wind SW. Went to Newcastle & Took the court Alnwick. Dined at the Mess & spent a pleasant day only about 12 officers present. Got to bed about 5 o'clock
Got up at 12 o'clock. A beautiful day. Dined with W Forster & afterwards attended the Ball in uniform. Then attended the Duke and Duchess there. Went out to Lamington at night. Mr & Mrs & Thiss
Most beautiful weather cool. Wind NW went into Alnwick with Mr Ildeston. Returned to dinner. Mr Hodgson MP came to supper
Delightful weather. Wind NW. Mr Hodgson, R Ilderton & young Fenwick walked to Whillingham & went to Roster to shoot. I was out all the morning. Got only two shots & killed nothing.
Fine weather. Wind NW. The Fenwick left for Newcastle. The family went to church. I stopped at home.
A beautiful morning. Mr Ilderton drove to toroles & left us at Ildeston Cottage. Went out shooting & had very good sport. Dined at the cottage at 5 o'clock. I slept all night in cots

Beautiful weather. Went out at 8 o'clock & shot ‘till 2 o'clock & had pretty fair sport. Dined at the cottage. The coach being full, we were obliged to walk, expecting to meet the carriage on the road, but again disappointed. Did not get home until after 7 o'clock quite tired

A dull morning. Wind from the East. Messrs J Friss & Elisabeth & Bob with young Fenwick left us for Newcastle. Dined at 2 o'clock. Ildeston & I spent a quiet afternoon over a bottle of old port & Burgundy
Fine weather. After breakfast Ildeston & I drove into Alnwick. Dined at home at 4 o'clock. Engaged ourselves over a bottle of Champagne & old port
A continuance of fine weather, but shooting all the morning. Killed a hare & partridge. Dinned at 4 o'clock & spent a quiet evening.
A fine morning. Left Carlow for Dublin to attend an appointment before Mr Townsend, a master in chancery tomorrow Arrived in Dublin ½ past 4 o'clock – after a pleasant journey. Dined at Mackens
Fine weather. Out shooting. Killed a brace of birds. Dined at 4 o'clock. Mr & Mrs Ilderton & Miss Fenwick returned from Newcastle
A fine morning. Went to church at Bolton. Dined & spent a quiet day at Lemmington

A rainy morning. Mr Itdeston drove to Alnwick. Took the Couseiur coach to Togston. Got there to dinner a little after 3 o'clock. Tom Smith at Newcastle. The family glad to see me. A quiet rubber in the evening
A dull morning & showery. Cleared up. Went out shooting. Got only one bird, lost two. Came in to dinner at 3 o'clock. Tom Smith returned. A very rainy night. A quiet rubber in the evening
A beautiful day. Went out shooting. Killed 2 ½ brace. Dined at 4 o'clock
A fine morning. Out shooting. Killed a hare, a brace of birds & a pheasant. Tom Smith, Fanny ofs all went to dinner with Mr Fenwick of ____ & to stay all night. Spent the evening as usual.
A very dull rainy morning. Wind SE. rained the whole of the day. Did not stir out. The party returned to dinner at 4 o'clock. Spent the evening as usual.
A beautiful day. Wind West. Went out shooting & killed a pheasant & 6 ½ brace of partridges. Dined at 4 o'clock. A rubber in the evening
A beautiful day & cold. Drove Fanny & Bell to church. Mr L:ord preached: Mr Forster came from Alnwick & with Mr R Fenwick dined with us
A dull rainy morning could not go out shooting. Will Forster left us. Dined at 4 o'clock & spent the evening as usual

Called the first thing upon Mr Carmichael. Attended the master at 11 o'clock at the Four Courts. Damm the law say I. My patience is exhausted, got nothing done this day, for want of an affidavit that there were no other next of kin having but Mr Falkener & ourselves. Dined at Mackens. Suppered at the Steades with Ian Gale
A Weather completely changed. Showers during the day. Went out shooting & killed a 1 ½ brace of pheasants. Captain & Mrs Pensills, Major Clutterbuck & Mr Tylie dined with us.
A fine frosty morning. The party left us. Went out shooting & killed 2 braces of birds & a hare. Dined at 4 o'clock & spent the evening as usual
A fine frosty morning. Dined early with the intention of leaving togston by the 3 o'clock coach but did not, the coachman being drunk & an accident having occurred & also being an hour after I one.
A dull damp morning but afterwards cleared up. Again dined early & left by the coach at 3 o'clock. Arrived at Shields at ½ past 9 o'clock. Called & saw Bess. Letters from Stephenson , WBS etc.
A fine morning. Wind SSE blowing hard, increased towards to a heavy gale with rain, moderate about 11 o'clock. Dined at home. Wrote to WBS & Stephenson. With Bess
A dull morning with showers. Wind from the westward. Dined with A Hurry. With Bess at night.
A fine morning and frosty. Wind W by N. Dined at 4 o'clock. A Hurry dined with us & we went to the Play in the evening.
Fine frosty weather. Wind SW by S. Went up to Newcastle in the morning. Returned to dinner at 5 o'clock. With Bess in the evening

Fine frosty morning. Wind WSW. Tom Smith left me. Went over the water & got a parcel for the Hg Wright & paid averages Hope Club, Robert £2.7.2 Mr Clay £ 7.7.4 = £ 14.14.6.

Dined at home. At the Bells and Table. With Bess
Bell to Chapman on WBS for £150 club. A fine weather morning. Wind NW. rather frosty & thick. Dined at 2 o'clock. Walked with A Hurry to Tynemouth. At the Whist Club in the evening

A beautiful morning. This being a holy day at the Court of Chancery, we could do nothing. I therefor went in the steam boat to Kingstown & dined with J Thompson on board the Royal Charlotte. The Mayor of Anglesey came down & took a sail in his yacht the Pearl. Lieutenant M Paget came on too and the Royal Charlotte to whom I was introduced. No great honor as it is not likely he will know me again.

A fine frosty morning. Went early by steam to Newcastle & returned to Dinner. At the Billiard table.

With Bess

Putus.sb J bill £95.11.5 due. Payable at Barnetts.

Fine frosty weather. Wind W by S. Dined at home. At the billiard table. Spent the evening with Mr Tenley
A dull morning. Wind SSW blowing fresh. Did not go to church. Dined at home. At Bess in the evening

A dull thick morning blowing fresh from the S by W. Received a letter from WBS and answered it sending Chapman & co an order to receive the fix gho & stop the cases for it, if not paid in full pec from Insam on the bill.

At the billiard room.

With Bess

A fine frosty morning. Wind S by E. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. At the billiard room

With Bess
A fine morning. Wind SE. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. At the billiard room & at the theatre in the evening
A fine morning. Wind SSW. Walked towards Tynemouth. Dined at home. At the billiard room. Attended the whist club. At Bess

A foggy morning. Wind SW. Walked to Tynemouth.

Dined at home.

At the billiard room

With Bess at night

A dull foggy morning. Wind WSW. Dined with Jobling. At Tynemouth & afterwards adjourned to Southerners to drink.

Before des lost cases of whiskey.

Attended the whist club at R Fenwicks with eve

A thick & very unpleasant morning. Wind SW & changed to NW.

Dined at home

At Bess at night. The doctor came in
A fine day. Attended the Master Townsend, who appointed us guardians. Dined at Mackens Before dinner had a hot & dusty walk to Phoenix Park

A fine morning. Wind SW. Received a letter from WBS. The merchant won't pay the freight. Answered it to deliver the thep & send her down.

Dined at home. At the Billiard room. Called at Bess. Attended a meeting at Ilderton's commission. At the Theatre

A fine morning. Rather cool & thick. Wind SW. Call upon captain Webb & on board the Crisis.

Dined at 3 o'clock at Tynemouth at Southerners. A dinner given by the Yhact club to j Cunningham.

With Bess at night

A fine morning after a rainy night, blowing fresh NNW.

Dined at home

At the billiard room

With Bess at night

A fine morning after a boisterous night. Wind WSW.

Dined at home.

At the billiard room & in the evening attended the committee room where Mr Alderton arrived. Suppered at Mr Back

A fine morning blowing hard from the WNW. Attended the committee room making arrangements for the election. Dined at Barkers. At the billiard room in the afternoon. A full meeting of the committee in the evening.

Suppered at Barking

A fine morning after much rain during the night. Blowing hard from WNW.

Mr Alderton left. Dined at home. At the billiard room. The whist club with me this evening
A fine morning but blowing a gale of wind & squally from the WSW. Went to church. Dined at home. A heavy rain & stormy afternoon

A fine morning & blowing hard from the WNW. Received a letter from WBS and answered it. Dined at home.

At the billiard room.

Attended the committee room & at night with Bess

A showery morning and blowing hard from the North. Sea high. Dined at home. AT the billiard room.

At the committee room in the evening. At night with Bess

A fine morning. At the committee room & made same cally. Dined at home. At the billiard room in the afternoon. A wet afternoon as an incessant torrent of rain. Went to the theatre. J H Richardson bespcalle
A stormy day blowing hard from the E to E by S & a heavy sea on the bar. Several ships arrived Dined with Mrs Scott

An exceptionally hot day. Attended the Master again for him to look over draft of report, when he thought it would be better to appoint me sole guardian. I cannot make up mind to take in so much trouble difficulties & anxiety that I feel very unhappy. Cannot stand it much longer. Dined at Mackens

A fine day. Wind NW. At the committee room.

Mr Young came into the town in procession which was very poor.

Dined at home. Tibbs with me at the committee room & whist club in the evening. Called at Bess
A fine frosty morning. Wind WSW. Attended the committee room. Walked to Cullercoats to canvass there. Dined at home. At the billiard room in the evening. At night with Bess

A fine morning. Wind from the West. Attended the committee room.

Dined at home. In the afternoon walked up to Preston expecting to meet Ilderton, but he did not come. At Bess.

Mr Ilderton came at 1 o'clock in the morning
A fine morning. Wind WNW. Call to see Mr Ilderton. Went to church. Dined at home. At Mr Barlless all the afternoon & with Bess at night.

A damp foggy morning. Wind WSW. Went over to South Shields Homeralson of quadsdates.

Dined at home. At the billiard room & committee in the afternoon and evening

A beautiful morning. Wind SW. Attended the committee room & canvassed.

Dined at the Barkers

With Bess at night
Beautiful weather. Met Mr Ilderton at the George & walked in procession with him to the leugs. Shew of hands in his favour. Dined at Barkers at the theatre in the evening, Bespeak

A fine morning. The following commenced at 9 o'clock. Young took the lead & kept all day 6/ ahead at the close. Dined at Barkers.

A very rainy night

A fine morning. Polling began at 8 o'clock. Young still kept the lead, our voters not daring to come up intimidated by the threats of the Young party. At the close Young won by.

With Bess at night
Beautiful weather. Went to the hustings at 10 o'clock. Mr Young declared elected. A deal of speaking sparking & angry feeling displayed. Both Young & Ilderton charged slight row.

Another hot summers day. Called at Mr Carmichael's & from the difficult situation in which I am placed, determined upon asking my brother to come to Ireland & going to Carlow tomorrow there to remain until I either see him or have a letter from him in answer to one I wrote this day. Wrote also to Mrs Scott. Dined at Mackens & went to the Lying In Hospital Gardens where there was an immense assembly of company
Beautiful weather. Mr Ilderton & family left. Dined at home. At Jobling in the afternoon & with Bess at night
Fine weather. Wind SW. gave Stephenson £20. Paid average Hope Club £7.2.11. Dined with W C Wright on board the Mulgrave Castl. At the billiard room in the evening & with Bess at night

A fine frosty morning. Wind NW. Attended Bells Committee Room. Walked up to the ship.

Dined at home

At the billiard room. Called at Bess

Went to Youngs Ball in the evening

A sharp frost. Wind NW

Dined at home

At the billiard room

Called at Bess

At an evening party at Mrs J Lainss

Got up early & went in Mr Robson's carrage to Newcastle & voted for Mr Bell. Found WBS at Dixon Dixons. Returned home to dinner. At the billiard room. Attended the club. Bell 332 ahead.

At Bess
A dull wet morning. Wind WSW. Mr Bell returned by a majority above order of 92. Dined at the Albion & had a merry night

Did not get up till 2 o'clock. At the billiard room in the afternoon. WBS arrived & dined at H Metcalfs.

Attended the whist club at the Doctors

A heavy rain. Wind NW. Cleared up about noon.

Walked to Tynemouth

Dined with J Tinley
A frosty morning. Wind SW. Turned out very rainy day. At the billiard room & at 5 o'clock dined with Mr Robson at Cheston
Fine day. Been raining heavily all night & continues. Wind variable between SW & NW. Went to Benton in a post chaise, dined and returned at night. With Bess
A very hot day. Left Dublin for Carlow The Heat most oppressive & clouds of dust. We did not reach Carlow until 7 o'clock. The coach wheel taking fire Dined at Mr Jamesons. Letter from William

A beautiful day. Wind WSW. Walked to Tynemouth. Had a warm bath. Called at Joblings. Walked with WBS to Preston. At the billiard room. Dined at home with WBS alone. At Barkers, no biscuits. Called at Bess

A fine morning. Wind WNW. Engaged with WBS in the morning. At the billiard room.

Dined at home at 6 o'clock & at the whist club in the evening
A fine morning & hard frost. Wind WSW. Engaged with WBS all the morning. Dined at home at 2 o'clock. At the billiard room. WBS left me at 6 o'clock for Newcastle, thence for mail to London. At Bess

A boisterous morning, blowing a gale all day at SE. Sea high. Dined at home at 2 o'clock. Jobblings quarrelled with me. At the billiard room in the afternoon. Called at Bess in the evening. & at whist club at J Tinley's in the evening
A moderate weather. Wind SW cold. Went to church. Dined at home. Walked to Tynemouth in the afternoon. With Bess at night. Very stormy SE

Quite a winters morning with snow. Wind SW. After a stormy night & SE wind

Dined at home. At the billiard room.

Spent the evening & night with Bess. The Doctor there

Highlights

1834-05-30 JRS sold the Hope to Mr Watson for £1005

1834-07-23 George Richardson punches H Hurry in the eye!

1834-08-04 Bess got the Cholera and dangerously ill

1834-10-12 JSR very unwell. Confined for a week

1834-10-22 JSR still unwell. Leeches applied
A fine morning. The hounds came down to Tynemouth & had a beautiful days sport. Dined at home. Took wine with Potts & Charton. Met Emma. At the theatre & finished at the Commercial
A fine morning. Wind N by W. Dis not rise till 11 o'clock. Took a walk round by Tynemouth. Dined with H Hurry & Lowrey at the Albion. Went to the Club

A rainy morning. Wind NW. Dined at home. At the billiard room. Called & sat with A Hurry., he not being well. At the theatre, the bespeak of the Subscribers to the Afsubbuis. A Welsh Rabbit at the Albion

Another very hot day. Attended morning service at Graigh Church to hear a sermon preached by Mr Vernon. For the education of poor children, a collection was made Dined at Mr Jameson. Bathed in the Barrow A letter from William
A fine morning. Wind NE. Called upon Mrs Ratcliff. Dined at home. In the afternoon at the Pig & Whistle. Turned out a wet night. The club at J Wrights, did not go. Spent the evening with H Hurry
A rainy morning. Wind W by N. H Hurry dined with me. Charlton came to wine. We spent the evening at the barracks
A fine morning. Wind SW. Walked over & dined with Charlton at Billy Mill. With Emma Galbraith in the evening
A fine morning. Charlton's gig came for me at ½ past 8 o'clock. Called at Howdon for him & drove to Burnhopeside to dinner & Charlton left afterwards for Dipton, Mr Fenwick
A very rainy morning & continued all day. Wind from the East. Messrs Richmond went to a ball at Lanchester in the evening & I stopped at home with Kit

An incessant rain since yesterday morning & still continues. Wind from the South & East. Left Richmond's after breakfast in his gig for Denton where I dined & then Charlton drove me to Newcastle & we took the omnibus for Shields. At the club. Rope received from Mr Paxton for WBS £30 & gave it to me
A continuance of heavy rain. Wind SE. H Hurry dined with me. At the billiard room. Tea at H Hurry's. Went to the theatre
Went by omnibus to Newcastle. A dull morning. Wind SSE. Took an early dinner at Dixon's. Emma Galbraith at Togston. At the club in the evening. E Charlton stopped all night.
A dull morning. Wind SSE. Walked to Billy Mill with Charlton & returned to dine with H Hurry. At the barracks in the evening

A beautiful day. Very little to do Received a letter from William. Saw Mr Turner who thought he would be able to give security Paid Carroll for spirits 19/- & Haughton for funeral expenses £8.18/-. Dined at Mr Vernon's & took a long walk in the evening. Bathed in the morning
A dull morning. Wind SW. Dined at home. At the billiard room. Met Bess at Pol Pakland. Raining
A very dull morning. Looks like more rain. Wind SSW. Walked up to Jarrow with Lowery Richardson & Hurry to see the Hasoey. Dined there & returned to the Albion in the evening where we made a finish.
A very rainy morning. Wind SW. Cleared up. Went out to Whetley & joined to hounds, but poor sport. Charlton & H Hurry dined with me. Went to the theatre in the evening. Captain Potts bespeak
A fine morning. Wind W by S. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined with the doctor at the Pig & Whistle. Drank tea at H Hurry's. At the club.
A deluge of rain. Wind SW blowing fresh. Cleared away about 10 o'clock. H Nicholson & I went out to Billy Mill to see the family. Dined there. At the barracks at night.
A fine morning. Blowing hard at WNW. Received a letter from WBS. At the Pig & Whistle. Dined at 6 o'clock & spent the evening at home.
A fine morning. Wind WNW. Went to church. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined with J Tinley

A fine morning, rather frosty. Wind W by N. Took a long walk round by Preston across the fields to Cullercoats & Tynemouth, home to dinner. At the Pig & Whistle & suppered with H Hurry. Heavy rain all evening
Finer weather, blowing fresh at WSW. Walked to Tynemouth. Jebbs dined with me at 6 o'clock & we went to the Ball in the evening, a very poor one.
A dull morning after rain, wind WNW. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined with J Craig at 4 o'clock

A very fine day after a fall of rain during the night. Bathed in the Barrow. Attended the examination of the boys at Mr Jameson's & dined there Took a long walk with Mr Vernon in the evening Paid Montgomery Chemist £1.2.4
A rainy morning. Wind SW. Walked up to the Fir trees to see the hounds but no sport. Dined with Saddler. At the club & finished at H Hurry's

A dull morning, appearance of rain. Wind W. Walked up to Newcastle. Paid Noakes for the last half year £47.2 for Emma Galbraith. Dined in Westgate & returned by the 4 o'clock boat. At home all evening
A fine morning, blowing hard from the NW. Wrote to WBS. Dined on board the XYZ with Mod Jarvis
A fine morning after rain, Wind W & WNW with showers during the day. At church in the afternoon. Dined with J Tinley
A fine morning. Wind WNW & cold. Walked to Tynemouth. The Curate, Dr Fenwick & J Tinley junior dined with me at 5 o'clock. Went to the theatre at ½ price. Finished at the Commercial
Been a deluge of rain all night & continued during the day. Wind NE. Dined with J H Richardson
A fine frosty morning. Wind NW. Dined with H Hurry. At the barracks in the evening.
A rainy morning. Wind SW. Cleared up at noon. Dined with the Curate & finished at the Albion
A dull morning after rain. Wind SW. Received a letter from WBS
A very heavy rain. Wind SW. Dined at home. At the Pig & Whistle. At the club at H Dales in the evening

Showers of rain in the morning, but towards noon cleared up & turned into a beautiful day. Attended the examination John & I walked out to Crossleigh & I returned to dine with Mr Vernon. In the evening took a long walk
A fine morning. Wind SW. The XYZ sailed for New York. Went to church. Dined at home. Walked to Tynemouth. At Southsea. Suppered with H Hurry

Beautiful morning. Wind SW. Went round & paid a few of the ships small bills. H Nicholson took Pot Leech with him. At the billiard room & in the evening went to the theatre, play Inspector Bull, bespoke by the ladies & gents of Tynemouth. On account of Mr Wmc Martin's death
A fine morning. Wind SW by S. Wind round & paid a few more bills for the Hope. Dined with H Hurry. At the Albion & psl Jagrir in the evening
A beautiful morning. Wind SW. Went up by steam to Newcastle. Dined & stayed all night at Dixon Dixon who was suffering under a slight attack of gout
A beautiful day. Wind SSW. Returned home by steam. Dined at home. Jobbs took Pot Luck with me. Attended the Mest Club in the evening. Raining night
A fine frosty morning. Wind SW. Dined with H Hurry on board the Choice & went over the bar. Went to the theatre, a full house. Suppered at the Albion
A beautiful morning, rather frosty. Wind NW. At South Shields & saw Mr Paxton. Dined at home. At the Pig & Whistle & the Albion in the evening
A fine morning. Wind SW. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined with H Hurry. At the barracks in the evening
A Beautiful day. Wind SW. Dined at the Albion with the gents: Railroad meeting. At the Pol Jarvis
A fine mild morning. Wind W. Went by steam to Newcastle. Dined & stayed all night with Dixon Dixon who was confined to the house with gout. Took Emma Galbraith's trinket box up.
A wet day, heavy showers of rain Received a letter from Bob Marsh. Dined at Mr Jameson A large party being the last day of the examinations
A fine morning but cold wind WNW. Returned to Shields by steam. Left Emma Galbraith's trinket box in charge of Mr & Mrs Dixon. Dined with Dr Fenwick. At the Albion in the evening
A beautiful morning. Frosty. Wind NW. Walked to Tynemouth. H Hurry took Pot Luck with me. At the Pig & Whistle club in the evening. Rain
A dull morning after rain. Wind NW. Dined at home. At the billiard room. Drank tea with H Hurry. At the Albion
A dull damp foggy morning. Wind N by E. Little of it. Received a letter from WBS. H Hurry dined with me. At the Albion. Met Bess at night.
Rather a dull morning. Wind NW. Turned out a beautiful mild day & wind changed to SW. Walked to Tynemouth both morning & afternoon. Dined with J Tinley
A dull morning. Wind WNW. Went to Whitley & was with the hounds all day & had the gon run. Dined at Craig. Both Bess in the evening & finished at Pols
A most delightful morning. Summer weather. Wind NW & increased till night when it became a heavy gale. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home at 5 o'clock. Attended the Ball in the evening. Few there.
The gale still continues heavy at WNW with showers. Walked to Tynemouth. H Nicholson & I dined & spent the evening with H Hurry
Beautiful weather. Wind NW. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. At the Pig & Whistle & club in the evening
A fine morning & blowing fresh at NW. Went to Cleadon & saw the hounds. Dined at Harton. At the George in the evening.
A fine day. Amused myself with the boys. Dined at Doctor Reeds a large party & spent a pleasant evening
A fine morning. Wind NW. Went to Newcastle by steam. Dined & stayed all night at D Dixon
A dull morning with rain. Wind NW. Returned to Shields by steam. Dined with H Hurry

A beautiful morning. Wind NW. Went to Sunderland & saw Mr Metcalf's new ship, the William Metcalf, launched. A very fine vessel of acar tous. A large party dined at the house & returned to Shields at night.
A fine morning. Wind NW. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. At the Pig. Albion in the evening.
A fine morning. Wind WNW. Went up to Newcastle by steam. Nothing determined about Emma Galbraith's leaving for London. Returned home in the afternoon. Met Bess
A dull damp morning. Wind NNE & SW in the afternoon. Dined at home. Wrote to WBS. Called at the Doctors. At the club. Heavy rain

A fine morning. Wind NE. At the ship. Paid several tradesmen's bills. Walked to Tynemouth. The doctor took his dinner with me. At the Pig. Spent the evening with Bess. Hove the ballast clear of the timbers that they flogin may been seen.

A fine day. Went to Newcastle. Brought Emma Galbraith down with me. We dined at Mrs Reeds to meet there Ilderton. Received a letter from BBG from the Macerations. All well except Mr Barnes who was deranged
A very wet unpleasant morning. Wind NW. Did not go to church till the afternoon. Dined at J Tinley
A fine morning. Wind SW. Received the bills from the British Club £490 & paid them into Cs & Co. Got an order for WBS on Barnetts for £150 on account. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at Messrs Reeds
A fine day. Amused myself with John, fishing. The Cary's dined with Mr Vernon & spent a very pleasant evening at Major Wolsleys, quadrilles etc

A fine morning, blowing hard from the WSW. Went to Newcastle with Emma Galbraith. Booked her place in the High Flyer to London with Mr & Mrs Batson. Returned by steam with R Ilderton. Dined with J Tinley & attended the sales of the Hope, put up at £1000 & no bidders
A beautiful morning. Wind WSW. Lunched with Mrs Reed & then Ilderton who returned home. Went to Newcastle & stayed all night. Much rain in the evening

A fine morning. Emma G left at 9 o'clock in the High Flyer with Mr & Mrs Batson for London. Walked with Dixon to Benton. Turned out a heavy rain. Returned to Newcastle in a hackney Chaise to dinner & stayed all night
A fine morning. Wind WSW & in the afternoon WNW. Came to Shields by steam. Dined with H Hurry. Suppered at the Albion.
Heavy showers & blowing hard at WSW. Changed to NW & NNW & a perfect hurricane. Dined at home. At the Pig & the club in the evening at Drury's
Fine weather. Wind NW. Went to church. Walked to Tynemouth after lunch. Dined with Iw Tynley
A dull damp morning. Wind NW. H Hurry dined with me. Drank tea with him. At the Albion in the evening
A mild morning. Wind WSW. Walked with Cunningham round by the ship to Saddlers & home to dinner. At the Pig. In the evening at the Albion & Pol Jarvis

Mild spring weather. Rather damp. Wind NW. Dined at 5 o'clock. Wrote to WBS. Went to dance & supper at Captain Potts, Wallsend, a large party. Spent a very pleasant night. A splendid supper, stopped rather too late, not getting home before 8 o'clock
In bed all day. At the club in the evening

1828

A

New Era

in my life

January
A bitter cold day with frost Wind ESE half a gale & a heavy sea on the bar. Two or three ships arrived. Dined at home. Went to the theatre in the evening. Mitchell's benefit £53 in the house

A fine day, Received a letter from William from Shields. Refusing to come over & assist me out of my difficulties. Much disappointed, determined upon leaving Carlow on Thursday & wrote to Captain Butler to send Emma to me.
A fine morning. Wind NE. Walked to Tynemouth. Went by steam to Jarrow with Richmond & saw the Harvey launched off the ship. Dined with a party at the Dock House.
Most beautiful weather. Wind NW & during the day NE to SE. Walked to Tynemouth. H Hurry took his dinner with me. At the Pig & the club with me in the evening. Received a letter from WBS
Beautiful weather. Wind NNW. Glass very high. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined with H Hurry & had cashius with him at J Moors

A foggy morning. Rather damp. Wind NE. Received a letter from WBS with leave from Lees & Co to sell the Hope. Called upon Mr Watson, not at home. Walked round by Preston & Tynemouth & Home to dinner. Met Jare Yoary in the evening. At the George

A fine mild morning. Wind SW. Saw Mr Watson. Did not make a bargain. Determined to lay the ship on shore off the taking her ballast out. Lunched with H Hurry. Dined with Hy Metcalfe & went to the play in the evening. A very good one about 80 people there

A beautiful morning. Wind SW. Nearly agreed to sell Mr Watson the Hope for £1100. Took a long walk with Dr Fenwick round by Chirton, Billy Mill, Murton, Preston & Home to dinner at Dr Fenwick's at 5 o'clock. At the Albion in the evening
Continuance of fine weather. Rather frosty. Wind about W changed to SW. Went to Newcastle by steam. Wrote to WBS. Dined at the George Tavern at 5 o'clock
A beautiful morning. Wind WNW. Took a long walk with Dr Fenwick. Dined with Mr Taylor

A fine morning. Wind SW fresh breeze. Receive a letter from WBS with the partition of the murder of poor Errington of the Alexander by the water between Montreal & St Donning. Dined on board the Mr Metcalfe. A large party of ladies, gents & children. At the club in the evening at J Tinley's
A dull cloudy morning & blowing very hard at NW. Went to the Catholic Chapel being Palm Sunday. Dined with H Hurry & C Cockrill's Walked to Tynemouth in the evening

A cloudy morning. Bathed before breakfast with the boys. Saw Mr Justin to inform him of my intention to endeavor to manage the property etc. without interference of chancery. Wrote to William of my determination to return to England. Turned out a very wet day Dined with Mr Vernon
A fine morning. Wind NE. Went up to the ship, parted her from the crake & laid her upon the shore. Walked to the barracks. Dined at home. At 5 o'clock. Met Jare Younry
A fine morning and cold NNE wind. Walked to the ship & afterwards to Tynemouth. H Hurry dined with me. At the Pig & Whistle. Suppered with H Hurry & finished at the Abbey Inn
A fine morning. Wind NW. Slepl at the Abbey. Dined with H Hurry. Saw Mr Watson. Nothing done.

A fine mild morning. Wind SW. Saw Mrs Watson who refused to confirm her agreement for the Hope & wished to reduce my price to £1000 which I refused to do. The br drove me round by Whitley, Hartley, the avenue head to Preston to dine with W C Wright. Came to the club in the evening
A fine morning & blowing hard at SW. Afterwards a hurricane with heavy showers. A small party dined at the Albion
A fine morning. Wind NW. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. At the Pig. Wrote to WBS. At H Hurry's in the evening
A fine morning but cold. Wind NW. Went to church. Cockrill, Hurry & Holroyd dined with me. At Tynemouth in the evening. Poxes
A beautiful morning. Wind NW. Went up to Tynemouth & had an early dinner with Jebbs. Too ill from cold & to dine with the party at Sothern's. The races very bad & weather changed. Cold & showery
A dull morning and cold NE wind. Walked to Tynemouth & lunched with Downey, a very handsome turn out at Southerns. Bad racing. A good many people there. Finished off at Southerns. A rainy night

A fine morning after much rain. Wind NW. Received a letter from WBS & answered it, G & Co's order upon Barchatts for £80. Saw the Messrs Evington's. Dined with Mr Dale being the christening of his daughter.

A beautiful day after a little rain in the morning. Emma arrived from Broomville & much better than I could have expected. Engaged with Mr Turner settling his accounts. Paid Haughton £9.12.6 Byrm Chymist £9.18. Mrs Connolly £7.4.6 Dined with Mr Vernon. Drank tea with Mrs Falkener
A fine morning. Wind NNW. Went to Newcastle by steam. Walked to Benton. Dined & stayed all night

A cold morning. Wind NNW. Benton agricultural show of cattle; well attended. Upwards of 100 sat down to diner. D Dixon in the chair. The room very crowded, hot & uncomfortable. At Dixons in the evening & stopped all night
A fine morning & cold NW wind. Dixon drove me into Newcastle. H Hurry & dined at the 3 Indian Kings. Returned by steam
A beautiful morning. Wind NNW. Took a drive with Drury. Dined with him at 2 o'clock. Spent the evening at Tinley
Most beautiful weather. Wind NW. Received a letter from WBS. Wind changed to ENE & cold. Wrote to WBS. Dined with J H Richardson & suppered with the Doctor. H Nicholson sailed for Riga
A fine morning. A cool NE wind. Walked with Dr Fenwick out to Whitley Park & called upon Mr J Wrights. Dined with Dr Fenwick
A dull morning & cold NE wind. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. At the Pig & Whistle. Suppered with H Hurry
A fine morning & cold NE wind. . Walked up to the ship. Paid Ballast crane 30/-. Dined with the Committee of the United Club at the Albion & spent a pleasant day
A continuance of cold NE wind & dry weather. Dined with H Hurry. At the Albion in the evening
A NE wind. Sea high & very cold, with showers of hail & sleet during the day. Walked to Tynemouth. H Hurry dined with me at the Pig & Whistle. Spent the evening with Messrs Tinley

A fine day. Engaged during the morning in paying bills etc. paid Davies £14.5 Sally bal wages £13.17.7 & left with Mr Vernon a bill at 1 month: WBS for the balance of his account £56.9/-. Wrote to Mrs Scott of my intention to leave Carlow tomorrow. Dined with Mr Vernon & took tea with Mrs Falkiner
A continuance of cold NE wind & showers. Walked to Tynemouth in the afternoon. Dined with J Tinley
A fine morning. Wind SE at 10 o'clock. Had been from the W. The Lord Gaulieu & Lady Jane sailed. Took a long walk with H Hurry round by Tynemouth through the county by Preston to the Doctor to dinner
A beautiful morning,. Wind SW. Took a long walk with Dr Fenwick along the coast through Cullercoats & the Dr dined with me at 5 o'clock
A fine morning. Wind SW. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined with Holdroyd at the Albion, he being sworn in High Constable. A pleasant party
A beautiful summer's morning. Wind SSW & SE. Dr Fenwick & I walked to Cullercoats & he took his dinner with me at 5 o'clock. At Albion in the evening
Beautiful weather, rather cool, wind SE. The Cove sailed yesterday & the Grenville Bay this morning. Walked to Billy Mill. Dined at home. At Dr Fenwick's in the evening

A beautiful morning. Wind NE. Went by steam with Dr Fenwick & Mr Taylor to Newcastle. Lunched at the Queen's Head. The Dr & I walked out to Benton with D Dixon, dined & walked to Shields through the country in the evening
A continuance of fine weather. Wind SE. Went to church. The vicar's brother fercactied. Dined with H Hurry at Tynemouth in the evening.
A dull morning. Wind NE. Walked with H Hurry round Cullercoates, Preston & collecting land tax. Dined with him
A fine morning. Wind NW & NE. Walked to Tynemouth. H Hurry dined with me. At Tynemouth again in the evening. At the Albion
A very fine day. Left Carlow at 9 o'clock for Dublin with Emma who bore the fatigues of the journey well. Took her to Mrs Balskams in Grafton Street to sleep. Dined by myself at Mackens
A dull cool morning. Wiind NE by N. Dined with C Cockerill at the Night Officer. At the Pig afterwards & Albion.
Delightful weather. Wind NE. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined on board the Craig. At the Albion in the evening. Quarrelled with W Charlton & pulled his nose

A fine morning. Wind NE. Walked round by Tynemouth with H Hurry & J H Richardson. Dined on board the Choise & went over the bar with her. Landed at Tynemouth & spent the evening at Southerners. E Charlton apologised & the quarrel amicably settled
A fine but dull morning. Wind NW. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at Home at 5 o'clock. At the fair & in the evening at the club at H Dales
A fine morning & fresh breeze at SW & S by E. Lunched at Tinley's. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at Tinley's. Rain at night. Much wanted
A rainy morning & blowing fresh from the ENE & sea high, wind increased to a gale. The rain continued all day without ceasing. Dined at 5 o'clock & spent the evening at home.
Fairer weather & dry, fresh NE breeze. Dined at 5 o'clock & spent the evening at home.
A foggy morning with rain. Wind NE. Received a letter from R Ilderton. Wrote to WBS & Mr Platts & spent the evening at home
Finer weather & less wind NE & sea fallen. Tom Smith arrived. Walked to Tynemouth. H Hurry dined with me

A foggy damp morning. Wind ESE. Mr Thompson of South Shields & another examined the Hope. Dined with C Charlton at the Northumberland Alms. At H Hurry in the evening. He has got a slight attack of gout. Met Bess

A fine day. After breakfast, called & saw Emma & took her to see her friends, the Bagots in Peter Street who requested she should spend the day with them. Called upon Mr Carmichael & got the leases. Dined with Charles Hurry & brought Emma home in the evening. Sent the leases by Mr Gale to Mr Vernon
A beautiful morning. Wind about W & SW. Walked to Tynemouth. Dr Fenwick dined with me. Suppered at H Hurry's
Most beautiful weather & very hot. Wind SW. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined with H Richardson
Summer weather. Wind SW. Dined on board the Jubrais a large party of ladies & had quadrilles. Met Bess

Beautiful weather. Wind SW. Went to Newcastle & took the Alnwick Coach & arrived at ½ past 4 o'clock. Had a mutton chop at the Swan & Walked out to Lamington. The Idleston's carriage was in but could not wait
A fine morning. Wind WSW. Accompanied Mark & R Ilderton out fishing. They caught 4 dozen. Dined at 5 o'clock

Fine weather. Wind SW. Mr Ilderton & party drove down over to the Game Keepers cottage at Ilderton. Bob Mark & I amused ourselves fishing in the Jilf. Dined at the cottage & returned to Lamington in the evening
A fine day. Amused ourselves shooting rooks in the morning. After lunch fished in the burn, caught a few. Dined at 5 o'clock
A cool morning. Drove into Alnwick for Mr & Mrs Mark to catch the 12 o'clock coach. A little rain. Spent the morning in Alnwick & returned to Learere at ½ past 4 o'clock. Wind SW
Fine weather. Wind SW & cold. Went to Edlingham church. Dined at 2 o'clock & spent a quiet day at home
Beautiful weather. Went to Alnwick being Fair day. A good show of women if not of other cattle. Got home to dinner at 6 o'clock. Shot rooks in the evening

A fine morning. Breakfast with Charles Hurry. Hired a car & took Emma to Kingstown. Left Luggage on board the St George steam boat & afterwards dined at Greshams Hotel Left Kingstown at 7 o'clock with a great many passengers on board
A continuance of fine weather & warmer. Amused ourselves fishing. (*) Mr Thompson dined with us. (* an attorney at Wooler)
Benton Park: country estate to housing estate

A beautiful morning. Mr & Mrs Ilderton drove us over to Ilderton. They stopped to attend Mr Howey's sale. Robert & I went on in the carriage to Benton beyond Wooler. I walked from there to West Newton & fished down the Glen, beautiful stream but had poor sport, being a bright day & water fine. Suppered at Benton & went by coach at ½ past 11 o'clock to the GameKeepers Cottage at Ildeston to sleep. Excessively fatigued
A fine morning. Took the coach to Whittingham & walked from thence to Lemmington. Dined with Mr Bussett at Broom park at 5 o'clock. Met the Smiths from Togston. Messrs Clatterbuck, the Morses etc
Delightful morning. Amused ourselves shooting rooks. After lunch Bob Ilderton rode to Alnwick. Heavy showers of hail & rain in the afternoon

A dull morning. Mr Ilderton drove Robert am me into Alnwick & we got the coach at 12 o'clock & arrived at Newcastle at ½ past 4 o'clock. Dined a7 staid all night with Dr Fenwick. Heavy rain all day. R Ilderton dined at the club house

A fine morning. The Doctor & I breakfasted with R Ilderton at the Turks Head and afterwards came down to Shields by steam. Received a letter from & wrote to WBS. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined with J Tinley at 5 o'clock. Much surprised to find the Doctor there, having left him in Newcastle. Captain Beckham 19th Regiment & the Curate there

A fine morning. Wind SW. Saw Mr Thompson of South Shields who would not offer £1000 for the Hope, also Mr Watson & Harrison, the brewer who did but I declined. Spoke to J Young about the payment of his bill for £100 & he offered to take £50 at present.

R Ilderton came down to dinner & we afterwards went to Shields races which were very good & many people there.

A fine morning. Wind W by N. Received a letter from Mr Watson offering me £1005. Called upon him & agreed to take it. R Ilderton & yound Fenwick came down & dined with me & afterwards went to South Shields races which were pretty good. Finished at the Albion

A fine summer's morning. Wind NE & SE. Mr Watson after being on board the ship, called & signed the agreement for the purchase at £1005. Dined at home at 4 o'clock. At C Cockwells. Walked to Tynemouth, at Southerns. Met Bess.

It began very early in the morning to rain & blow hard & it increased to a heavy gale. Nearly all on board sick. Obliged about 12 o'clock to lay to not being able to see land or make the floating light. The weather so thick. Between 1 & 2 o'clock made the light & got into Liverpool at 3 o'clock after a very stormy passage across of 20 hours and landed very wet. Got Emma to bed, much exhausted from the fatigues & sickness. We stopped at the Angel Inn

Most beautiful weather & wind SE. Received a letter from WBS. Answered it with the Kent & Gth account & informing him of the the sale of the Hope. R Ilderton came down & we & H Hurry dined with Mr Tibbs
A fine morning. Wind SE. Rob Ilderton left for Newcastle. Dined with Messrs Dobson, Richard, Richardson, Lowing & Hurry at the Albion. An excellent dinner. Met Bess

The glass continues very high, at set fair & fine weather. Wind NE. Mr Young gone from home, consequently his bill not paid. Went to Newcastle by steam. Paid Augur for cleaning carriage 18/-. Dined with Dr Fenwick & returned in the evening. At the Albion
Fine weather, fresh breeze at NE & sea high & rather cool. H Hurry & I walked round by Preston. Dined with him & spent the evening at Tynemouth, the Barracks & the Abbey
A fine morning. Wind NE. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined with S H Richardson at 4 o'clock & spent a pleasant day.
Fine weather & blowing fresh from the NE & sea high. H Hurry dined with me. At the Pig & Whistle. Took tea with C Cockrill. Walked to Tynemouth in the evening & fresh. At the Albion.

Fine weather. Wind NE. The Kings birthday. Took a walk with C Cockrill to Tynemouth. The military fired a salute. Went round by Cullercoats where I bought an old net for C Richardson for 10/- Whitley & Preston home & dined with C Cockrill. Met Bess

A fine morning. Wind E by S. Received a letter from WBS saying he had sent the bill of sale etc off. Walked to Tynemouth at 4 o'clock. Wrote to C Richardson & sent him a pressing net for his fruit trees. The Deeds did not arrive till 5 o'clock. Wrote to WBS to inform him of it
A dull morning. Wind NE. Met Mr Watson & received £1005 & gave him possession of the Hope. Dined on board the Choise. At Tynemouth. Wrote to WBS
A beautiful morning. Wind WNW. Started for Alnwick. Got there at ½ after 2 o'clock & went out to Lemmington with the Ilderton's to dinner

A deluge of rain which continued all day. Left Liverpool for Leeds at 5 o'clock where we arrived about 6 o'clock. Poor Emma much annoyed by an eruption on the skin with great heat & itching like the nettle rash from the heat & sickness on board the steam boat. Took tea & slept at Greaves
A beautiful morning. Wind as well as I can judge from the S & W. the family did not attend morning service, it being at Bolton where they have no pew. They went in the afternoon. I did not.
Extraordinarily fine weather. At home all day. Robert & I went out fishing, had poor sport.
Beautiful weather. At home all day

Fine weather. Mr Ilderton drove me over to Ilderton. Bob & Tom rode. Left Mr I there & we went out to the Glen to fish & had pretty fair sport considering the weather. Sent some trout to Dr Drury & so tired that we stopped & slept at Wooler Cottage
A fine morning. I Ilderton, Jack & I went considerably above Kirk Newton, but the sun being too bright & no wind, we had bad sport. Slept at Ilderton Cottage
A fine day. We returned to Lemming ton. Received a letter from WBS. Wrote to Mr Stoker
Most beautiful weather. Mr Ilderton drove us into Alnwick
The weather continuing unvaried. Went to church at Edlingham & dined early
Fine weather. Called upon Mr Welkg & Mr Burrells, Broom Part. Fished afterwards. Poor sport. At home
Most beautiful weather. Wind SW. Went with Mr & Mrs Ilderton to Ilderton Cottage & returned to dinner at 6 o'clock. Robert went to Woolie to join Major Grunward. A heavy fall of rain with thunder

Rather cloudy in the morning, but turned out a fine day. Left Leeds at 6 o'clock for Shields where we arrived at 8 o'clock & got home at 9 o'clock. Poor Emma tormented by the eruption. Dr Grunhow saw her & sent some physic. Mrs Scott from home at Togston. Got some tea & went to bed early
A continuance of most beautiful weather. Fished with worm in the Aln, but poor sport

No change in the weather. Went to Rosen & found Robert, I & Major Greenwood there. Drove up in a cart to the Dod. Saw the ship washing. Dined upon the Jarf "Pie Nie". Took tea at Rosene with Mr & Mrs Neil & returned home at night
A fine cloudy morning & quite a breeze. Went to the Aln & caught a good dish of fish, which I brought home to dinner at 4 o'clock
A cloudy morning. Wind SW blowing hard. Mr Ilderton drove me into Alnwick where I met Tom Smith who drove me to Togston. Caught in a tremendous heavy rain & got wet through
Beautiful weather. Wind SW. Went to Warkworth Church. William Forester rode from Alnwick, dined with us & returned in the evening.
Fine weather. Wind SSW. Amused myself walking all the morning. Mr & Mrs R Fenwick & called & dined
A fine morning. Walked to the Barnes & Collinary. Fished in the pond in front of the house & caught several eels. Dined at 4 o'clock

A fine morning. Wind SW. Walked round by the colliery & Barnes. And afterwards to Amble where a Newcastle steam boat had arrived with a party. Commenced raining & continued heavy for the rest of the day

A dull morning. Wind SW. Tom Smith drove Robert & me to Felton where we got upon the coach & drove to the Race course. The sport very good. Mr Ord with Tomboy won the gold cup again, having won it last year. Captain Potts won the Wallsend Harrier Cup. Mr & Mrs Dixon drove me out to Benton where I dined & stayed all night.
Beautiful morning. Dixon & I walked to Newcastle. In the afternoon walked out to the Course, but nothing going on. Dined with Dr Fenwick & returned home in the evening by steamer.
A very heavy gale with sleet, wind SE. Sea on the bar. Dined with Mr J Carr at Mrs Hutchison & spent a pleasant evening. Declined Mrs Mathews Party
A fine day. Emma a great deal better. Engaged all morning writing to Mrs Falkener, Mr Verrnon & Miss Scott. Dined with I Tindley
A fine morning. Wind SW. Dined at home. Wrote to WBS. At the Pig. Walked to Tynemouth. At H Harry's in the evening

A fine morning. Wind W by S. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined with H Harry. We with Holdroyd & Mr Burns went up by water & Sadlers & spent the afternoon. In the evening crossed the river to see the railroad & walked down it. At the Albion
A fine morning. Wind SW. Had some dinner with H Harry & walked out & had wine with Charlton at Billy Mill. Went to Monkseaton races
A fine morning. Wind WSW. Took a long walk. Dined at 5 o'clock. At Tynemouth in the evening. Met Bess in a Richmond

A fine morning. Wind WSW. Sailed round to the Haven & walked back. Dined at 2 o'clock. The steward of the St Hilda called, having brought Mr Baskes home & gave me good account of BB Galbraith. Saw Mr Pletts. Out fishing for an hour with the doctor. Came on a very wet night. Finished at H Harry's
Heavy showers. Wind NW. Walked round by Grays garden & H Harry dined with me. At Tynemouth in the evening. Took wine with H Metcalf. Met Bess

A fine morning blowing hard from NE. H Hurry, Cunningham & I took a long walk round by Preston across the country to Whitbey. Cullercoats Sands, Tynemouth. Dined with H Hurry. At Tynemouth in the evening
A fine morning. Wind NW. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined with C Cockrill & H hurry & in the evening took a sail up to Holburn Quay & drank tea
Beautiful weather. Wind from the E. H Hurry dined with me. At Tynemouth in the evening

A continuance of most beautiful weather. Wind NW. Bathed for the first time. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. H Hurry & C Cockrill & I rowed down to see the salmon fishing & landed at the Haven. Met Bess
A fine day. Dined at home & turned in the evening. Went with Mrs Reed & Miss Harrison to take tea. Not very well. Returned home early. Wrote to William
Fine weather. Wind NE. H Hurry & I went with the doctor & spent the day at sea. Landed at Tynemouth in the evening

A fine morning. Wind NE. Received a letter from WBS which much relieved my mind & made me feel happier than I have done some time, stating the almost certainty of his getting appointed to a situation on the Coal Exchange by the Factors & also giving me leave to dras upon him for the Hope's tradesmen's bills. H Hurry dined with me. At Tynemouth. Met Bess

A dull morning. Turned out fine. Wind SE. Received threatening letter from J Metcalf & Son about the Hope's bill. Went over the water & saw them. Promised to pay in 4 months. Dined at home. At the Pig. Walked to Tynemouth in the evening
Beautiful weather. Wind SE. Out trying to catch horneal, none to be seen. Dined at home. Out boat sailing in the afternoon. At Tynemouth in the evening
Extraordinarily fine weather. Wind ESE. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined with C Cockrill & H Hurry at the Custom House. At the Pig. Drank tea with C.C & spent the evening with H Hurry
Most delightful weather. Wind ESE. At church. Walked to Tynemouth in the afternoon. The Doctor. C Cockrill & H Hurry dined with me at 5 o'clock. At Tynemouth again
Beautiful weather. Wind ESE. Walked to Tynemouth. H Hurry came up & we had some cold beef with Henderson & spent the afternoon. Met Bess. A fine shower in the afternoon & wind changed to SW

A fine morning. Wind SW & warm. Rose before 6 o'clock. Walked by the fields to Cullercoats, bather & returned by Tynemouth & the shore, home to breakfast. Took a drive with the doctor. Dined with H Hurry. At the Albion with Harrison &
A dull morning & fresh breeze at NNE. Dined with H Hurry, Charlton & Deacon of the 19th at Southerns & spent the day. Met Bess
Showers & wind SW. Dined at home. At H Hurry's in the afternoon. At Tynemouth in the evening
Another fine day. Walked out with Emma & dined again, Emma and I, with I Tindley
A fine morning. Wind SW. bathed. Dined at home. At Tynemouth in the evening. Met Bess
A fine morning. Wind SW & SE & SW within. Bathed. A few minutes. H Hurry & I walked to the Black Middens & got into the Doctor's boat. H Hurry dined with me. At Tynemouth in the evening.
A fine day. Fresh breeze at WNW. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined with H Hurry. At Tynemouth again in the evening
A fine day. Wind WSW. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. Spent the evening with JH Richardson. Met Bess
A fine morning. Wind WSW. A slight shower. Bathed. Dined with Durthman at Tynemouth & spent the afternoon there.
Beautiful weather. Wind WNW. Bathed. Wrote to WBS. Paid J Young £50 account & ½ years interest. Dined with H Hurry & C Cockrill at Tynemouth in the evening
A fair day. Wind NE. Walked to Tynemouth. The Doctor dined with me. Called to see H Hurry who has the gout. At Tynemouth

A foggy damp morning after heavy rain during the night. Wind E by S. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. Went out in the boat with the Doctor. No sport. At Tynemouth again in the evening. At The Albion with My Sproogy & Holroyd. Met Bess.
A rainy morning blowing hard at ENE & sea high. Dined with H Hurry. Called at the Doctor's & finished at the Pig
A dull morning after a deluge of rain all night. Wind E, E by S & SE. Dined with the Doctor. At Tynemouth both morning and evening
A cloudy day. Emma not very well. Stayed and dined at home. I dined with I Tindley

A fine morning after more heavy rain in the night. Wind SE. Dined at the Pig & Thistle, intended to be beefsteaks to be sent by Jos Elder, but not done in his usual mean way, the beef was so course & tough that was not fit to eat or be sent on board any ship. We were properly treated for condescending to receive a treat from such a man & I blame myself much for going. He took good care not to be present himself. Drank tea at Hurry's & at Tynemouth in the evening. Met Bess
Beautiful weather. Wind NE. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined with H Hurry. Spent the evening at Tynemouth, Bartman etc

A fine morning. Wind NNE. In the court all the morning. Dined at home. That low scoundrel George Richmond made a most brutal attack on H Hurry & hit him a tremendous blow on the left eye, but they punished him for it. At Hurry's in the afternoon & the Albion in the evening
A dull damp morning & blowing hard at N. Bartleman dined with me. At H Hurry's & the Albion.
A most beautiful day. The artillery horse & foot & the 7th Hussars had a field day on Cullercoat Sands. A fine sight & Richardson & I afterwards dined with Charlton at Southerns
Got up early & bathed, it afterwards rained, wind S by W. Dined with H Hurry & spent the day. Heavy rain
Heavy rain until 9 o'clock. Wind from the East. C Cockrill breakfasted with me & we went to the Catholic Chapple. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined with J Tinley. Moist scotch
A foggy dull morning. Wind NE. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. At H Hurry's in the evening
A continuance of fog & misty weather & very damp. Wind N by E. Played at Billiards at Tynemouth. With Dr Fenwick & at the Pig. Drank tea with Cockrill, at Tynemouth
A beautiful day. Wind NNE. Played at billiards again at Tynemouth with Deacons, 19th regiment. Dined at home. At H Hurry's in the afternoon 7 at Tynemouth in the evening

A fine day. Received a letter from Fanny Smith to take Emma to Togstow which I'm not able to do expecting the Hope. Went to church in the morning. I dined with H Harry, walked to Tynemouth in the evening & on our return found Geo & his wife had arrived. Wrote to Fanny Smith
A fine morning & fresh breeze at NNE. Dined with GH Richardson & in the afternoon went out boat sailing. Drank tea at the Albion. Met Bess
An unpleasant foggy damp morning. Wind NNE. Went to Newcastle by steam. Dined with Mr Aevcy & slept at Dr Fenwick's

Beautiful weather. Wind NE. called upon the Ildertons & at Dixons. Dined with J H Richardson etc at the George ordinary. Drank wine at Mr Whitfield's at the Halfmoor. Returned by steam & suppered with JAK
Most beautiful weather. Wind ENE. Took a short walk. Dined with JH Richardson. At Tynemouth in the evening
Delightful weather. Wind WNW. Charlton & H Hurry went over with me to Sunderland & dined with R Jobling on board his new ship the Duchess of Northumberland 550 tons, bound to New South Wales

Fine weather. Wind SW. the Doctor drove me to Carville Preston etc. dined with him. Saw Mr Platts & agreed to give him a bill at 2 months. At the Golden Fleece. Drank tea with C Cockrill. Called with H Hurry at Mr Websters & the Albion
A fine morning. Wind SW. Paid the Harmonies bill into Cr & Co & wrote to WBS. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined with H Hurry & C Cockrill. Spent the evening at the Albion

A fine smooth wind WSW. Went to sea with J H Richardson & landed at Cullercoats & walked home JHR Cockrill & H Hurry dined with me at ½ past 4. Attended the first meeting of the Tynemouth Musical Society in the evening at the George
A dull cloudy morning after much rain in the night. Wind NE. Turned out a most beautiful day. Went across the water with H Hurry. Dined with a party at the Albion. Called at πολ Jarvis
Most beautiful weather. Wind NW. Bathed this morning. Dined at home. At the Pig. Drank tea with C Cockrill. Walked to Tynemouth. At the Albion. Met Bess
A tremendous fall of rain all the morning, fear it will do much injury to the crops. Dined with I Tindley. Emma spent the day with Mrs Greenhow
Most delightful weather. Wind from the W changed with the heat of the day to SE. Bathed. Walked to Tynemouth. H Hurry took a rump steak with me. At Tynemouth again in evening

A dull but mild morning after a little rain. Wind SW. Bathed. The harvest began last week & is now very general in this country & good. Walked to Tynemouth & the sands. Dined at home at 2 o'clock. At H Hurry's in the evening. Met Bess
Most extraordinary fine harvest weather. Wind SW. Bathed again. Dined Yorkshire with C Cockrill at the Custom House. Walked up to Billy Mill in the afternoon
Fine weather. Wind SW very hot. Bathed. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined with & spent the afternoon with H Hurry. At the Albion in the evening
A continuance of beautiful weather. Wind NW & NE. H Hurry, Richardson & I went up to Newcastle by steam & dined with E Charlton at the Turf Hotel & returned in the evening. Called at the Albion.
Glorious weather. Very Hot. Wind NE. Dined with H Hurry at 4 o'clock. Walked to Tynemouth in the evening. At Southerns. Met Bess

A beautiful morning. Wind from the W but changed with the heat to E by S. Gave Metcalf & Dale a bill at 3 months on WBS for £20. Dined at home. In the afternoon J H Richardson, Hurry & I went to sea. At Tynemouth in the evening & finished at the Albion

Fine weather. Wind from the W and again changed with the heat to SE. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined with C Cockrill 7 H Hurry at 3 o'clock. Walked to Tynemouth again in the evening. At the Commercial with C Charlton. Wind changed to NW with rain 10aC
Been raining all night & still continues heavy. Wind changed to NNE. Received a letter from WBS. Dined at home. Had a glass of grog with H Hurry in the afternoon at the Albion. Met Bess
Fine weather. Wind NE. Wrote to WBS. J H Richardson & Hurry dined with me & we afterwards walked up to Billy Mill. Took tea & spent the evening with Holdroy's
Another extremely wet morning. A deluge of rain, cleared & turned out a fine afternoon. Wind varying between NW & NNE Dined with a large party at Mrs Reeds Emma spent the day at Mrs N Fenwicks
A dull morning after rain. Wind W by S. Turned out fine. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined with H Hurry. At Tynemouth again in the evening. At the Albion. Met Bess
A fine morning. Wind NW. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. At the Pig & at the Albion in the evening
Finer weather after a heavy rain from 6 o'clock yesterday evening. Wind WSW. Dined at home. H Hurry with me. Very wet. At the Albion in the evening. Met Bess, nothing
A dull morning. Wind from the W. Went to Newcastle by steam. Walked out with Dixon to Benton's. Met Dr Fenwick who went back & dined with us.
A most delightful day. Wind NE. Went with Mr Dixon to Benton Church. Walked about until dinner time when Mr Benley the evening joined us at dinner
Torrents of rain all night & the whole of the morning. Wind NE. Walked from Benton to the turnpike & got a gig to shields. Received a letter from WBS. Dined with J H Richardson. Met Bess
A dull morning. Wind N by E and rain during the day. Dined at home. Drank tea at C Cockrill's Took a walk in the evening & finished at the Albion & H Hurry's
Fine weather. Wind N by E. Called at Chapman. Took a long walk round by Tynemouth & Cullercoats & dined with H Hurry at 3 o'clock. The Corn not injured by the rain. At the Albion in the evening
Beautiful morning. Wind NW. Went over the water. Dined with C Cockrill & H Hurry at the Custom House. At Tynemouth in the evening the George & H Hurry

A cloudy morning after a little rain in the night & appearance of more. Wind SW. Walked to Tynemouth. C Cockrill & H Hurry dined with me at ¼ past 4 o'clock. Turned out a very wet evening. Went to meet Bess but not there

A dull cloudy morning. Wind E a little rain. Robert arrived at 5 O'Clock this morning from Togston for Emma & they left in the evening intending to stay all night at Newcastle & take the coach to Fillon. Went over the water but did not see Mr P Laing about C Harry's business. Left the papers with R Bowlby. Dined with J Tinley
A fine morning wind SW & SSE. Took a walk round by Cullercoat fields & Sands through Tynemouth, home to dinner. Wrote to WBS. At the Pig. At Tynemouth. Met Bess
A fine morning. Wind variable between SW & SE. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined with H Hurry at Tynemouth with cle
A cloudy morning. Wind SW. Dined with H Hurry. Took a walk round by Billy Mill, Preston & stopped at Tynemouth for the evening. Met Bess. Not well
A fine morning. Wind W. Walked to Cullercoat Sands. H Hurry dined with me. At Tynemouth in the evening. Suppered with HH
A fine morning. Wind SW. Dined at home. Met at the Albion at 6 o'clock & drew for the St ledge

Much rain last night. Now fine most rather cloudy. Wind WSW. Took a walk round by High Cheston. Dined at the Custom House. Attended the first monthly meeting of the Tynemouth Amateur Musical Society at the George. A musical company & performances good. Bess got the Cholera & dangerously ill
A fine morning. Wind WSW. Took a drive with the Doctor to Tynemouth & Carville & dined at the Goose & Gissrey Club at 3 o'clock. Finished at the abbey & πολ Jarvis
A dull damp morning & blowing fresh from the N by E. Heavy rain. Dined with H Hurry. At Jymesth in the evening. Finished at C Cockrill
A fine morning. Wind SE. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined with C Cockrill & H Hurry at 3 o'clock ay Jymesth again in the evening
A dull morning. Wind SE. Began to rain heavily after breakfast & never ceased all day. Dined at home. In the house all day.
A fine day. Received a letter from William & answered it. Walked to Tynemouth in the morning & evening. Dined with Mrs Tenley

Been heavy showers during the night & every appearance of more. Wind NE. Sat in the house till 12 o'clock. Dined at 3 o'clock with J Harrison at a house warming he gave at the "King Well". Stephenson Street a large party & finished at the Albion

A dull morning. Wind N by E. Went over the water, being the opening of the Stanhope railroad. When the commissioned loading a ship for the first time & with a new coal from ____. H Hurry dined with me. Rained in torrents the whole of the afternoon & evening. At the Albion
A fine day. Wind WNW. Walked to Tynemouth. J H Richardson & I dined with H Hurry. At the Albian

A dull damp morning & blowing hard NE. Received a letter from Mr Apedaile begging money & Merro. Done too much for them already, been ruined by my actions. Dined at house. Went in the evening to Billy Purvis' theatre. The bespeak of the Tynemouth Bachelors & a good house. At Southerns
