I hope he has left a world of misery & is now I trust happy with his dear parents. Remained in the house all day in consequence of this sad news. Wrote to WBS, Mr Vernon & D Dixon

A fine morning. Rather cool. Wind NW. In consequence of the account of J Galbraith's death, did not go to church. Dined at home. In the evening went & drank tea with J Tinley. Turned out a boisterous night.

A fine autumnal morning. Wind NW by W. Sea high upon the bar. Took a walk with mark & captain Webb round by Cullercoats. Held the annual meeting at newsrooms. Old Crofs discharged in consequence of his continued disgraceful & insolent conduct. Temple, Mr Lins Rell's late butler appointed in his place. Dined at home at 2 o'clock.

Fanny Smith arrived from Togston for a few days.

Paid Sabn to newsroom 30/.
A damp morning. Wind SW & blowing fresh. Walked out. Dined at home at 2 o'clock. Emma came from school for a few days. Spent the evening at home

A dull thick morning. Wind W by N. Received a letter from WBS. No account yet of the Hope's arrival. At the billiard room all the morning. Dined at home at 4 o'clock & spent the evening in the house. Paid Mrs Stephenson mom o £4 carpenter £2.5/- & cook £1.10/-

A foggy and wet morning. Wind WSW. At the news room & in the house all the morning. Received a notice from Brown of the George to quit in May. Called & told him I would not accept it. Dined at home at 2 o'clock. In the evening went to the whist club being a wet evening Tom Smith would not go. Wrote to Baker Galbraith

A dull morning. Blowing hard from the SE. Walked to Shields with Tom Smith. He set off for Togston, being such an unpleasant morning. Fanny remained. Dined at home at 2 o'clock. Took wine with H Harry & J Cunningham at the Commercial.

A thick & very damp morning, having been a great deal of rain. Wind South. Fanny Smith left for Togston. Dined with Boswell on board the William Shard. Mark, H Harry & Richardson took wine with us. Spent a pleasant day.
A fine weather. Wind WNW. Engaged painting ship. Several ships sailed for the Baltic. Dined at home
A very wet day. Wind N & NE. Went to church in the morning. Dined at home. Boswell & I took wine & tea with H Harry. At the Mulstrum in the evening.

A rainy morning. After a stormy night. Wind variable N by W. N & NE & a heavy sea upon the bar. Wrote to WBS & sent him an account of rents. Received a letter from him of the arrival of the Hope at Gravesend. Dined at 5 o'clock at J Tinley's. William & H Metcalf, H Dale, Mr Gosling, R A J. Wright jn & Mr Duncan from Liverpool there. A very pleasant party.
A damp, thick morning. Wind NW & cold. Dined with Bill Wright on board the Stephen. J Wright jr & Mr Hawks, H French, Mr Wright, Mr Watt, Mr Hobroyd, Mr Hall & myself.

A fine morning. Rather frosty. Wind NW. Received a letter from WBS. Mrs Scott very unwell. Dined with Boswell on board the William Shand. Mark, H Harry, Richardson & myself there. Spent a very pleasant day.

A very fine frosty morning. Wind WNW. Took a walk with Boswell to Tyneside. Dined at home at 2 o'clock. Mark, H Harry& I had some brandy & water together. Afterwards attended the whist club. With Bell Jerves.
Another fine frosty morning. Wind about West. An idle day with me. Dined at home at 2 o'clock. Boswell & I spent the evening with Allen.

A rainy morning. Wind NW by N. Received a letter from WBS with a bank post bill for £50. Went to church.

The wind suddenly changed to NE blowing very hard with heavy showers.

Dined at home. H Harry & Boswell came in & took wine with me. Wrote to WBS. At the Mulstrum in the evening.

A dull morning. Wind E by N blowing fresh & a heavy sea upon the bar. Paid accounts Chapman £50 to Cm of my account & paid by diss upon them Premium Club bill £25.12.6 & average Hope club £5.10.5. Dined at home. Went to a lobicst party in the evening at Mr Harrison's

Been blowing very hard all night from ESE & still continues nearly the same about E by S with a heavy sea upon the bar but clear weather & exceedingly cold. Dined at home & afterwards went on board the Choice & had some punch with H Harry. The wind increased to a heavy gale. Drank tea with Miss Harry & spent the evening with mark

A very stormy morning & a heavy gale of wind at E by N with sleet showers & been so all night. Increased to a perfect hurricane with a most tremendous sea. Dined at home. H Harry, H Nicolson, Boswell & I had some punch at the Commercial.
A beautiful mild weather. Wind WSW. The Grenville bay sailed for Greenland Dined at Mrs Banks

Weather more moderate & sea much fallen. Wind SE. Dined at home. Had some punch on board the Unanimity with H Nicholson. Attended the card club & had some oysters in the evening with H Harry at Jane Moors.
A dull morning. Thick weather. Wind NW. Drew £5 out of Chapmans. Dined at home. H Harry, Boswell, Nicholson & I took grog together at the Commercial & afterwards went to the theatre

A thick dull morning with a little rain. Wind about north. Allen & I took a walk to Tynemouth. Government having given up the burial ground to the parish again, excepting 40 feet round the sides of the yard. Dined at home.

Spent the evening with Mr Lewison, H Harry, and A Nicholson at the Duke of York.

A foggy and damp morning. Wind SW. Received a letter from Stephenson of the Hope being out on Saturday having delivered 279 loads 49 feet of timber equal to 320 loads with deals of broken stowage.

Took Emma to church with me. Dined at home & afterwards took wine with Boswell. H Harry & Allen there.

In the evening at mother Maxwell's
Finer weather. Wind SW. Received a letter from William. Dined with H Harry on board the Choice. A pleasant party.

A dull & damp morning. Wind S. Afterwards got to SE blowing very hard towards night with heavy rain. Mrs Scott so unwell obliged to keep her bed & not able to see any person. Dined at home. Drank tea & spent the evening at J Tinley's

Another damp & unpleasant morning. After a stormy night, a heavy sea upon the bar. Wind SE.

Dined at home. At another max with Catherine. In the evening went to South Shields to Mr Bullocks & partook of an oyster supper & milk. Punch with H Harry, Boswell, Allen & J Richardson. The oysters very large & fine, from Wells

A very unpleasant damp morning. Wind about south with a heavy sea upon the bar. Two ships have got upon the rock in entering the harbour. Dined at home. Mr Allen came & took wine with me. In the evening attended the whist club.

Finer weather but still rather foggy & dull. Wind S & S by E. The Qurnoury belonging to Messrs Young son got upon the rocks last night. Allen & I walked round by Tynemouth & the rocks to see them. Dined at home. Boswell treated H Nicholson & me to some punch at the Mulstrum, it being his last night at Shields
Fine weather. Wind SW. Sea fallen. Received a letter from WBS enclosing £50 BK post bill. Wrote to WBS paid the £50 bill into Chapmans. Dined at home. With Ann Stokes in the evening.
Mild weather. Wind NNW. Dined with J Tenley to meet Cambell & Alloa of the 4th Regiment. A fantastic dinner. A letter from William
A fine morning. Wind SSW. Attended morning service at the Church. Walked in the afternoon with J Tinley & his boys to Tynemouth & afterwards dined with him.

Fine weather, rather frosty. Wind SW & SSW. The Hope arrived safe last night at 11 o'clock. Determined upon laying her up & therefore took her off risk in the Premium & Hope Clubs. Gave Stephenson £20 to pay wages. The William Shand, Mr Boswell sailed today for Ryes to take on passengers for New York. A great many colliers also got to sea. Dined with the Committee of the ____ & in the evening went to the theatre, it being the bespeak of the Bachelors of North Shields.
Another fine day & frosty. Wind WNW. On board the Hope all the morning. The people busy unrigging. Mr Allen & I dined on board. Took wine and spent the evening at J Tinley's. Mr Temple there.

A fine seasonable morning & a hard frost. Wind SW. On board the Hope all the morning, where I dined. Hauled her upon Platty ways to get upained in the safe port etc. Drank tea with H Harry & went to the theatre at half price, it being the Officers bespeak.

A cold frosty morning. Wind WSW. On board the Hope. One man at work replacing the after raftports. Paid Walker block maker £8.13/- for making new mainmast in 1828 outfit. H harry & I walked up to Tynemouth & had some whiskey toddy with J Cunningham & afterwards attended the whist club.
A very fine morning & hard frost. Wind SW. On board the Hope. The carpenter still employed at the raftport. Dined at home. Mrs Dixon down to see Mrs Scott.
Milder weather & wind SW. Been blowing a gale all night. On board the Hope. At ½ past 12 o'clock went by steam to Newcastle. Met Dixon there & walked with him out to Benton to dine & stay all night.

A fine mild day. Wind SW. Dixon & Bessy went to church. I walked down to Walker & called upon Mr & Mrs Carr, there being no steam boats. I proceeded & walked to Shields, afterwards to Tynemouth & back & dined with J Tinley. With Bell Wait
A dull foggy morning. Wind SW. On board the Hope. H Harry with me. Examined her stern inside & all appeared sound & good. Dined at home. Suppered with H Harry.
A beautiful morning. Wind NW. Took a walk to Tyneside & had a warm bath. Dined at home. With Bell Jarvis in the evening at the Mulstrum
A cloudy morning. Went to Newcastle. Mr Proctor could give me no information about the Ariel. Walked home to dinner. Wrote to William
A fine frosty morning. Wind WNW. On board the Hope. The after raftport nearly finished. Dined with H Harry. With Bell Jarvis in the evening

A frosty morning. Rather foggy. Wind WSW. Took a long walk with Captain Webb round Cullercoats, Tynemouth. Dined at home. Wrote to Boswell at Refe informing him of the odesoan freights being £4 per ton & 10 pct for tullers. At the whist club & with Bell Jarvis

A fine frosty morning. Wind NNW. On board the Hope. The carpenter's busy with the stern bolling. The timber ends etc & going to put in another hook, having finished the after raftport. Drew £5 cash out of Chapmans. Dined at home. Spent the evening with Allen. Paid E Reed's mother £2.9 the balance of his wages. Turned out a very wet night.
A dull damp morning, having been a heavy fall of rain & hail during the night. Wind WNW. Dined at home. Drank tea with Allen & spent the evening at home.
A damp raw morning. Wind SE by E. received a letter from WBS with Hope's freight account. Stayed in the house all day, having a swelled face

A thick frost morning. Wind SW by W. Paid the washerwoman for a quarter washing £1.11.6. On board the Hope. The carpenter busy fixing the new hook at the stern. Dined at home. At the billiard room in the afternoon. In the evening at home.

A foggy damp and very unpleasant morning. Some snow on the ground, having fallen during the night. Wind, the little there is NNW. Dined at 4 o'clock at Mr Metcalf's in Saville Street. A party there. Spent a pleasant day. Wrote to William. Called at the Bank. Spencer promised to under me what accommodation I may want this Xmas. Paid Linskill & etc £24.11.6 for cordage & Lane & Spence & Foster £8.10/- for canvas

A frosty morning. Wind East. H Harry went with me on board the Hope to give me his advice with regard to the repairs. Found they had taken the broken hold beam out & preparing a new one. Ordered several new knees to be put in. Dined at home & spent the evening

A cold frosty morning. Wind E by N. Been blowing a gale all night. A heavy sea upon the bar. On board the Hope. The master & carpenter absent looking for some knees for the hold beans. Dined at home. H Harry came in & took wine with me. Mrs Dixon down & took Emma to Benton with her. Attended the whist club in the evening. Saw Ann Maxwell
Xmas day. Seasonal weather. Very cold with a little snow. Wind East & blowing hard. Walked up to Benton. Dined & remained all night.

Again at Newcastle. Saw J Smith Senior & Junior: the old gent: very kind, asked me to dine, "no go" entered upon the subject of the Ariel, showed them W S Brewer's accounts, they seemed to be of our opinion & against any arbitration. Dined with Dixon, had a long conversation about his assisting me. He was extremely kind in his expressions, but said it was out of his power, from his heavy advances to others & having heavy payments to make himself to but that he would consider about it. memo: Its what I expected, not much disappointed. A promise ought to be held sacred. Cold day with rain afternoon
A dull cloudy morning. Wind NNW. At church in the morning with Fanny Smith Walked to Tynemouth in the afternoon with J Tenley. Dined at home

A fine frosty morning. Wind ESE. A slight fall of snow during the day. Walked into Newcastle with Dixon. Nothing doing on the Quay side in the way of freights, at least none to suite me. Returned to Shields in a gig. Dined at home. In the evening attended the whist club at H Dales. Received a letter from Boswell from Rye informing me he had got 90 passengers for New York

A fine seasonal morning. Wind NW & snowing heavy. Did not go to church. Made up the Hope's final voyage in the ships log. She clears nothing much to my unsurprised & disappointment. Dined with H Harry. In the evening with Bell Jarvis & Jane Dryden.

A continuance of frost, but not yet much snow has fallen. Wind NW. On board the Hope. The carpenter nearly finished. Intend hauling her off the shore at high water. Dined at home.

Mary Carss called upon me.

H Harry, Mark & I had a glass of grog together. Spent the evening at home.

A dull winters morning. Frost gone, having been rain during the night. Wind E by S but still cold.

Attended a meeting at the church to take into consideration the offer of the board of ordinance either to purchase the burial ground at Tynemouth or give a piece of ground in lieu of it. The meeting determined not to do either, but to let the Board apply to Parliament for an act to take it from us, which they had threatened to do. Dined at home. In the evening H Harry, H Nicolson & I had a glass of grog at the George together

Rather a dull morning. Inclined to freeze. Wind E by S. Drew £5 out of Chapmans. On board the Hope. Carpenter nearly finished laying the half deck. H Harry & Nicolson lunched on board. Dined at home. Received a letter from WBS & answered it In the evening H Nicholson & I called to see jane Mills. With Jane Dryden

The wind continuing from the SE makes it appear as if there was not much if any frost. Though some snow has fallen during the night.

The last day of the year, which has been to me anything but a prosperous one. I trust I may be more fortunate the next one. I know not what will become of me. It appears to me my destiny is fixed & that I'm never to rise in the world again.

Walked to Cullercoats & saw the fishing boats come in having been successful. The fish very firm, particularly the haddock. There were 16 boats. Dined at home. Attended the whist club & sat the new year in.

Highlights

1830-01-24 Mrs Scott falls out of bed and breaks her leg

1830-07-13 JSR witnessed an accident which killed a girl sitting under cliffs

Seasonal weather but not very severe. Wind WNW. Walked again to Cullercoats & saw them land their fish which were remarkably fine. Dined at home. In the evening Cunningham, Nicolson, & I went to the Duke of York & drank a jug of punch. In the evening at the Mulstrum & with Bell Jervis

A cold morning rather inclined to thaw. Wind NW. J Tinley drove me to Newcastle but could do nothing for the Hope. The Colliers being still off work. Returned with J Tinley & dined with him. In the evening attended the whist club at H Harry's
A fine day. Wind W by N. Got a warp and buoy rope from Linskill House Dined at home. Took wine & spent the evening with W C Wright

A fine morning having been a frost in the night. Wind NW. Went to church in the morning. Received a letter from WBS & answered it. Walked with Mr Lens Kills & J Tinley to Tynemouth Lodge & afterwards to Tynemouth with J Tinley. Dined with him. Mark came in after dinner.

Mild weather. Frost gone. Wind WNW. Walked up to the Point with H Harry, H Nicholson & J Elder & dined with Mr Sadler. In the evening went up to Newcastle to see Duncan. Had an oyster supper afterwards & got home at about 2 o'clock in the morning
A beautiful morning. Wind NW. Walked with Mark to Cullercoats & saw the boats come in. Returned home to dinner. Spent the evening at J Tinleys
A dull morning & rather damp after a frosty night. Wind W by S. Dined at home. At the billiard table in the afternoon & spent the evening at home.

A dull morning & fresh weather. Wind about north, been blowing hard all night, sea coming on. Received a letter from WBS. Took a walk with a party to Cullercoats. Dined at home. In the evening at the whist club.

The country covered with snow Which has been very heavy during the night. Wind north. Dined at home. H Harry, Nicholson, H French & I drank wine together at the George & afterwards went to the theatre to see West of the 80th regiment perform Fredrick in Lover's Vows. He got on tolerably well for a first attempt.
A fine morning. Wind WNW. Thawing after a slight frost during the night. Very sloppy & unpleasant. Walked to Cullercoats. Dined at home. In the evening attended the whist club at Craigs

It has been a hard frost & blowing a gale at north all night & still continues with a very high sea. Went to church in the morning. Dined at 2 o'clock with H Harry. Mr Sadler there. In the evening at the Mulstrum
Been a slight frost in the night with a little snow. Wind NNW. Mrs Dixon brought Emma home. Dined at home. Spent the evening at J Tinleys

Last night very stormy. A gale from the NE with heavy showers of sleet & hail.

Received a letter in the name of the Bank, but evidently written by that little puppy F Chapman without consulting his partners, desiring me to pay the balance of my account with them of some £106. Called & saw Spence who seemed ignorant of such a letter having been written. Told him what I thought of such conduct. I having ample security in their hands.

Dined at home. At the Duke of York with Mr Hewson, Nicholson, Cunningham & Wheatley. Received of newsroom £3.10/- for WBD

A fine mild day. Wind SSW. The surveyors of the British & Hope clubs on board They thought we ought to get a new mainstay sail & that we ought also to have a new towline. Bound two boys E Read for 6 years at £45 & G Floss for 3 years at 30. Dined on board & went to a party at W C Wrights in the evening. Paid Gibson butchers £8.7/ & Hall £3.13/- & self cash £5

A fine dry winters morning. Rather frosty & blowing fresh at NE. Dined at home. H Harry, Mr Hewson, Nicholson & I had a glass of grog together at the Duke of York. A stormy night, a hurricane with snow.
Still blowing a gale of wind after an awfully stormy night with snow showers. Wind E by S. Dined at home. In the evening at the whist club

A very unpleasant morning. Heavy rain & blowing fresh at E by S & sea high upon the bar.

Received a letter from WBS to receive some £88 from Mr Salmon of South Shields. Wrote to him. Dined at home. At the theatre in the evening. The last performance for the season.

A dull rainy morning. A few light ships in light wind E by S & sea fallen. Went over the water & saw Salmon who had not this money ready for me, but expects to give it this next week. Dined at home. Wrote to WBS. Attended the whist club at Jebbs. Walked there. A stormy night.
Another dull & rainy morning. Wind ESE. A few light ships off. Went to church in the morning. Dined at home. H Nicholson took wine with me. In the evening at the Mulstrum.

A fine morning & hard frost. Wind WSW. The frost continued very keen throughout the day. Went to Newcastle by steam. Things very dull. Could get nothing for the Hope. Dined at home at 5 o'clock. In the evening Nicholson & I had a glass of grog together at the Duke of York.
A beautiful morning & very intense frost. Been a little snow in the night. Wind NW. Took a walk to Tynemouth with Captain Webb. Dined at home. At the Commercial with Brown & Newton

A continuance of very severe frost. Wind fresh at ESE. A large fleet of light ships coming in. Dined at home. In the afternoon a heavy snow storm, turned in the evening to a thaw with sleet & rain very wet & sloppy. Spent the evening at J Tinley's. A ship got upon the Heard Sand at night.

A continuance of thaw but finer weather. Wind WNW. Dined at home. With a party at the Duke of York in the afternoon. At the whist club in the evening. Received a letter from WBS Paid an average £20.2.6

A continuance of fresh weather & been blowing very hard all night from the SE. One ship has got upon the Heard Sand, another upon the rocks & two riding off the Bar. One having cut away her masts & the other with main mast gone. Both these ships & the one on the Heard Sand got into the harbour. Walked to Tynemouth with Nicholson & Cunningham. Dined at home. In the evening H harry, Nicholson & I went to the Duke of York where we found Mr Heweson
A fine day but blowing very fresh from WNW. Dined at J Tenleys
A dull morning with rain. Still blowing fresh from S by E. Dined at home. Attended the whist club in the evening at Drury's

A very unpleasant raw damp morning. Wind SSE

A serious accident has befallen Mrs Scott. This morning having fallen off the bed & broken her thigh. It is only a simple fracture & having got it set immediately, she is suffering as little pain as could possibly be expected. Wrote to Mrs Dixon to come down immediately. Sent a messenger off to Togston. Dined at J Tinleys. Met Mr Mark there. At the Mulstrum

A beautiful morning. Wind NW. Took a walk round by Tynemouth & the rocks to see the wreck. Mrs Smith & Fanny arrived in the afternoon. Dined at 4 o'clock. Mrs Scott not so well this evening. Called at Messes Marsh & saw Emma, she having had a cold.

A fine morning & hard frost. Wind about west. Mrs Scott has had a bad night & is very sick and ill. Walked with D Dixon round by the rocks to Tynemouth & afterwards to Benton by the river & Wellington. Dined there & staid all night.
A fine frosty morning. Wind SW. Left Benton after breakfast & walked down to Shields. Mrs Scott considered a little better. Dined at home at 3 o'clock. Spent the evening at the billiard room

A beautiful winter's morning & a sharp frost. Wind NW. On board the new ship "William Green" built by Mr Smith at St Peters of 600 tons as from a vessel as fine a vessel as was ever built, to sail this evening. Walked to Tynemouth. Mrs Dixon down to see Mrs Scott. Dined at home & in the evening attended the whist club.

Another fine morning & a very intense frost. Wind about west. Walked with H Nicholson to the Ridges at High Cherton. Had a little scaling, soon tired. Walked round by Tynemouth. Returned to dinner at 3 o'clock. In the evening walked again to Tynemouth & took wine, played a rubber & suppered with Mr Brown & a party at the Star & Garter. Not my favourite. Got home at 1 o'clock. Frost again & a very wet night.

A damp morning. Wind NE. Went to the newsroom, read the papers. Dined at home at 9 o'clock. Spent the afternoon at the billiard room. Wind suddenly changed to SE. Blowing fresh. Attended the whist club at J Tinleys

A fine winter's morning. Frosty with snow. Wind SW. Prevented attending church in the morning. The Smiths coming down so late to breakfast. Wrote to B B Galbraith. Walked to Tynemouth in the afternoon with J Tinley& C Milner. Attended afternoon service & afterwards dined at the castle with west of the 80th. In the evening at the Mulstrum.

A cold winters day, Wind fresh at about East with Showers of snow. Attended the sale Of the Glattons stores upon the Low Lights Quay. Brought a Capstan for £3.1. and 23 faths of 1 3/16 mock chain quite new at 17/6 a cwt. Played a few pools at billiards W Peast H Nickolson and all at the Duke of York in the evening.

A countenance of winter weather, very cold. Been blowing a gale all night with snow showers A heavy sea upon the bar. Wind E.S.E Dined at home. At 3 o'clock at the billiard room in the afternoon. In the evening called and sat an hour or two with Mark, he having had a severe loin attack

Still very cold and frosty and A good deal of snow on the ground Wind about East blowing fresh. Received from Robert and paid into Chapmans £86 rents. Gave Mrs Scott a draft for her quarter annuity £75. Mrs Dixon down I returned with her in the carriage to Barton. Dined & stayed all night.

A fine morning (wind NW), Frosty with a show of showers. After Breakfast Dixon & I had the beagles out & started above base which We left them running & walked Into Newcastle & not being able to get anything for the Hope, I got into a gig & came down to Shields Dined with the whist club at the Commercial, spent a pleasant day In the evening at the Card club and Afterwards at the Mulstrum

A continuum of Winter weather with snow showers Wind East S E blowing fresh. Stayed at home at 2 o'clock at the billiard room after dinner. After tea walked upto Tynemouth & spent the evening with Capt French at the Castle. Played a few rubbers at whist & lost
A fine day. Wind S.W. & keen frost. Walked to Cullercoats Dined at home. In the evening the whist Club. Tea at Mr N Finwicks

A most inferior frost Wind S.W. Received a letter from WBS Went to church in the morning Dined at home at ½ past 1 o'clock. In the evening at the Duke of York With T Nicholson and afterwards at the Neuls home. This evening a caped this commenced with rain

The thaw continues & the snow has disappeared. Blowing a gale of wind at WNW. Went by Dunn's coach to Newcastle Fixed the Hope for the Bursaton Walls to be loaded on Monday. Gave Stephenson orders to lay her the shore line. Dined at home at 3 then took wine with I Craig & afterwards spent the evening At Tynemouth Castle with Captain French of The 80th. A large Hulk sailed today. Ann Maxwell delivered of a fine boy

A beautiful morning and Mild weather. Wind SW. A great deal Of ice in the river. Walked up to the Ship. & dine at the annual dinner of the Great Premium Club. Reduced my insurance in at to £500 & paid £500 into the eligibles. Mrs Scott very ill
A fine day and frosty The Hope upon the shore to see Ivo Karl. The people busy rigging. Dinner at home. Spent the evening At J Teschays. My birthday

A frosty morning. Very cold Wind SW. Got the Hope down to her loading birth & surveyed by Smiths foreman for the club. Excepting two hold beam Knees which are rather decayed, he saw no fault to find. People busy rigging. H Nicholson & I dined on board. Attended the Whist Club in the evening. Wrote to WBS
A continuance of fine weather. Wind NW. Walked out to Whitley Park in the morning. Dined at home. A letter from William & answered it. At the whist club in the evening
A dull soft morning Wind SSE. Dined at home. At the billiard room in the afternoon at the Duke of York & at the Maltbeam in the evening

A fine day. Wind about SW. On board the Hopes & engaged looking for a Kedger getting but the beef at 4 o'clock. Dined with I Tiney & at the Whist Club in the evening at Mr Richmounds The Hope got these Rich

A beautiful spring morning. Wind SW. Went to church Mr Mark & the vicar dest the duty. Dined at home at 1 o'Clock. H Harry, H French Nicholson & I walked to Tynemouth round the castle & took wine at the Star & Garter In the evening at the Mulstrum

Another beautiful morning & quite mild wind about north. On board the Hope only got J Kuls down Today. Dined at home. Mrs Dixon down to See Mrs Scott. Drank tea at home & in The evening at the George with H Harry & Wrote to WBS

A delightful morning & frosty. Wind mild. On board the Hope When she finished her loading leffering in 16 Kule & 5 Char. Attended the annual meeting of the eligible & afterwards and dined with Placaad & spend a pleasant day. In the evening with Bell Jervis

A fine morning Rather frosty wind fresh at NW. Got up at 7 o'clock and went on board the Hope. The pilot on board but decided to not venture to take her out, it being in bad tide & threw feet sea upon the bar. Received a letter from WBS & one from Tom Lee. Answered Tom Lees. Dined at home & spent the afternoon at the billiard table. In the evening, heavy rain & wind to NNE. At the Duke of York with H Harry & Nicholson
A frosty morning wind NW. A sea upon the bar which will prevent the Hope getting out. Dined at home In the evening at the Whist Club.

A course frost. Wind NNW & blowing fresh & although the sea was breaking upon the bar, several small ships ventured out & some were literally smothered in the surf, but all got out safe. Dined with I Readhead on board the Nautalus At the billiard room in the afternoon. Drank tea at home & in the evening With Bode Jerois & afterwards at the Duke Of York

A continuance of frost Wind NW. Got up early & went by stream to Newcastle; had a heavy snow storm Returned to dinner at 1 o'clock. Emma G with us. Mrs Dixon came to see Mrs Scott Not water sufficient for the Hope to get to sea. Attended the Whist Club at Allans in the evening

xx

A fine frosty morning Been a delightful fall of snow in the night. Blowing fresh at NWW. Attended morning Service; a collection was made for the singers £9.6 received. Dined at home. Being a fine sea tide a great many ships got to sea among them the Hope. Dined at home & went to afternoon service. Afternoon walked to Tynemouth In the evening at the Duke of York
D Brown Spouts & heavy ballast £2.12. Fine weather but rather frosty. Wind WNW. Dined at home. Gave captain Stephenson £2. Received from Scott for spars £4.14/- & allowance for ballast 19/2

A countenance of severe frost. & NW wind. Payed 5/- for the Hope's foy boat. Having a cold & Pain in my side, took physician & remained in the house. Dined at home At the billiard room in the afternoon & spent the evening at home.

A dull weather morning Having been a great deal of snow during the night but now a thaw Wind SE. Several light vessels off the harbour. Dined at home. At the billiard room in the afternoon & spent the evening at home.

A dull morning. Wind W by N Went to South Shields & saw Salmon who was not persuaded to give in the money, but promised to send it over tomorrow. Dined at home. In the afternoon at the billiard room & spent the evening at home

A fine mild morning. Wind W by S. Received a note from T Young demanding the return upon the note. Called upon him, not at home. Dined at home. In the evening at the Whist Club. Received a letter from Salmon enclosing a draft for £88.9.3 Dated 11th March for Mrs Ghireson's Estate

A beautiful spicy morning. Very mild wind NSW. Saw I Young & told him I could not pay him this just at present. Walked out to Billy Hill to see the Hassiers, no sport. Dined at home. At the billiard room In the afternoon. Suppered with H Harry
A delightful morning Blowing hard at West. Dined at home. In the evening at Whist Club at A Metcalfe
A mild morning Rather dull; been a great deal of rain in the night. Wind NW. Went to church in the morning. A rainy afternoon. Dined with I Judy At the Mulstream
A dull thick morning Wind SSW. Took physic & stayed in the house all the morning. Mrs Dixon & Tom Smith down to see Mrs Scott On board the Brodnick with R Peach & in the evening at the Duke of York
A delightful spring day, quite warm weather. Went up to Newcastle by stream. The Courts so crowded could not get in. Dined & stayed all night with D Dixon Tom Smith & Hnoises there

Another beautiful Day. Wind SW. Returned to Shields by stream early with the intention of going back to help them but changed my mind & dined at home. On board the Choice in the afternoon with A Harry & A Nicholson & at the Mulstream at night
A beautiful morning, but cold & frosty. Walked to Newcastle everything very dull, little or nothing doing. Returned in the steam boat. Dined at home. Wind NNW
Most extraordinary Fine weather. Wind about South. Took a walk with A Nicholson round by Preston & Tynmouth. Dined with A Harry on board the Choice & in the Evening at the Whist Club

Another fine morning, rather Frosty. Wind SW. Sent an answer to Mr Anderson's letter. Hope Club stating the Hope being laid up between 20 Dec & 20 Feb Went with H Harry & the H Pemberton of Quebec to Sunderland. Called upon Capt Bunbury of the 80th Regiment & returned to dine with H Harry at 5 o'clock A small party to mubt Mrs Pemberton. attended Mrs Heddill's evening party. Received a letter from WBS confirming the of the sale of the Hope's cargo at 29/6 A miserable price, about 6/6 pecght Shall lose I dare say between £30 & £40

A duller foggy morning. Wind SW. Afterwards got to the L&E Cold accompanied Took a walk with Captain Webb to Tynemouth. Dined with Nicholson a party spent a very Pleasant day & in the evening Attended the Whist Club at I Dales

A foggy morning. Wind NE. Afterwards changed to SE & fine clear weather. Went to Church in the morning. Mr Pemberton accompanied me. I was engaged to dine with I Tealey today but on my return from Church. I found that Mrs Scott was so much poorer & her death expected every moment. I sent an apology. She expired precisely at 9 o'clock without a struggle
A fine morning. Rather Frosty. Wind SSW. Emma G came From school. Mrs Dixon down & Took Emma to N Coatts with her. Wrote to WBS: BBG: & A Deighera of Mrs Scotts death. Kept the house all day.
A cold morning. Rather Frosty. Wind S by W. In the house All day

Dull & thick weather & rather cold. Blowing fresh at NSW. Mr & Mrs Dixon & I Smith came down today for the purpose of having Mrs Scott's will read & which not a little surprised all of us, a more extraordinary one perhaps never was: By it I am left the very handsome legacy of £10 !!! the same to my brother, plainly proving & confirming what her feelings towards us throughout life must have been, inveterately bad, & carried to the grave with her. Peace go with her. I forgive her For all the mischief & misery she Has caused in our family. The party left us in the afternoon.

A fine day but blowing hard from about west. Received at the bank for Salmon's debt £88.9.3 for WBS & deducted from it 20/- for my trouble & £11.6 money lent to Bob Marsh & sec by WBS in London. Dined with I Finley, being less Of the confinement to the house. Received a letter from WBS

Beautiful weather, but very windy at West. Received a letter from ABS in reply to their informing him of Mrs Scott's death, saying he cannot leave London before tonight or tomorrow morning Dined at home. Wes & Fanny Smith excessively angry that we should claim the amount of taxes upon the house paid by us in error & which ought to have been paid by Mrs Scott. Fanny inclined to be very violent, her conduct disgusting & very insulting; displaying more regard for the money than for the aunt. Blew a perfect hurricane with heavy rain the afternoon
A fine morning, but still Blowing very hard at NW. In the house All day
A fine clear frosty morning & cold. Wind NNW. Showers of sleet & rain in the afternoon. Attended morning service. Dined at home. Carlea Sunday

A cool morning & blown very hard all day at west. Of course in the house. Fanny Smith again exceedingly violent today. More so than before & insulting. Than I was obliged to speak to her in a way that had the effect of making her silent. Wonder ? Be at opposite William BS did not arrive until after 11 o'clock having called & stopped a short time in Westgate Street. Went to bed from after his arrival.

A very wet morning, wind SE Afterwards changed to SW & blowing fresh with fine weather. Brought a large fleet down amongst them the Hope. Dixon & his aid Tom Smith Mrs Yellowley & Emma came down to attend the funeral which took place between 12 & 1 o'clock. Captain Caudisson of the 80th Regiment kindly allowing the hearse and carriages to enter the castle ...

... yard. Mrs Scott's remains placed in the vault above my father. Fanny Smith more violent than ever. Her conduct most disgusting & indecent. Dixon Mrs B & Mr Gallowley returned to Newcastle. Tom Smith accompanied

A fine morning. Wind NW & rather cold. Tom Smith, his mother & Fanny left us for Foyston & fortunately without any more unpleasantness. After they left us the weather changed & we had a very stormy day, heavy showers of snow Was & I had the servants up & told them of our plans. Robert agreed to remain with me, also Leadbetter. Hutchison of course leaves us, but will stay in the house until she gets a situation or I wish her to leave. Stephenson has been at NCastle but could obtain nothing for the Hope only 8/6 pecght offering. Ordered Him to unbind the sails. Gave him a draft upon Chapman for £20 to pay wages. At home all the evening

A dull showery day. Wind fresh at NW. Engaged at home in the house with ABS. I gave him his note at 40 days for £75.10/- Accepted & returned Mrs Bulemer a bill at 3 hours. Due 23 pricing for Policy presumably almost £16.13.8 Dined at home. At 5 o'clock the owner & Master of the Commerce with me about the damages received by him in the wold when the Hope came in contact, agreed to leave it to two gentlemen to decide with have to call in a this. At home all the evening

A very boisterous day. Blowing hard at N & NNW but fine weather. Payed E Ried apprentice ¼ years ways £1.8.9 & also Jeaslop the balance of his ¼ wages £1.3.9 & advanced him 16/3 = £2 Nman & Leng aged all the moral with Robert Taking due account of the wine in the cellar. Mary Carts called & in consequence of Mr Wrights bad conduct to her with whose children she was governess, we asked her to come and stay with us, until she goes to her situation as governess to a school in Newcastle. Dined at home at 2 o'clock. Paid into chapmans WBS; note for £75 Miss Emma & I took a walk round by Cullercoats Sands & came home to tea. At the whist club in the evening.

Another boisterous day blowing a hurricane at about W by N Walked up to the Hope. Dined at home. After dinner went to the George to settle the damage done to the Commerce of Whitby referred it to A French & H Walker who awarded the owner of the Commerce (Mr Wood) £4 which I paid him. After which we had A few bottles of port. At the Mulstrum house in the Evening
A fine morning but blowing fresh at WNW. Norman & I went by steam to Newcastle. Called at Dixons, Mr Loathinby's for the Dined & stayed all night at Dixons

A dull morning Wind WNW. After breakfast & having some conversation with Dixon respecting the will Fanny Smith consort to be embarked on board a steamer & got to DSguases about of ½ past 1 o'clock & had our dinner; found Mary Cary there, having got down the night before
A fine day blowing fresh at SW. Paid my washerwoman £1.11.6 for one quarter washing Dined at home. Emma returned to school A Harry A Nicholson R Peach & I took wine together at the George
A cold frosty day. Wind NNE & a sea upon the bar. Dined at home. Went in the evening to hear a lecture by Martin the self-styled natural philosopher
A fine morning after a windy & rainy night blowing fresh at W by W On board the Hope. Sent the filtering machine on shore to be repaired. Dined at home

Fine weather wind WNW. Blowing fresh Dined on board the Cluanicucty with A Nicholson, A Harry, French & I Wright There. Attended a meeting at the Northumberland circus raspectary the Customs House & approved his departure to proceed to London
A dull morning but mild & calm wind West by South. Dined at home. In the evening at the whist club
A fine morning blowing fresh at NW. Paid I Young £30.6 puts. Dined at home at 2 o'clock. In the afternoon on board the Brodanick

A beautiful morning, quite seasonal weather. Wind NW Took a long walk with Mrs Marg Carf & Emma G (round Cullercoats & Tynmouth) Dined at home. Attended the whist club. In the evening at Dr Drawings. Paid I Elden £1.10. on averafer

Most extraordinary weather uncommonly fine & warm. Wind West. Went to church in the morning Dined at ½ push 1 o'clock walked to Tynemouth with A Nicholson & W French & the same party in the evening has castins & ale at the Duke or York
Another delightful morning wind W by N. Mrs Sharp called upon Mary Carfs from Sheffield to dinner & spent the evening. H Nicholson sailed for keil
Rather a dull morning. Wind ENE. Dined with a party at H Harrys invitation at Roddany & spent a pleasant day
A fine morning. Wind WNW bun a great day of dunny this night. Wind and off to the NE & very cold. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined with the vicar a pleasant day.
A fine morning but still very cold & wind NE. Sea upon the bar. Dined at home. Captain Webb spent the evening with us
Returned to Shields from Newcastle by steam. A miserable wet cold & boisterous day. Wind SE. Dined with J Tenley. By my own invitation, to inform him what passed with Dixon

Beautiful weather & exceedingly warm. Wind NNE. Dined at J Tenleys & attended the ball in the evening. Spent a very agreeable evening & suppered at ardold Hutchinson's. Mrs Decghton died this evening after a short illness
A cold frosty morning wind NE heavy showers of snow during the day. Dined at home. On board the choice in the afternoon. A stormy night

A stormy morning with heavy showers of snow. A great deal having fallen during the night. Wind ENE. Dined at home. Emma G: came from school to us. In the evening attended the whist club at Mrs Creigs. And asked the club to come to me on Thursday

A fine frosty morning wind NW. Emma Mary Carfs & went to church. Heard a funeral sermon from Mr Mark who held the service. The Vicars father being dead & also young Mrs Read he died in London of the gout in the head & after two days illness. Dined at home & afternoon walked with H Henry to Tynemouth. In the evening at news room & H Harry's
Another frosty morning blowing fresh at NW Dined at home

Mild weather & blowing fresh from the WNW. Saw Brown about his continuancy in the George. He is to give us an address by Thursday Took the steam boat & went to Newcastle Could not get anything for the Hope Lunched with A Weyhtos & at 3 o'clock called in Westgate Street. I found Mrs Dixon just arrived from Brenbuch & Joys Cow Dined & stayed all night with them
Milder weather. Wind SW. WBS came up to Newcastle. We lunched in Westgate Street & afterward returned to Shields by steam. Dined at home. In the evening A Harry & I at the Duke

Fine weather. Wind SW. A dull morning, the glass down & evening appearance of rain Saw Brown who declined taking the George again excepting at a very great reduction of rent he offered £50 a year. Dined at home. The Saturdays nights whist club spent the evening with me. Heavy showers during the day & much thunder & lightening in the evening. A number of light ships arrived

A beautiful morning after a great deal of rain. Wind SE. Walked with A Henry to Tynemouth. Dined at home. Took another walk in the afternoon with A Harry down by Dr Drury's garden. In the evening at the Duke of York
A thick damp morning. Wind WNW Walk with J Tinley to Newcastle. WBS & Mary Carf went up in Dunn's coach Torrents of rain the whole day after our arrival. Dined & stayed all night at A Dixon

A beautiful morning. Wind SW. Embarked on board a steam boat at 10 o'clock and returned to Shields. Dined at home. After dinner walked with A Harry to Cullercoat Sands. About a dozen tents erected & a great many people there. Met W E Wrights & adjourned with him to Spencer's where we had some wine. At the Mulstrum in the evening.
A cold day. Wind in the morning NE & changed to SSE blowing fresh. Received a letter from William & answered it. Dined at home
A wet morning. Wind SW. Walked with A Harry to Tynemouth races which were very bad & few people there it being so wet a day. Dined with W C Wright on board the _____ a new purchase

A fine morning. Wind changed about during the day. Dined early, the Decghtow called & dined with us & in the afternoon Harry & I walked to the races, a great many people there being so beautiful a day. The rest of the party went to hear the choral society at the church. In the evening A H & I went to the Ball . Very few people there, Mr Craig behind very ill. He took offence at something & having a strong ...

... party consisting of the Joblary & he took them all away, which prevented the remainder of the company, being too few, having any dancing. Craig it appears took the party with much of the gentlemen to his own house & prevailing upon the musicians to accompany him. May these had a dance. But that would be expected from a fellow brought up behind a counter ! the filles ! place for him.

A beautiful spring morning. Wind West. Walked with Williams to Preston & looked at the different tenements & ordered what repairs were necessary afterwards we crofsid the conatrg & called upon Mr Flbceght, Whitley Park when this it began to rain& we got wet through before we reached home & dinner at ½ past 2 o'clock Mary Carp left us & returned to Newcastle with A Deighlow. In the evening at the Duke of York with A Harry & Mr Heweson

Another fine spring morning. Wind SSE. Went with Weller & called upon the Vicar Miss Ratcliff & Mr Matthews. Saw Brown of the George and offered him the house at £80 the nominal rent to be £100. Dined at the George Tavern. The whist club dinner a party of sextecan & spent a pleasant evening

A beautiful warm morning. Wind W by S. The painters began painting the house. Repairing the doors, windows. & Dined at home at 2 o'clock. Emma with us. WBS left us at ½ past 5 % o'clock by steam for Newcastle and thence to take the ship to London
A fine soft spring morning with showers. Wind blowing fresh at W by S. Dined at home. Took tea with W Allen & attended the whist club at Mr Richmonds in the evening
A beautiful morning Wind WNW. Went to church Rev Mark did duty & gave us an excellent sermon I Tenby & I walked to Tynemouth & I afterwards dined with him, Mr Mark with us

A fine morning blowing fresh from SW. A letter came for Captain Jameson of the London which I sent by one of the Hopes boys to the ship at Bewick oCrasters spout. Dined at home, H Harry came in & took wine with him & in the evening he Captain Webb & Peash Frantook of a cockle supper with us.
A very heavy fall of rain in light air at NNW. Dined at home. In the evening at the Duke of York
A very cold day. Wind SSE blowing hard. A sloop laden with grain got upon the rocks, crew saved by the life boat. A great many light ships arrived. Dined at home
A very wet morning & continued raining all day. Wind SW. Dined with R Pearch on board the Brondenick & spent a pleasant day

Fine weather blowing fresh at WNW. Received a letter from WBS of his arrival in London & also one from I Smith to say he will dine & stay all night with me on the 1st May. Wrote to WBS. Dined at home. Saw Mr & Mrs Ildegton, he very lame with the gout. Spent the evening at Allens, got home at ½ past 2 o'clock

x

A dull morning. Wind SW. Received a note from In Carr of Walkers, that he could not see me to dinner today a fixed upon & immediately me for next Tuesday. Got £5 from Chapmans. Paid Bulman cargo club £1.12. Entrance on policy 1830. Dined at home. At the Duke in the evening.

Another dull morning with rain. Wind SE. Walked with Captain Webb to Tynmouth & called upon Mr & Mrs Ilderton at the Star & Garter. Dined at house & attended the whist club in the evening at the A Fenwicks. Rained very heavy all the afternoon with the wind changed to N by W

Fine weather again & glafs risen considerably since yesterday evening about 1 ½ inch & up to fair. Wind NNW. Attended morning wives. Dined with I Tealeg, Mrs Cumliff & keifs of the These. Walked to Tynemouth in the afternoon; At the S Cellegator off several ships went to sea, bound foreign, the Broderweck, 3 Brothers, Dalsymple, Hannah, Equity les. Spent the evening at Tealegs A heavy rain at night.

A dull morning. Wind W by S. Walked to Teymouth; called at Libb's where I met Mrs Ildeston, he returned to Shields with bum. Invited by him to go & stay at Lnasoington with Captain Webb. Dined at home. Jebbs & Webb took wine with over at the Duke of York in the evening

A beautiful morning. Wind SW. Walked up to Sadlers at Lokiltsy Point and took lunch & he & I afterwards got onboard a steam boat & went up to Walker where we dined with I Carr & spent a very pleasant day. Returned to Shields in evening in a gig. Wind changed to SE
Another fine morning. Wind SE. Attended Kiefs onttes sah. Dined at home & in the afternoon on board the Anus with Mr Ascoerson onffstong. Took tea with the latter & had a walk in the evening with
A countenance of beautiful weather. Wind ESE. Took a walk to Tynemouth with Lt Harry. Dined at home. Onboard the John Dunn in the evening with I Wesglot & afterwards at the Duke of York.

Most beautiful weather. Wind ESE. Went by Steamer to Newcastle could get nothing for the Hope. Dined with D Dixon, a party Tom Smith, Mr Busqter; they all went to the theater to see Liston, I looked in but did not remain long, the house very full for his benefit. Got into a gig & returned to Shields
A beautiful day but rather cool. Wind NNE. Dined at home. Engaged to an evening party ay Mrs Heddells but sent an apology in consequence of Mrs Deghton's death

A cloudy morning much like rain. Wind WSW Turned out a most beautiful day. Went with H Harry by steam to Newcastle. Could not fix the Hope, but almost determined to talk 11 Gr Kent to Dublin. Returned home to dinner. Tour Seventh A Harry & Emma G: dined with me. Mark came in to wine. In the evening we went to whist club at Allens

A fine morning. Wind West. Tom Smith & I went to Church. Afterwards called at Mrs Marr's who would not let Emma go up to Newcastle to see Bell Smith. The King by Lodges paper a little better back still in a very precarious start. Dined at home. Pscous to which I Smith left. Walk to Tynemouth in the afternoon & took wine & tea with Libbs

Another fine morning. Wind about West. By Steam to Newcastle but did not find the Hope to load coal for Dublin as intended as they could not load her before they did of much works. Returned to Dinner on board the Choice in the afternoon. Drank tea with H Harry & In the evening at the Duke of York

A continuance of most beautiful weather with a West wind. Turned out at 6 o'clock & took a long walk round by Cullercoat Sands & before breakfast. And afterwards Webb, Mark & I took a walk along the hard sand where I made a sketch of Tynmouth Castle be. Returned home to dinner. In the evening at the Duke of York

Glorious weather. Wind very variable between SE & W. Went to Newcastle by steam. Gave up the Dublin charter & returned home to dinner. A Harry took a bottle of port with us & I gave him an order to fix the Hope for anchorage & Hull dealers at £4.7.6 At the Duke of York in the evening

Delightful weather. Wind East & SE. Walked beyond Marsden Rocks with Webb, Gosling RNW To see exfrenements laid for saving shipwrecked men, my means of a rope ladder & air jacket. Returned home to dinner. Webb & Gosling dinned with us. Afterwards walked to Tynemouth & spent the evening at Webb

A dull think morning with wind SE blowing fresh. Dined with I Finely, met char Nicholas & in the evening went to the whist club at I Newghts. A very stormy night, a gale of wind at ESE with torrents of rain. Gabe Stephenson a debt on Chapmans for £30 & got £5 for self. Gave G Stafs £1 on account of wages

All last night marsh dismal & stormy blowing a gale of wind at ESE with a deluge of rain & still continuous Did not go to church. Employed myself in writing to WBS & G Farell. Gave Stephenson a draft upon Chapmans exors at £14.11.7 ( £5 cook + £9.11.7 Balance of after) Dined with a Harry. Called on Webb in the evening who had gout a which prevents him going to Mr Aldertons At the Duke of York in evening. Weather inadesater
Finer weather. Wind East blowing fresh & heavy sea. Lower ladder off its put back left Shields
at ½ past 8 o'clock. Got the Alnwick coach at Newcastle at 10 o'clock and reached Alnwick at 3. Mr & Mrs Ilderstow there in the carriage & took me out to Leamington to dinner
A cold morning with showers of rain & sleet. Wind E by N. Dined at home. In the afternoon attended Mrs Deighton's funeral at Tynemouth
Still blowing fresh from the NE & cold. Robert & Tom I Ldestow & I started after breakfast to fish in the Alm, but had bad sport & river busy sheet & cold weather

Fairer and warmer weather. Robert Ilderstow & I had an early breakfast & rode over the river till below Hedghey, where we fished until it began to rain when we took shelter at a mill & then walked up to Rosea an estate of the Ildestonn's. Had tea & eggs & rode home in the evening, when we found Mrs Crosby & Mrs Strothard had arrived from Newcastle on a visit. Had better sport today, brought home a few good trout
Fine weather again. Wind about SW. After breakfast we went to fish in the Ala Had fair sport & got home to dinner. Spent a quiet evening
Another fine day. Wind much the same. Again went & fished in the Alm. Not such good sport. Returned to dinner found Mrs Forston of Alnwick there, who fed with us. Got a letter from WBS.

Got up in the morning at 5 o'clock & after having some bread & milk, started on horseback to fish in Breamish, starting from the Powburn & leaving off at Ingram, caught a dog trout but very small. Got home to dinner before 5 o'clock very tired

A beautiful morning. Wind somewhere from the W. After breakfast, accompanied Jane of the family in the carriage to Bottom Church. Mr Manestry did the service. Mrs I Winton not well. Dined at home. Wrote to A Harry to ask if he had fixed the Hope
A continuance of fine weather. Wind from the S & W. Engaged all the morning fishing in the Aln & had good sport. Returned home to dinner

A fine morning. Wind the same. Robert Ilderton & I rose early & rode over to the Till about 8 miles off where we spent the day in fishing & had most excellent sport. I tickled ½ day of lays trout. Returned to Lemmington to supper
Another fine day. Amused ourselves this morning in shooting rooks. Rode over to Broom Park to call upon Mr Burrell, not at home.
Another fine day but rather cooler wind SE. Again binoculars in shooting rooks. Bob Alderton & I rode over to Broom Park to dinner. Met there Tom JW & Mrs Dixon. Spent a very pleasant day
A beautiful day but rather cool. Wind E. At church in the morning. Walked to Tynemouth in the afternoon. Dined at home
A fine day. Rather cool. Wind SE. shooting rooks. In the moor. After lunch went out to fish & got down at ½ paid 8.6- killed two dozen good trout

Fine weather and warmer. The whole of the moors answered ours lpes in shooting rooks, killed about 70. Young Clensed Fiawick came from school to stop until Monday chat. Ilterton's birthday, made a jug of punch in the evening to drink his health
A most beautiful day. Went with the carriage in the morning to church. Passed the afternoon in walking about the garden. In the evening a thick fog set in & the wind from the SE.
The fog still continues with a little rain.
A continuance of cold weather with each. Winds & clouds heavy rains. But fishing two or three times, but nothing very successful
ditto
ditto
ditto

A fine morning, but still rather cool & wind about SE. Left Lemmington after having spent a very pleasant time. Rode Bob Ildercoade home onto Alnwick & got them onto place, left at 1/s past 10 o'clock. The day got cloudy & cold & before we left Morpeth it began to rain. ...

... & continued showering all day. Got upon Dunns coach at 4 o'clock & arrived at home a little after 5 o'clock to dinner. Received a letter from lorss. That my friend A Harry & A Nicholson the latter the first time since his parried extect es captain his ship the Tenacity having foundered in the North Sea & he & the crew taken aboard on gallcot that Cuekerly hove in sights before dark. Spent the evening together with Mr Com Hewesion at the Duke of York

Finer weather. Wind about West. Icy cold having flown to the locns suffering some pain. Got Robert to sub the park with opadildoc, took a scidlily & did not go to church. Wrote a long letter to ABP Emma G: came over to see us. Dined at home & in the afternoon A Harry & I walked up to North Sheilds to take wine
A dull morning. Wind NSW Blowing hard. Sent my letter off to WBS. Gave a draft on estate then 4 on after for £50 for ABS. Crew also from £10.10s + £16.3.8 = 27.3.8 for av wages ...

... Hope & Liberal club. A Harry, A Nicholson & Richardson NP took 1 o'clock dinner with me & we afterwards crossed the water to South Shields Races, but it came on such a stormy afternoon we could not do the sport

A fine morning. Wind blowing fresh at SW. A Harry, Nicholson took a walk around Tynmouth & at 2 o'clock dined with I Richardson MP at 4 o'clock. We crossed the water to attend the races which were all won easy by chamber horses. Got home at 10 o'clock

A most beautiful day, particularly the afternoon. Wind west, Took a walk with Captain Webb to Tynemouth. Met Smiths, Hannah, I Weston. Webb took her & the Blenkensops on board the Merserard Tatter, laying too off the Castle & gave them a few hours sail to the Sunderland. Dined at home & the afternoon being so fine tempted H Harry, for the sake of the walk to go to the tents on the sands but there was no racing. One match

A dull morning with rain. Wind SSE About 11o'clock the weather cleared up, Harry, Nicholson & I walked with I Richardson in his cable up to Mr Sadlers at the Point & then to Jarrow Slake where we had two hours fishing, but very poor sport, we afterwards landed & dined with Sadler & spent a very pleasant day. It turned out a rainy evening & we had a wet & unpleasant walk home

A stormy morning. Wind N by W. Accepted Baleracus bill at 5 mos for the archangel prrorraccon for £12.13.8 down 22nd but from the great fall of rain last night a heavy fresh in the season, take ch with the wind drove two sloops upon the headland & a brig over the points of the sand where the rode very heavy for 2 or 3 hours, but the life boat pulling some hands on board the got a offering upon his cable & thus succeeded in taking her to sea. Turned out a fine afternoon. Walked in the evening to Tynemouth to near the band of the 80th Regiment
A beautiful morning Wind SE. Took a walk to Tynemouth With A Nicholson. Called upon Rve Clenton at the Mathew's Dined at home. In the evening at the Duke

Another fine day Wind SE, Received a letter from ABS Went over the water to see I Salmon Returned to church. Dined at home & took wine with A Harry & went to Tynemouth in the evening to hear the band. A great many people there at night with Mr Jarvis Wrote to ABS

A dull morning, cloudy & appearance of rain. Wind NW Which we had during the morning, but it cleared up & after dinner we had fine weather. Took a walk to Tynemouth. Drank tea at home & in the evening at the Duke
A fine day but still cold & wind SSE. Dined at home & took wine & with W C. Wright & H French at the Commercial
A wet morning. Wind N by W Changed to NNE. At the billiard room all the morning . Dined at home. Spent an hour or two with Mark in the afternoon & the evening with Mr Simpson at the bank
A dull hazy morning Came fresh at NNS. Walked to Tynemouth Dined at home. Suppered with A Harry
A dull unpleasant morning Blowing fresh from the north with rain Which continued in torrents & without ceasing the whole day & a gale of wind. Dined at home & in the evening at the Duke of York

A stormy morning blowing a gale at about N by E It has never ceased raining since yesterday morning. Still coming down in torrents. I fear it will do great harm to the country. Turned out fair about the middle of the day, but still very cold & stormy Dined at home. At the Duke of York in the evening

Fair weather after a great deal of rain in the night but still blowing hard at NE & cold Received a letter & notes from ABS. Took a walk around by Cullercoat Fields & Tynemouth. Found Mrs Dixon at the house on my return. Dined at home & in the evening again walked to Tynemouth. Finished at the Duke of York

Another wet morning Wind West. Walked to Tynemouth after breakfast & saw the soldiers parading. Returned by the fields. Dined at home. Wrote to Fanny Smith that Emma would meet his at Morpeth on Thursday next. Paid monthly money for the Hope to do which I drew on Chapmans for £20. Turned out a wet evening & at bed time it was a deluge

Finer weather but still showering. Wind NW. Paid Ned's mother yesterday a quarter wages £1.13.9 & lent Mary Carfs £2. Dined at home. Wrote to WBS & sent him the last search account. Joined a party at Roddames & spent the evening

A fine morning but still cloudy with the appearance of showers wind NNW. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. Went to church in the afternoon. Drank tea with A Harry, again walked to Tynemouth to hear the band. A great many people there. Returned & had a glass of whisky toddy with A Harry
A cloudy morning with a cold NE wind. Went over to South Shields to see Salmon. He was not at home. Dined at home & afterwards A harry Ltd French & I went up to the Point & took wine with Sadler

A dull morning wind NE with showers. H Harry, French & I went up to Newcastle in a steam boat. Walked out to the race course. Very little company there. The running very good. Dined at the Stand & got to Shields again in a gig by the country road at 9 o'clock
A fine day but exceptionally cold. Wind from SSE. Dined at home
A fine morning but still cold. With a NE wind. Walked round by the high end of Shields to Dr Drings garden. Dined at home. At the Pig & Whistle & in the evening at Tynemouth. Suppered with A Harry

Rather a dull morning with a continuance of SE wind. & cool. Tool Emma G up with me in Dunn's coach to Newcastle where we met Tom Smith who drove he home with him to Royston for the whole day. Went in the afternoon to the races. A good deal of company, the Gold Cup being to be seen for; which was won by Lord Elcho's Gondolence. Dined in the Grand Stand. Got home at 11 o'clock
A fine morning. Wind east blowing fresh. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. H Harry came in after dinner & took wine with me & he & H French spent the evening supplied with beer with Mr Jervis

A rainy morning and blowing fresh at SE with a heavy sea upon the bar. Took a short walk. Dined at home. A French gave me a bottle of wine at the George. An awfully heavy thunder storm with a deluge of rain which overflowed the streets in two or three minutes & changed the wind to NW
A fine morning but the wind again from the SE. Took Jehy sec & did not go to church. Dined at home. A French came & took wine with me. In the [afternoon] walked to Tynemouth, rather showery

A dull cloudy morning with appearance of rain. Wind SE. Received an account of the poor vicar's death at ¼ past 8 o'clock on Saturday morning to the inexpressible sorrow of the a alecow. All the ships be hoisted their colours half mast high. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined at home. In the afternoon a heavy thunder storm with showers at intervals. Went to see A Harry in the evening who has got a light attack of gout.
A cloudy morning & like more rain again blowing fresh at WNW. Received a letter from B B Gallbraith & answered it. Dined at home. Walked to Tynemouth in the evening

A very fine morning something like summer weather at last. Wind WNW afterwards the heat brought is round to SE. Walked out to Whitley Park & called upon I Wright & returned by Cullercoats to dinner.Webb came in & took part of a bottle of port with me. Walked to Tynemouth in the evening. King William the 4th proclaimed at Newcastle today & the guns fired at Tynemouth castle
A fine morning. Wind SE blowing fresh. At the heavy roam. Called to see A Harry who was much better. Dined at home. Partook of a bottle of port at ward with Charlton Howard
A very cold day with a little rain. Wind NNE. Dined on board the Hope. Had a very pleasant party. J Tinley, H Harry & Mr Marks. Received a letter from William

After a night of heavy rain the weather cleared up a little. Wind SE & thick. Received a letter from Ryan L Parkinson, Sackville Street, Dublin stating that nothing had been done with the Fitznanances affairs. At 12 o'clock this solders with the band marched out the garrison & afterwards with the peaceful inhabited in procession & winner racecourse of people marched round the town & proclaimed king William 4th. In the afternoon a party of us dined at the George Tavern & spent a very pleasant day

A beautiful morning. Wind SE. Walked to Tynemouth. Much to my surprise met with Mrs Lumley and Mrs Bcagdon who had arrived by sea. The long gifore. Dined at home & in the afternoon Webb Hopkins the boy & I went in a boat to fish but had no sport, weather unpleasant & thick.

A dull morning. Wind ESE Did not go to church. Walked to Tynemouth. Attended afternoon services A Mr Hicks preached. Dined with I Tealey & in the evening again walked to Tynemouth, an immense number of people there

A most beautiful morning. Wind SE. Had a pleasant walk by the shore to Tynemouth, Cullercoat Sands & dined at home. Mark & Webb came & took wine with me. Walked to Tynemouth again in the evening & suppered at Marks

A dull calm morning. Wind SW. Went by coach to Newcastle. Received £4.9.2 balance of premium out of Hope club. Saw the exhibition of paintings which was very good. Walked with D Dixon out to Beaton. Dined & stayed all night

A stormy heavy thunder storm this morning. A deluge of rain. Wind SW & afterwards NW. Set off after breakfast & walked down to Shields between storms. After my arrival it commenced again & continued the remainder of the day, heavy thunder & rain. Dined at I Tealeys

A fine clear morning blowing fresh from W by N. Dined at home. Wrote to ABS & sent him his inventory of fumition & by Mr Gosling who sets off for London in the morning. In the evening walked with H Harry to Tynemouth & called in at the Duke of York on our way home
A fine morning. Rather cloudy & not walike showers. Wind E. Walked up to the point & dined with Sadlar, spent a pleasant day & got home late in the evening.
A beautiful morning. Wind WNW. Did not go to church. Walked to Tynemouth. Dined with Allen. Turned out a very rainy afternoon. At the Mr Estream in the evening

A fine morning after a heavy fall of rain during the night. Wind NW. Captain Webb & I intended going out fishing but the clouds looked so threatening we thought it prudent to stay on shore. Went with the Teinleys to L Midney at Biddick, dined & walked home in the evening
